````text
My read

The video’s method is:

Use Hermes Agent + Apify/Google Maps scraping to find local businesses without websites.

Put leads into Google Sheets.

Use Google Antigravity to generate demo websites for each lead.

Host demo pages on GitHub Pages.

Pitch: “I already made this for you; we can build the real version.”

I checked the linked YouTube page; the video is positioned around “Google Antigravity + Hermes Agent = 1000+ Leads/Day.” The underlying tools are real: Google describes Antigravity as an agentic development platform where agents can plan, execute, and verify work across editor, terminal, and browser; Hermes is an open-source agent with Telegram/Slack/WhatsApp/email support and scheduled automation; Apify openly markets Google Maps scraping for lead generation.
YouTube

Google Developers Blog

Hermes Agent

Apify

Strategic verdict for MenuList

Use the pattern, not the product framing.

The good part is artifact-first outbound. Instead of sending a generic cold pitch, you show the business something specific and pre-filled. That is much stronger than “Hi, we help restaurants improve online presence.”

The bad part is positioning it as website development. That pulls MenuList into a commodity agency category. For MenuList, the artifact should not be a “demo website.” It should be a claimable public business truth page.

Better framing:

“Your public menu, hours, and business info are fragmented or missing. We created a preview of your MenuList page. Claim it, correct it, and make it the canonical source customers can trust.”

That supports MenuList’s infrastructure thesis. A website demo does not.

What is useful from the video

The lead-gen logic is directionally correct:

Businesses with no website, no public menu, weak hours data, missing phone number, stale photos, poor review response, or inconsistent public info are high-intent targets for MenuList.

The valuable insight is not “AI can build websites.” The valuable insight is:

AI can cheaply generate a personalized evidence artifact that reveals the business’s public-info problem.

For MenuList, that artifact should be one of these:

Unclaimed MenuList profile preview

Public-info health audit

Menu/hours freshness report

Customer-facing listing preview

“What customers currently see about you” page

The workflow becomes:

discover weak public truth → generate preview → ask owner to claim → verify → keep fresh → distribute.

That is much more aligned with MenuList’s long-term moat.

The big risks if copied literally
1. Google data dependency risk

The video’s system leans heavily on scraping Google Maps. That is not a stable foundation for infrastructure. Google Maps Platform terms explicitly prohibit exporting, extracting, scraping, storing, resharing, or rehosting Google Maps content outside the services, including copying and saving business names, addresses, places information, or user reviews.
Google Cloud

Even Google Business Profile APIs are not a clean workaround for lead generation. Google’s Business Profile API policy says the APIs may only be used for listings you own or are authorized to manage, and the GoogleLocations endpoint is only for merchants that already have a business relationship with your company; using it for lead generation is against policy.
Google for Developers

So: scraping can be a short-term seed, but it cannot become MenuList’s source of truth.

2. Rehosting photos/reviews is risky

The video suggests using Google Maps photos or profile content in generated websites. That is dangerous. Google says user-contributed Maps content may appear on third-party sites through Google embeddable widgets or Maps Platform, not because anyone can freely scrape and rehost it.
Google Help

For MenuList previews, do not rehost Google photos, reviews, or menus unless you have rights. Use:

no image,

generic placeholder,

AI-generated non-representational image with clear labeling,

owner-uploaded assets after claim,

embedded Google map where permitted.

For restaurants, synthetic food/ambience photos are especially dangerous because they can misrepresent the actual business.

3. Cold call/SMS/WhatsApp compliance risk

In India, telecom outreach is not a free-for-all. TRAI’s TCCCPR framework exists to protect customers from unsolicited commercial communication, and TRAI’s 2025 amendments tightened spam complaint handling and enforcement.
TRAI

Press Information Bureau

For MenuList, avoid high-volume automated calling or WhatsApp blasting. Use controlled, consent-aware outreach. Early-stage founder-led or human-assisted outreach is acceptable; mass automated outreach is not where I would start.

4. GitHub Pages is fine for demos, not production business hosting

GitHub Pages can publish static HTML/CSS/JS from a repository, so the video’s demo hosting method works technically. But GitHub also says Pages is not intended as a free web-hosting service for running an online business, e-commerce site, or SaaS.
GitHub Docs

GitHub Docs

For MenuList, use your own domain and infrastructure. Do not scatter thousands of public demo pages across GitHub. It looks cheap, creates duplicate/noisy pages, and does not build MenuList authority.

The MenuList-native version

I would redesign the workflow like this:

Step 1: Lead discovery

Target restaurants/cafes where customer-facing truth is visibly broken.

Score leads by:

no website,

no menu link,

menu only exists as old photos,

hours missing or suspicious,

Google profile exists but looks unmanaged,

active review volume but weak owner response,

high footfall category,

public phone/WhatsApp available,

no canonical customer-facing page.

Do not call these “verified businesses.” Call them candidate leads until the owner confirms.

Step 2: Generate a MenuList preview, not a website

Create a private or noindex preview page:

menulist.com/preview/duas-cafe-bangalore

The page should say:

“Unclaimed preview”

“Information may be incomplete”

“Claim this page to correct menu, hours, photos, and public details”

“Last checked: date”

“Sources: public web / owner submission / customer report” where applicable

This protects trust. It also makes the claim action natural.

Step 3: Outreach with a truth-gap angle

Bad pitch:

“We built a website for you.”

Better pitch:

“Your menu and hours are hard for customers to verify online. We created a pre-filled MenuList page for your business. You can claim it and correct everything in two minutes.”

This is not a service pitch. It is an authority-transfer motion.

Step 4: Owner claim flow

The conversion event should be claim + correction, not “book a web design call.”

Minimum claim flow:

Owner enters phone/email.

OTP or callback verification.

Owner confirms business name, menu, hours, address, phone, links.

Page becomes “verified by owner.”

Owner gets a canonical MenuList URL.

This turns outbound into first-party data acquisition.

Step 5: Compound the data

Every claimed page should produce durable infrastructure assets:

verified menu,

verified hours,

verified phone,

verified location,

update history,

freshness timestamp,

owner account,

customer-facing canonical URL,

structured data,

discovery surface eligibility.

That is the moat. Not the scraper. Not the AI website.

What I would not do

I would not mass-generate 1,000 public demo websites.

I would not use Google reviews/photos directly in pages.

I would not position MenuList as a website builder.

I would not let AI invent menu items, prices, photos, ambience, or claims.

I would not fully automate outreach until the message, claim rate, data accuracy, and complaint rate are proven manually.

I would not store scraped third-party data as if it were MenuList truth. Scraped data should be temporary lead intelligence, not canonical data.

What I would test now

Run a tight experiment:

Market: one city, one vertical, e.g. Bangalore cafes or casual restaurants.
Sample: 100 manually reviewed leads.
Artifact: noindex MenuList preview page + public-info audit.
Outreach: founder-led WhatsApp/call/email where compliant and appropriate.
CTA: “Claim and correct your MenuList page.”
Success metric: claimed profiles, not replies.

Track:

lead validity rate,

contactability rate,

positive response rate,

claim rate,

correction rate,

menu/hour update completion,

owner objection themes,

complaint/negative response rate.

A strong signal is not “they liked the demo.” A strong signal is:

They correct the page because they believe MenuList is worth being accurate on.

Bottom line

The video is useful as a tactical inspiration, but it is a freelancer/agency funnel. For MenuList, the same machinery should be converted into a business truth acquisition loop.

The correct move is:

AI-personalized lead artifact → owner claim → verified business truth → canonical public page → freshness loop.
````

````text
Yes. I would use the video’s idea only as a primitive. For MenuList, there are better ways.

The video optimizes for:

“Find businesses without websites → generate demo websites → pitch website service.”

MenuList should optimize for:

“Find businesses with broken public truth → generate a claimable truth page → get the owner to verify and maintain it.”

That is a fundamentally stronger loop.

The better idea: build a “Truth Gap Engine”

MenuList lead generation should not start with “who needs a website?”

It should start with:

“Where is customer-facing business truth broken, missing, stale, fragmented, or untrusted?”

That gives you a much better lead list because the pain maps directly to MenuList.

A restaurant may not care about a website. But it will care if customers cannot reliably see:

current menu,

opening hours,

location,

phone/WhatsApp,

reservation info,

price range,

active offers,

photos,

delivery/pickup info,

festival/holiday timing,

whether they are open today.

That is MenuList territory.

Why this is better than AI demo websites

The AI website method has weak strategic leverage.

It says:

“I can build you a nice-looking page.”

That puts you in the same bucket as freelancers, agencies, Wix, Shopify, Squarespace, Canva, and AI website builders.

The MenuList method should say:

“Your public business information is not reliable enough. We created a pre-filled public truth page. Claim it, correct it, and make it the source customers can trust.”

That is infrastructure positioning.

The conversion object changes from buy a website to claim your business truth.

That is much more powerful.

The system I would build
1. Create a “Public Truth Score” for every business

For each restaurant/cafe, calculate a score based on how broken their public information is.

Example signals:

Signal	Meaning
No website	No canonical public page
No menu link	Customers cannot inspect offering
Menu only exists as photos	Hard to search, update, or trust
Old menu photos	Prices/items may be stale
Hours missing or inconsistent	Customer trust issue
Multiple conflicting listings	Fragmented public truth
Instagram-only presence	Poor structured discovery
High reviews but weak info	High demand, bad conversion
Popular venue with no clean menu	High-value target
Phone present but no menu	Good outreach target
Business replies to reviews	Owner is active and reachable

Then prioritize leads by:

Public Truth Gap × Customer Demand × Owner Reachability

That is better than simply “has no website.”

A business with no website but low demand is not valuable. A business with messy menu/hours and high customer demand is valuable.

2. Generate a MenuList preview page, not a website

For every qualified lead, create:

menulist.com/preview/business-name-city

The page should be clearly labeled:

“Unclaimed preview. Information may be incomplete. Claim this page to correct menu, hours, and public details.”

The preview should include only safe, factual, non-invented information:

business name,

category,

area,

phone if publicly available,

map link/embed,

possible hours if confidently available,

“menu not verified” state,

“claim to add current menu” CTA.

Do not let AI invent menu items, prices, photos, reviews, ambience, or business claims.

The goal is not to impress with design. The goal is to expose the gap.

3. Generate a private “Truth Gap Report”

This is the real outbound artifact.

Example:

Public Info Audit for Cafe X

Customers searching for you currently face these issues:

No verified menu available.

Hours are unclear or missing.

Photos do not show current pricing.

No canonical page to share on WhatsApp/Instagram.

MenuList preview is ready to claim.

This is more compelling than “we made a website.”

It frames the problem as lost customer trust, not lack of design.

4. Outreach with a claim CTA

The pitch should be simple.

Not:

“We build websites.”

Instead:

“We created a pre-filled MenuList page for your restaurant because your menu/hours are not easy for customers to verify online. You can claim it and correct everything here: [link].”

The ask is small.

Not “book a call.”

Not “pay us.”

Not “hire us.”

Just:

“Claim and correct your page.”

That is the right first conversion.

5. Turn claimed pages into compounding data

Once the owner claims the page, MenuList gets:

verified menu,

verified hours,

verified phone,

verified location,

owner account,

freshness timestamp,

update history,

public canonical URL.

That is the asset.

Every claim improves MenuList’s data graph. Every update improves trust. Every verified page makes the next business more likely to join.

That is a compounding loop. AI website demos do not compound.

The strongest lead-generation plays for MenuList

I would rank them like this.

1. Customer-demand-led acquisition

This is the best one long term.

Instead of only outbounding to businesses, create pages where customers can signal demand.

Example:

A user searches:

“ABC Cafe menu”

If MenuList does not have verified data, show:

“Menu not verified yet. Request updated menu from ABC Cafe.”

The user clicks Request Menu.

Then MenuList contacts the business:

“Customers are trying to see your menu on MenuList. Claim your page and add the latest menu.”

This is much stronger than cold outreach because now you are not saying:

“We think you need this.”

You are saying:

“Customers are already asking for this.”

That creates authority.

This can become a core acquisition loop:

customer search → missing info → request → owner notified → claim → verified page → better customer experience → more search traffic

That is the highest-leverage loop.

2. Public Truth Gap Audits

Run automated audits for specific local categories.

Start narrow:

Bangalore cafes,

Delhi cloud kitchens,

Mumbai dessert shops,

Pune restaurants,

Gurgaon salons later if you expand beyond food.

For each business, score:

menu availability,

hours reliability,

phone visibility,

location clarity,

public page quality,

photo/menu freshness,

online ordering/reservation clarity.

Then outreach only to businesses above a threshold.

Do not contact every scraped lead. Contact only businesses with visible truth gaps and reasonable demand.

This keeps quality high and protects the brand.

3. Claimable unverified profiles

Seed MenuList with unclaimed profiles, but carefully.

Each unclaimed page should be conservative:

no fake menu,

no fake photos,

no invented descriptions,

no misleading “verified” label,

no scraped reviews,

no claim of accuracy.

Use states:

Unclaimed

Owner Verified

Recently Updated

Needs Update

Customer Reported Issue

This creates a public trust hierarchy.

The business owner’s job becomes obvious:

“Claim this so customers see the correct version.”

This is how MenuList starts becoming the canonical layer.

4. QR acquisition

This is underrated.

For restaurants, a QR code is a natural bridge between offline and online truth.

After a business claims its page, give them:

“MenuList verified menu QR”

They can place it:

at tables,

on takeaway packaging,

on counters,

on Instagram bio,

on WhatsApp auto-reply,

on Google Business Profile website/menu field,

on flyers,

on receipts.

The QR page should be fast, clean, and owner-controlled.

This creates repeated customer exposure. Over time, customers learn:

“MenuList is where the current menu lives.”

That is stronger than SEO alone.

5. “Menu freshness” reminders

Once the owner claims the page, MenuList should not be passive.

Build a freshness loop:

“Your menu was last updated 47 days ago. Confirm it is still accurate.”

Owner clicks:

“Still accurate”

“Update menu”

“Temporarily unavailable”

“Holiday hours”

This gives MenuList a freshness advantage over static websites, Google photos, Instagram highlights, and old PDFs.

Freshness is one of your possible moats.

A normal website says:

“Here is our menu.”

MenuList should say:

“This menu was confirmed by the owner 3 days ago.”

That is much more authoritative.

6. Owner comparison pages

Create simple internal lead artifacts like:

“How your restaurant appears across customer surfaces”

For example:

Surface	Menu	Hours	Phone	Photos	Verified?
Google	Partial	Maybe	Yes	Old	No
Instagram	Hard to find	No	Maybe	Yes	No
Zomato/Swiggy	Delivery menu only	No	No	Yes	Platform-specific
Website	Missing	Missing	Missing	Missing	No
MenuList	Ready to claim	Ready to verify	Ready to verify	Owner-controlled	Pending

This makes the fragmentation visible.

The owner sees why a canonical page matters.

7. Local cluster strategy

Do not acquire random businesses across India.

Pick dense clusters.

Example:

Indiranagar cafes,

Koramangala restaurants,

Bandra dessert shops,

CP cafes,

HSR cloud kitchens.

Why?

Because local density creates social proof.

A restaurant is more likely to claim MenuList when nearby restaurants are already on it.

Your pitch becomes:

“We are building the verified menu layer for cafes in Koramangala. Your page is ready to claim.”

That is stronger than:

“We help restaurants online.”

The strategic unit should be local category dominance, not scattered leads.

8. “Missing menu” SEO pages

This needs careful execution, but it can become powerful.

For businesses where MenuList does not yet have verified data, the page can rank for:

“[Restaurant name] menu”
“[Restaurant name] hours”
“[Restaurant name] contact”
“[Restaurant name] location”

But the page must not fake completeness.

It should say:

“This menu has not been verified by the owner yet.”

Then let customers request the menu.

This creates customer-side pressure.

Again, the loop:

search traffic → missing truth → customer request → business claim → verified data → better page → more traffic

That is a real infrastructure loop.

9. Founder-led “concierge claiming”

For early markets, do not over-automate.

The highest-quality early motion may be:

Identify 100 high-value restaurants.

Create clean preview pages.

Call/WhatsApp owners manually.

Offer to set up their MenuList page in 5 minutes.

Ask for menu/hours confirmation.

Send final public link and QR.

This is not scalable forever, but it teaches you:

what owners understand,

what they ignore,

what they fear,

what they will update,

what they will pay for later,

what language converts.

Automating before learning the owner psychology is dangerous.

The best version of the AI workflow

Use AI for these things:

lead enrichment,

public truth gap detection,

business categorization,

duplicate detection,

page draft generation,

audit generation,

outreach personalization,

menu extraction from owner-uploaded images,

hours normalization,

data quality checks,

follow-up scheduling.

Do not use AI to:

invent menu items,

generate fake restaurant photos,

scrape and reuse protected content,

mass-send low-quality outreach,

create thousands of public pages without QA,

make MenuList look like an agency.

AI should support the truth layer. It should not become the product’s identity.

The better workflow

Here is the version I would actually build:

Phase 1: Lead discovery

Find restaurants/cafes with high public-info gaps.

Input sources:

search results,

maps listings,

Instagram bios,

food directories,

customer searches,

local directories,

manual field research,

owner submissions.

Output:

business name,

category,

area,

contact,

public links,

suspected gaps,

confidence score,

priority score.

Phase 2: Truth Gap Score

Each business gets a score from 0–100.

Example:

Business: ABC Cafe, Koramangala
Truth Gap Score: 82/100

Issues:
- No verified menu
- No website
- Menu exists only as old photos
- Hours unclear
- Phone available
- High review volume
- Good outreach candidate

Only contact businesses above, say, 65.

Phase 3: Preview generation

Create:

menulist.com/preview/abc-cafe-koramangala

The preview includes:

“Unclaimed” label,

basic business info,

missing menu state,

missing hours state,

claim CTA,

“customers can request menu” CTA.

Phase 4: Outreach

Message:

Hi, we created a pre-filled MenuList page for ABC Cafe because customers do not have a reliable place to see your current menu and hours.

You can claim and correct it here: [link]

Once claimed, you get a clean public menu link and QR code for customers.

This is direct, useful, and not desperate.

Phase 5: Claim

Owner verifies:

phone,

menu,

hours,

address,

WhatsApp,

social links,

photos if they want.

Then page changes from:

Unclaimed

to:

Verified by owner · Updated today

That is the trust asset.

Phase 6: Distribution

After claim, give the owner:

public MenuList link,

QR code,

Instagram bio link,

WhatsApp share message,

Google Business Profile menu link instructions,

printable table QR,

freshness reminder.

Now MenuList is embedded into customer behavior.

My strongest recommendation

Do not build a “lead gen automation system.”

Build a business truth acquisition system.

The difference matters.

A lead-gen system gives you prospects.

A truth acquisition system gives you proprietary, verified, compounding data.

For MenuList, the correct loop is:

Detect truth gap
→ Create claimable preview
→ Show owner what is broken
→ Owner claims page
→ Owner verifies menu/hours/info
→ MenuList becomes customer-facing source
→ Customers use/share/request updates
→ Freshness improves
→ More businesses claim

That is better than the YouTube method because it directly strengthens MenuList’s long-term authority.
````

### Message 9 - Assistant
- Message ID: ca4ea33d-2744-4b58-b56b-124503ebb0ba

````text
Yes. Build this in-house. Do not stitch together Google Sheets + agents + GitHub pages. That is fine for a YouTube demo, but not for MenuList.

For MenuList, this should be an internal Business Truth Acquisition System: a pipeline that finds businesses with broken customer-facing public truth, creates a controlled claimable preview, gets the owner to verify, and turns that into canonical MenuList data.

Below is the spec I would build.

Business Truth Acquisition System
1. Core thesis

The system should not generate “leads” in the normal SaaS sense.

It should generate claimable truth records.

A normal lead is:

“This restaurant might buy something.”

A MenuList acquisition target is:

“This restaurant has fragmented, stale, or missing public information, and MenuList can become the canonical customer-facing record.”

That distinction matters because the system’s output is not a sales call list. The output is a growing, increasingly verified business-truth graph.

2. Product boundary

This system is internal infrastructure. It should not turn MenuList into CRM, POS, ordering, payroll, loyalty, or website-building software.

The external product surface remains:

verified menu, hours, public business info, reputation/discovery context, and freshness.

The acquisition system exists only to acquire, verify, and maintain that customer-facing truth.

3. Recommended stack

Use:

Next.js for public pages, owner claim flow, and internal ops dashboard.

Firebase App Hosting for deploying the Next.js app.

Firestore as the operational database.

Cloud Functions for Firebase for ingestion, scoring, jobs, webhooks, and scheduled maintenance.

Cloud Tasks for rate-limited asynchronous processing.

Firebase Auth for owners and internal operators.

Firebase custom claims for role-based access.

Firebase App Check for abuse reduction.

Cloud Storage for Firebase for owner-uploaded menus, photos, PDFs, and QR assets.

Apify as the external crawling/extraction runner.

Optional later: dedicated search/index layer, analytics warehouse, and ML/LLM extraction service.

Firebase App Hosting is now the better Firebase route for dynamic Next.js apps because it has built-in support for Next.js, GitHub integration, Cloud Build, Cloud Run, Cloud CDN, and Secret Manager integration. Next.js App Router is suitable here because it supports file-system routing, Server Components, Server Functions, and route handlers. Use route handlers for external webhooks and API endpoints because Next.js route files support standard HTTP methods like GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS.
Firebase
+2
Next.js
+2

Use Cloud Functions and Cloud Tasks for heavy work, not Next.js request handlers. Firebase scheduled functions use onSchedule with Cloud Scheduler, and Firebase task queue functions use Cloud Tasks for asynchronous, resource-intensive, or bandwidth-limited jobs with rate limits and retries.
Firebase
+1

Apify should be treated as a pluggable ingestion layer. Its official JavaScript client can interact with Actors, runs, datasets, key-value stores, and request queues, and Apify webhooks can trigger on Actor run states such as ACTOR.RUN.SUCCEEDED and ACTOR.RUN.FAILED.
Apify
+1

4. Non-negotiable architecture principle

Separate these three layers:

1. Observation layer
   Raw, untrusted, third-party or public-source observations.

2. Candidate layer
   Normalized business candidates with confidence scores and gaps.

3. Canonical truth layer
   Owner-verified or otherwise permitted MenuList business truth.

Do not let scraped data directly become MenuList truth.

Every third-party input should be stored as:

"Observed from source X at time Y with confidence Z."

Not:

"This is true."

This is the main difference between a defensible infrastructure product and a scraper directory.

5. Data acquisition policy

You can use Apify, but the source policy must be strict.

Google Maps data is high-risk as a canonical input. Google Maps Platform terms prohibit exporting, extracting, scraping, pre-fetching, indexing, storing, resharing, or rehosting Google Maps content outside the services, including copying business names, addresses, places information, and user reviews. Google Business Profile APIs are also limited to listings you own or are authorized to manage, and Google specifically says the GoogleLocations endpoint may only be used for merchants that already have a business relationship with your company; use for lead generation or other analysis is against policy.
Google Cloud
+1

So the safe internal rule should be:

Apify may help discover candidate businesses.
Apify may crawl permitted first-party/public web sources.
Apify may enrich internal lead intelligence.
Apify may not create canonical MenuList truth from restricted third-party content.
MenuList truth must come from owner verification, owner uploads, customer requests, permitted sources, or manual review.

Do not rehost Google photos, reviews, menus, or Maps-derived descriptions. Do not use Google Business Profile APIs for cold lead generation.

6. System modules

The system should have 10 modules.

1. Campaign Manager
2. Source Ingestion
3. Raw Observation Store
4. Entity Resolution / Deduplication
5. Truth Gap Scoring
6. Preview Generator
7. QA Review Console
8. Outreach / Claim Initiation
9. Owner Claim + Verification
10. Freshness Engine

These should be modular from day one. The mistake would be building one giant automation script.

7. End-to-end flow
Flow A: Discovery to preview
Create campaign
→ Run source collectors
→ Store raw observations
→ Normalize business candidates
→ Deduplicate candidates
→ Score truth gap
→ Generate preview page
→ Generate audit report
→ Send to QA queue
→ Approve for outreach
Flow B: Outreach to claim
Approved candidate
→ Create claim token
→ Send/manual outreach
→ Owner opens preview
→ Owner verifies phone/email
→ Owner confirms business
→ Owner edits menu/hours/info
→ Operator or automated validation checks
→ Page becomes owner-verified
Flow C: Freshness loop
Verified business
→ Freshness timer starts
→ Owner receives confirmation prompt
→ Owner confirms or updates
→ Freshness timestamp updates
→ Public page shows "Updated / confirmed recently"

The compounding asset is not the preview page. It is the verified update history.

8. Core state machine

Every business candidate should move through explicit states.

TypeScript
type CandidateStatus =
  | "raw_observed"
  | "normalized"
  | "duplicate_suspected"
  | "scored"
  | "preview_ready"
  | "qa_pending"
  | "qa_rejected"
  | "approved_for_outreach"
  | "outreach_started"
  | "claim_started"
  | "owner_verified"
  | "published"
  | "stale"
  | "archived";

The important states:

State	Meaning
raw_observed	Imported from source, not trusted
normalized	Basic business entity created
scored	Truth gap score calculated
preview_ready	Noindex preview generated
qa_pending	Human/operator review needed
approved_for_outreach	Safe to contact
claim_started	Owner clicked or responded
owner_verified	Owner identity confirmed
published	Public MenuList page live
stale	Freshness threshold exceeded
archived	Bad lead, duplicate, closed, irrelevant

Do not skip states. State history becomes operational intelligence.

9. Firestore data model

Firestore is fine for the first serious version. Keep documents small, denormalize intentionally, and avoid storing large raw scrape payloads forever. Use Firestore TTL policies for temporary raw observations or temporary tokens because Firestore TTL can automatically remove stale documents based on an expiration timestamp.

10. Scoring engine

The scoring engine should prioritize acquisition targets.

Use five scores.

Truth Gap Score
Demand Score
Reachability Score
Confidence Score
Risk Score

Then compute:

Priority Score =
  (Truth Gap Score * 0.40)
+ (Demand Score * 0.30)
+ (Reachability Score * 0.20)
+ (Confidence Score * 0.10)
- (Risk Score * 0.30)

Do not overweight “no website.” That is an agency-style signal. For MenuList, the stronger signal is no reliable customer-facing menu/hours truth.

Truth Gap Score

Example weights:

Signal	Weight
No verified menu	+25
Menu exists only as image/PDF	+15
Menu appears stale	+15
Hours missing or conflicting	+15
No canonical customer-facing page	+15
Phone/contact incomplete	+5
Fragmented presence across platforms	+10
Demand Score

Use proxy signals:

Signal	Weight
Customer requested menu on MenuList	+35
High search impressions for business name	+25
Dense local category cluster	+15
Popular category, e.g. cafe/restaurant	+10
High review volume / footfall proxy	+15

Be careful with restricted third-party review data. If used, treat it as temporary lead intelligence, not canonical public MenuList content.

Reachability Score
Signal	Weight
Public phone available	+30
Website contact page available	+20
Instagram DM link available	+10
Email available	+20
Physical location in target cluster	+20
Risk Score
Signal	Penalty
Source terms risk high	+30
Low entity confidence	+20
Possible duplicate	+15
Possible closed business	+20
Missing contact path	+15
Outreach compliance risk	+20

High risk does not necessarily mean reject. It means route to manual QA.

The preview should not look like a website builder output. It should look like MenuList infrastructure.

This page is currently unclaimed. Claim it to verify your business information and publish an owner-confirmed MenuList page.

The preview page is a claim artifact, not a content farm.

19. Apify integration design

Do not hardcode one scraper. Build a connector model.

Source connector interface
TypeScript
type SourceConnector = {
  id: string;
  provider: "apify";
  sourceType:
    | "search_results"
    | "business_directory"
    | "business_website"
    | "social_profile"
    | "manual_seed";

  actorId: string;

  buildInput: (campaign: Campaign) => Record<string, unknown>;
  normalizeItem: (item: unknown) => RawObservation;
  termsRisk: "low" | "medium" | "high";
};
Apify run lifecycle
1. Scheduled function selects active campaign.
2. Function creates `sourceRuns/{id}`.
3. Function starts Apify Actor with campaign input.
4. Apify webhook calls `/api/webhooks/apify`.
5. Webhook validates secret.
6. Webhook writes event and enqueues dataset ingestion task.
7. Dataset ingestion task fetches dataset items.
8. Items become `rawObservations`.
9. Normalization tasks create/update `businessCandidates`.

Apify supports running Actors/tasks programmatically and retrieving default dataset output, while Apify webhooks can call your endpoint when Actor runs transition to states like succeeded or failed.
Apify
+1

Webhook handler behavior

The webhook handler should return quickly.

Validate webhook secret
Validate event type
Check idempotency key: actorRunId + eventType
Create ingestion task
Return 200

Do not process the dataset inside the webhook request.

20. Entity resolution / deduplication

This is critical. Dirty duplicates will destroy trust.

Candidate key
normalized_name + normalized_area + city

Example:

"third-wave-coffee-indiranagar-bangalore"
Deduplication signals
name similarity
phone match
website match
address similarity
geo proximity
social link match
manual override
Entity confidence
entityConfidence =
  phoneMatch * 0.35
+ websiteMatch * 0.25
+ nameSimilarity * 0.20
+ geoProximity * 0.10
+ categoryMatch * 0.10

If confidence is below threshold:

status = duplicate_suspected
qa.required = true

Do not merge automatically when phone/website conflict.

24. Security model

Use Firebase Auth for owners and operators. Use custom claims for roles such as owner, operator, admin, and superadmin; Firebase Admin SDK supports custom claims for access control, and those claims can be enforced in Firebase security rules.
Firebase

Firestore Security Rules should prevent direct client writes to sensitive internal collections. Firestore rules evaluate client requests against path-specific allow expressions, but server client libraries bypass Firestore Security Rules and rely on IAM, so privileged server code must be treated separately.
Firebase

Use App Check on client-accessible Firebase resources to reduce abuse from unauthorized clients. App Check can reject requests that lack valid attestation, but it does not eliminate all abuse vectors, so it should complement—not replace—auth, rate limits, and server-side validation.
Firebase

Use Cloud Storage for owner-uploaded menus/photos/PDFs, with file-size and content-type validation in Storage Rules. Firebase Cloud Storage supports web uploads, and Storage Security Rules can restrict access by path, user auth, file metadata, content type, and size.
Firebase
+1

Role matrix
Collection	Public	Owner	Operator	Admin
businesses published fields	read	read/edit own allowed fields	read/edit	full
businessCandidates	no	no	read/edit	full
rawObservations	no	no	read limited	full
previewPages	token only	token only	full	full
claimTokens	token validation only	token validation only	read limited	full
outreachAttempts	no	no	read/edit	full
auditReports	token only	token only	full	full
Sensitive rules

Public users cannot read raw observations.

Owners cannot see source scraping details.

Owners can edit only their claimed business.

Operators cannot change billing/security config.

All publish actions create immutable verification events.

All field changes produce audit history.

25. Firestore rules shape

Simplified example:

JavaScript
rules_version = '2';

service cloud.firestore {
  match /databases/{database}/documents {

    function signedIn() {
      return request.auth != null;
    }

    function isAdmin() {
      return signedIn() && request.auth.token.role in ["admin", "superadmin"];
    }

    function isOperator() {
      return signedIn() && request.auth.token.role in ["operator", "admin", "superadmin"];
    }

    function isOwnerOfBusiness(businessId) {
      return signedIn()
        && exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/businesses/$(businessId))
        && request.auth.uid in get(/databases/$(database)/documents/businesses/$(businessId)).data.verification.ownerUserIds;
    }

    match /businesses/{businessId} {
      allow read: if resource.data.status == "published" || isOperator() || isOwnerOfBusiness(businessId);
      allow update: if isOperator() || isOwnerOfBusiness(businessId);
      allow create, delete: if isAdmin();
    }

    match /businessCandidates/{candidateId} {
      allow read, write: if isOperator();
    }

    match /rawObservations/{observationId} {
      allow read, write: if isAdmin();
    }

    match /outreachAttempts/{attemptId} {
      allow read, write: if isOperator();
    }
  }
}

Actual rules should be stricter and field-specific, but this is the shape.

  maxCandidatesCreatedPerDay: number;
  maxPreviewPagesPerDay: number;

Add kill switches:

pause campaign if duplicate rate > threshold
pause campaign if QA rejection rate > threshold
pause outreach if complaint rate > threshold
pause source if termsRisk becomes high
pause source if cost per valid candidate exceeds threshold

Do this from the beginning. Agentic/scraping systems can burn money and create junk quickly.

31. The strongest strategic version

The best version is not:

Find restaurants → pitch MenuList

It is:

Detect broken public truth
→ create claimable preview
→ show owner the gap
→ owner verifies
→ MenuList becomes the fresh public record
→ customers use/share/request updates
→ freshness improves
→ nearby businesses see adoption
→ cluster authority compounds

That is the correct loop.

The in-house system should make this loop repeatable.

But enforce this rule:

That is the difference between a scraper-led growth hack and infrastructure-grade business truth acquisition.
````

````text
You are right to simplify this. Do not build another product. Build an internal lead engine for MenuList.

My decision: do not generate AI preview links for every cold lead.
Use a cheaper flow first:

Find valid restaurant/cafe leads
→ filter hard
→ one-click outreach
→ ask them to send menu on WhatsApp/email
→ generate MenuList menu link only after they respond
→ send their finished MenuList link + QR

That is cleaner, cheaper, and better aligned with MenuList.

My recommendation
Do not send an AI-generated preview in first message

The preview sounds attractive, but it creates three problems:

Most cold leads will not reply, so preview generation is wasted.

AI can hallucinate menu/items/photos, which is dangerous for MenuList’s trust layer.

The real conversion event is not viewing a preview. The real conversion event is the owner sending their menu or confirming their business info.

So the first message should not be:

“We created a preview page for you.”

It should be:

“We help restaurants create a clean digital menu link and QR. Send us your menu photo/PDF on WhatsApp and we’ll create your MenuList link.”

That is a lower-friction ask.

What link should you send?

You should send a link, but not an AI-generated preview link.

Send a tracking/onboarding link that uses your existing MenuList flow.

Example:

menulist.com/start?lead=abc123

or:

menulist.com/create-menu/abc-cafe-bangalore

This link should not generate a full page. It should only:

identify the lead,

show the business name if available,

let them upload/send menu,

let them continue on WhatsApp,

track who clicked,

attach the response to the lead record.

This costs almost nothing because it is deterministic. No AI needed before they show intent.

The correct flow
Flow 1: WhatsApp-first

For leads with phone number:

Apify finds lead
→ system validates lead
→ owner/operator clicks Send WhatsApp
→ WhatsApp opens with predefined message
→ business replies with menu/photo/PDF
→ MenuList generates menu link
→ send final MenuList link + QR

Do not fully automate WhatsApp blasting at the start. WhatsApp’s own policy says you may only contact people if they gave you their number and you have opt-in permission; it also says business-initiated conversations must use approved templates, and negative feedback can limit access.
whatsapp.com

So for the first version, build one-click assisted sending, not blind bulk automation.

Meaning:

Button: Open WhatsApp
→ opens wa.me/{phone}?text={template}
→ human reviews
→ human sends

This still removes 90% of manual work without risking your WhatsApp account quality.

Flow 2: Email-first

For leads with email:

Apify finds lead
→ system validates lead
→ email template sent
→ reply or click tracked
→ menu received
→ MenuList link generated

Email is cheaper and more scalable. Amazon SES lists outbound email at $0.10 per 1,000 emails, excluding attachment/data extras.
Amazon Web Services, Inc.

Use email for colder volume. Use WhatsApp for higher-quality or more reachable leads.

Flow 3: Preview only after signal

Generate an AI/menu preview only after one of these happens:

They replied
They clicked the onboarding link
They sent a menu photo/PDF
They asked “what is this?”
They are a top 5–10% lead by score

This is the key rule:

No intent → no AI preview.
Intent shown → generate asset.

That keeps cost and operational noise low.

Cost reality
Apify cost is small

Apify’s maintained Google Maps Scraper lists pricing from $2.10 per 1,000 scraped places. Another Apify Google Maps scraper lists $2.50 per 1,000 results.
Apify
+1

Rough math:

10,000 scraped places = ~$21–$25
100,000 scraped places = ~$210–$250

The expensive part is not scraping.

The expensive parts are:

bad leads
duplicate leads
wrong category
unreachable contacts
WhatsApp compliance/account risk
manual cleanup
AI previews for people who never reply

So the system should optimize for lead quality, not scrape volume.

WhatsApp cost is manageable, but risk matters

WhatsApp Business Platform charges per delivered message, based on market and message category. Meta lists marketing, utility, authentication, and service as the main categories, and says pricing varies by market-category pair.
WhatsApp for Business

For MenuList cold acquisition, your first outbound message will likely be treated as marketing, not utility.

The bigger issue is not only cost. It is deliverability and account health. WhatsApp can limit accounts that receive negative feedback or send at scale in unauthorized ways.
whatsapp.com

So start with:

manual one-click WhatsApp
small daily volume
high-quality leads only
track block/negative response

Then automate only after the message is proven.

AI preview cost is not worth it before reply

Text-generation cost may be small, but AI preview cost has hidden overhead:

prompting
page generation
image generation
QA
hallucination risk
wrong business info risk
cleanup
hosting clutter

If you generate 1,000 AI previews and only 2–5% reply, 950+ previews are wasted.

Instead, use AI only after they send their actual menu. Then AI is doing useful work:

menu image/PDF → structured MenuList page

That directly creates product value.

The internal tool you should build

Keep it brutally simple.

1. Campaign creator

Fields:

City
Area
Category
Keyword
Max leads
Lead quality filters

Example:

City: Bangalore
Areas: Koramangala, Indiranagar, HSR
Category: cafe / restaurant
Keywords:
- cafe near Koramangala
- restaurants in Indiranagar
- cloud kitchen HSR
2. Apify importer

Use Apify to pull:

business name
category
phone
email if available
website
Google Maps URL
address/area
rating/review count as internal signal only
opening status if available
menu URL if available

Important: use Google Maps data only as lead intelligence, not as MenuList canonical data. Google Maps Platform terms restrict scraping/exporting/storing/resharing Maps content outside the services, including business names, addresses, places information, and reviews.
Google Cloud

Practical rule:

Apify helps us find who to contact.
Owner-provided data becomes MenuList truth.
3. Lead database

Minimal schema:

TypeScript
type Lead = {
  id: string;

  businessName: string;
  category: string;
  city: string;
  area?: string;
  address?: string;

  phone?: string;
  email?: string;
  website?: string;
  mapsUrl?: string;

  source: "apify_google_maps" | "manual" | "directory" | "referral";
  sourceRunId?: string;

  hasWebsite?: boolean;
  hasPhone?: boolean;
  hasEmail?: boolean;
  hasMenuUrl?: boolean;

  score: number;

  status:
    | "new"
    | "qualified"
    | "rejected"
    | "contacted_whatsapp"
    | "contacted_email"
    | "replied"
    | "menu_received"
    | "menu_link_created"
    | "converted"
    | "do_not_contact";

  outreach: {
    whatsappSentAt?: Date;
    emailSentAt?: Date;
    lastMessageTemplateId?: string;
    repliedAt?: Date;
    notes?: string;
  };

  menuList: {
    businessId?: string;
    menuUrl?: string;
    onboardingUrl?: string;
    qrUrl?: string;
  };

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};

That is enough.

Do not build complex provenance, freshness engines, preview pages, audit reports, etc. yet.

4. Lead scoring

Score leads with simple rules.

+30 phone available
+20 email available
+20 no website
+20 no menu URL
+15 restaurant/cafe category match
+10 high local relevance
-30 chain/franchise
-40 no contact
-50 wrong category
-50 duplicate

Example:

Score >= 70 → send now
Score 40–69 → review manually
Score < 40 → reject

The goal is to avoid wasting outreach on junk.

5. Outreach dashboard

Simple table:

Business
Area
Phone
Email
Website?
Menu?
Score
Status
Actions

Actions:

Open WhatsApp
Send Email
Mark Replied
Mark Menu Received
Create MenuList Link
Reject
Do Not Contact

This is the whole system.

One-click WhatsApp message

Use this as the first version:

Hi {{business_name}}, this is Danny from MenuList.

We help restaurants create a clean digital menu link + QR that customers can open instantly.

If you send your current menu photo/PDF here, we’ll create your MenuList link and share it back.

Example: {{example_menulist_link}}

You can also start here:
{{onboarding_link}}

Do not say:

We scraped your Google listing.
We made a page for you.
Your information is wrong.
We are an AI tool.

Keep the ask simple:

Send menu → get link.
Email template

Subject:

Quick digital menu link for {{business_name}}

Body:

Hi {{business_name}} team,

I’m Danny from MenuList.

We help restaurants create a clean digital menu link and QR code that customers can open instantly from WhatsApp, Instagram, or in-store.

If you share your current menu photo/PDF, we can create your MenuList link and send it back.

Start here:
{{onboarding_link}}

Or reply with your menu attached.

Thanks,
Danny
MenuList

This is better than overexplaining “business truth layer” to local restaurant owners.

Internally, MenuList is the business truth layer. Externally, the first wedge is:

clean digital menu link + QR
Should you use preview links at all?

Use three tiers.

Tier 1: No preview

For normal cold leads.

Message:

Send menu → we create link.

Use this for 80–90% of leads.

Tier 2: Lightweight onboarding link

For all qualified leads.

Example:

menulist.com/start/abc-cafe-bangalore

This page says:

Create your MenuList menu link

Business: ABC Cafe
Step 1: Upload menu photo/PDF
Step 2: Confirm business info
Step 3: Get menu link + QR

No AI. No generated menu. No fake preview.

Use this for almost everyone.

Tier 3: AI-generated preview

Only for:

high-value leads
businesses that clicked but did not submit
businesses that replied
businesses with uploaded menu images
manual founder-selected leads

This should be maybe 5–10% of leads, not 100%.

The experiment I would run

Run an A/B/C test with 300 leads.

Group A: Template only
No link.
Ask them to send menu.
Group B: Template + onboarding link
Ask them to send menu.
Include menulist.com/start/{lead}
Group C: Template + AI preview
Include generated preview.

Measure:

reply rate
click rate
menu received rate
menu link created rate
converted/claimed rate
negative response rate
cost per menu received

Decision rule:

If AI preview does not improve menu_received_rate by at least 2x over onboarding link, kill it for cold outreach.

Why 2x? Because AI previews add complexity, QA, and brand risk. A small lift is not enough.

My bet: Group B wins on cost-adjusted basis.

The lean system architecture

Since MenuList already exists, add only one internal module:

/admin/leads
Pages
/admin/leads
/admin/leads/import
/admin/leads/campaigns
/admin/leads/[leadId]
/start/[leadSlug]
Backend jobs
runApifyCampaign()
importApifyResults()
dedupeLeads()
scoreLeads()
generateOnboardingLink()
sendEmail()
recordWhatsAppClick()
No new product surface

The only external page is:

/start/[leadSlug]

That page pushes them into the existing MenuList menu creation flow.

What “automation” should mean here

Not:

scrape 10,000 leads
blast 10,000 WhatsApps
generate 10,000 previews

That creates spam risk and low-quality data.

Instead:

scrape 10,000
filter to 1,000
score to 300
manually/assisted-send 100/day
generate menu links only for responders

This is much more efficient.

Daily operating flow
Morning:
Run Apify campaign for target area/category.

System:
Imports leads.
Dedupes.
Scores.
Rejects weak leads.

You/operator:
Reviews top 100.
Clicks WhatsApp/email send.
Tracks replies.

When menu arrives:
Upload into existing MenuList flow.
Generate menu link.
Send back link + QR.
Mark converted.

That is enough.

What to avoid

Do not build:

AI website generator
GitHub hosted demo pages
public unclaimed pages at scale
AI-generated restaurant photos
Google review/photo reuse
fully automated WhatsApp blasting
complex CRM
multi-step sales pipeline

You are not building HubSpot. You are building a lead intake machine for MenuList.

My final call

Build the internal tool.

But build it like this:

Apify lead discovery
→ lead scoring
→ one-click assisted outreach
→ onboarding link
→ menu received
→ existing MenuList menu generation
→ send final link + QR

Use AI after menu received, not before.

The strongest first CTA is not:

“Check your preview.”

It is:

“Send your menu. We’ll create your clean MenuList link.”

That is cheaper, simpler, and much closer to MenuList’s real wedge.
````

````text
Stage 0 — Strategy and operating rules

This stage defines the operating doctrine. No code yet. No database yet. This prevents us from building a bloated internal CRM or a risky spam engine.

0.1 The system we are building

The system is:

MenuList Lead Engine

Its job:

Find restaurants/cafes with weak digital menu presence
→ qualify them
→ send one-click outreach
→ collect menu from owner
→ generate MenuList link using existing MenuList flow
→ send back menu link + QR
→ track conversion

It is not:

a CRM
a website builder
a public directory scraper
an AI demo-page generator
a sales automation platform
a separate MenuList product

This distinction matters. The system should serve MenuList’s current acquisition motion, not become a parallel product.

0.2 Core decision

My recommendation:

Do not generate preview links for every cold lead.

Default first message should ask for the menu.

The cold flow should be:

Lead found
→ qualified
→ outreach sent
→ owner sends menu/photo/PDF
→ MenuList generates menu link
→ owner receives final link + QR

The preview flow should be reserved for:

high-value leads
leads who clicked but did not submit
leads who replied
leads who sent menu
manual founder-selected targets

So the rule is:

No intent → no AI preview.
Intent shown → generate asset.

This keeps cost low and avoids fake or hallucinated business information.

0.3 Primary success metric

The main metric is not:

leads scraped
messages sent
WhatsApp opens
email opens

The main metric is:

verified MenuList menu links created from outbound leads

The second metric is:

cost per MenuList link created

The system is successful only if it creates actual MenuList assets.

0.4 Source doctrine

Use Apify or similar tools for lead discovery, not truth creation.

Operating rule:

External data finds who to contact.
Owner-provided data becomes MenuList truth.

This is important because Google Maps Platform terms restrict extracting, exporting, scraping, caching, storing, resharing, or rehosting Google Maps content outside Google services. Google’s terms specifically include restrictions around business names, addresses, Places information, and user reviews. So we should treat scraped Google Maps data as temporary lead intelligence, not MenuList’s canonical business data.
Google Cloud

Practical implication:

Allowed:
- use source data to identify candidate restaurants
- use phone/email/website to reach out
- use category/city/area for qualification
- use source URL internally for operator review

Not allowed as MenuList truth:
- scraped reviews
- scraped Google photos
- copied descriptions
- copied menu photos
- long-term public rehosting of Maps-derived content

For MenuList, this is strategically correct anyway. The moat should come from owner-confirmed menus/hours/info, not from scraped third-party data.

0.5 Apify doctrine

Apify is suitable for the first version.

Apify supports running Actors or tasks through API, polling runs, and fetching results from the default dataset. Its JavaScript client also supports programmatic access to Actors, runs, datasets, key-value stores, and request queues.
Apify
+1

Pricing varies by actor and pricing model. Apify’s own help article for Google Maps Scraper pay-per-event pricing says the base charge is $4 per 1,000 places, while a public Apify Google Maps Scraper listing shows “from $2.10 / 1,000 scraped places.” So we should not hardcode cost assumptions; the system should track source-run cost per valid lead.
Apify Help & Support
+1

Operating rule:

Start with Apify.
Do not integrate multiple scraping vendors in v0.
Benchmark alternatives only after first 1,000–3,000 imported leads.

Why:

The first bottleneck will not be scraping cost.
The first bottleneck will be lead quality, duplicates, bad categories, unreachable numbers, and reply rate.
0.6 Outreach doctrine

This is the highest-risk part.

WhatsApp

Do not start with blind automated WhatsApp blasting.

WhatsApp’s business documentation says businesses must obtain opt-in permission before messaging people on WhatsApp, and WhatsApp Business-initiated conversations must use approved message templates. WhatsApp’s business policy also says businesses may initiate conversations only using approved templates.
Facebook Developers
+1

India also has an active regulatory framework for unsolicited commercial communication. TRAI’s TCCCPR framework covers unsolicited commercial communication, and 2025 amendments strengthened consumer protection against UCC.
TRAI
+1

So v0 should be:

one-click assisted WhatsApp

Meaning:

Dashboard button → opens WhatsApp with prefilled message → human reviews → human sends

Not:

system sends 1,000 WhatsApp messages automatically

This still saves most of the work while keeping account risk lower.

Email

Email should be the scalable cold channel.

Amazon SES pricing is currently listed at $0.10 per 1,000 outbound emails, excluding extra data/attachment charges. Resend lists a free tier of 3,000 emails/month and a Pro plan with 50,000 emails/month.
Amazon Web Services, Inc.
+1

Operating rule:

Email can be automated earlier.
WhatsApp should remain assisted until reply quality and complaint risk are understood.
0.7 First outreach CTA

The first CTA should not be:

Check the preview page we made for you.

The first CTA should be:

Send your menu photo/PDF and we will create your MenuList link + QR.

Reason:

Menu submission = intent.
Preview viewing = curiosity.

A restaurant owner sending their menu is a much stronger signal than clicking a pretty page.

0.8 Link strategy

There are three link types.

Type 1: No link

Use for some early WhatsApp tests.

Message asks them to reply with the menu.

Best for testing pure message-market fit.
Type 2: Lightweight onboarding link

Default recommended link.

Example:

menulist.com/start/{leadSlug}

This page should show:

Create your MenuList menu link
Business: {business_name}
Upload menu photo/PDF
Confirm WhatsApp number
Get menu link + QR

No AI. No generated menu. No fake preview.

This page is cheap and useful.

Type 3: AI-generated preview link

Use only after intent or for high-value test groups.

Example triggers:

lead replied
lead clicked onboarding link
lead uploaded menu
lead is top-score lead
operator manually selects lead

This avoids wasting AI and QA cost on cold leads that will never respond.

0.9 Cost doctrine

The system must track cost by campaign, not only globally.

Every campaign should record:

source cost
number of raw leads
number of qualified leads
number of contactable leads
number of messages sent
number of replies
number of menus received
number of MenuList links created
cost per qualified lead
cost per menu received
cost per MenuList link created

Hard caps for v0:

Max raw leads per campaign: 1,000
Max qualified leads contacted per day: 50–100
Max AI previews per campaign: 0 by default
Max AI previews for experiment: 5–10% of contacted leads
Max follow-ups: 2
Max campaign duration before review: 7 days

Initial budget logic:

Spend on scraping: acceptable.
Spend on AI previews before intent: not acceptable.
Spend on email: acceptable.
Spend on WhatsApp automation before proof: not acceptable.
0.10 Data doctrine

Store only what is needed to qualify and contact the lead.

For v0, keep:

business name
category
city
area
phone
email
website
source URL
source type
lead score
status
outreach history
MenuList onboarding link
MenuList generated menu link
notes

Do not store:

reviews
scraped photos
scraped menus
large raw payloads forever
unnecessary personal data
irrelevant third-party profile data

Use source data as temporary acquisition data. Once the owner provides the menu, MenuList stores the owner-provided menu as the real asset.

0.11 Lead quality doctrine

Do not contact every scraped lead.

The system should reject aggressively.

Reject if:

wrong category
no phone and no email
large chain/franchise
duplicate
outside target area
business appears closed
already has strong menu/website presence
low confidence business identity

Prioritize if:

restaurant/cafe/food business
phone available
email available
no website
no obvious menu link
small/local business
in target area
has enough public demand signal

The first version should prefer fewer, cleaner leads.

A small batch of 100 high-quality leads is better than 5,000 noisy contacts.

0.12 Human vs automation boundary

Use automation for:

finding leads
normalizing leads
deduping
scoring
creating onboarding links
preparing messages
tracking statuses
sending email
generating MenuList links after menu intake

Keep human/operator control over:

first WhatsApp send
manual QA for top leads
edge-case rejection
high-value lead handling
negative replies
business disputes

Reason:

WhatsApp account health and brand trust are more valuable than saving the last 10% of manual work.

Automation should remove repetitive work, not remove judgment.

0.13 System states

Keep statuses simple.

TypeScript
type LeadStatus =
  | "new"
  | "qualified"
  | "rejected"
  | "ready_to_contact"
  | "whatsapp_opened"
  | "email_sent"
  | "contacted"
  | "replied"
  | "menu_requested"
  | "menu_received"
  | "menulist_link_created"
  | "menulist_link_sent"
  | "converted"
  | "not_interested"
  | "do_not_contact";

Do not build a complex sales pipeline yet.

This is enough to operate.

0.14 First campaign rule

The first campaign should be narrow.

Recommended first test:

City: Bangalore
Areas: Koramangala, Indiranagar, HSR, Jayanagar
Categories: cafes, restaurants, bakeries, dessert shops
Raw leads: 500–1,000
Contacted leads: 100–200
AI previews: 0 by default
Experiment group: optional 20 leads max

Why this shape:

Dense geography
food-focused
MenuList-relevant
enough businesses
easy to manually inspect
good for learning owner response patterns

Do not start India-wide.

0.15 A/B testing doctrine

Do not debate preview links forever. Test them.

Run three groups:

Group A: message only
Group B: message + onboarding link
Group C: message + AI preview link

But keep Group C small.

Suggested first test:

A: 50 leads
B: 50 leads
C: 20 high-quality leads

Measure:

reply rate
click rate
menu received rate
MenuList link created rate
negative response rate
cost per MenuList link created

Decision rule:

AI preview becomes default only if it materially improves menu_received_rate or MenuList_link_created_rate.

My bar would be high:

AI preview must improve conversion by at least 2x over onboarding link.

If it gives only a small lift, do not use it broadly.

0.16 Outreach positioning

External message should be simple.

Do not say:

business truth layer
canonical infrastructure
AI-generated profile
we scraped your listing
your online presence is broken

Say:

We help restaurants create a clean digital menu link and QR.
Send your current menu photo/PDF and we’ll create your MenuList link.

The owner-facing wedge is:

digital menu link + QR

The internal strategic asset is:

verified business truth

This is the correct split.

0.17 Operating red lines

Hard no:

No scraped Google reviews on MenuList pages.
No scraped Google photos on MenuList pages.
No fake menu items.
No fake prices.
No AI-generated restaurant-specific menu without owner input.
No mass WhatsApp blasting in v0.
No public unclaimed pages at scale.
No AI preview for every cold lead.
No CRM bloat.
No sales pipeline complexity.

Hard yes:

Use Apify for discovery.
Score and filter hard.
Use one-click assisted outreach.
Use onboarding link as default.
Ask owner for menu.
Generate MenuList link after menu received.
Track conversion economics.
Keep source data separate from owner-provided truth.
0.18 Stage 0 final operating charter

The internal rulebook:

MenuList Lead Engine exists to acquire verified menus, not scrape directories.

Apify finds candidate restaurants.
Scoring filters them.
Operators send one-click WhatsApp or automated email.
The default CTA is: send your menu and get a MenuList link + QR.
The default link is a lightweight onboarding link, not an AI preview.
AI preview is used only after intent or in small experiments.
Google/third-party data is lead intelligence, not MenuList truth.
Owner-provided menu/info becomes MenuList truth.
Success is measured by MenuList links created, not leads scraped.

That is Stage 0.

Next stage: Lead source strategy — exactly where to get leads from, what fields to extract, which Apify actors/providers to use, and how to compare source quality.
````
