````text
4.17 Source campaign relationship

Use this hierarchy:

growthCampaign
  → growthSourceRun
      → sourceLeadCandidate
          → growthLead

A campaign is the strategic container:

Bangalore cafe QR/menu-link acquisition

A source run is one source execution:

Apify query for cafes in Koramangala

A candidate is raw imported source data.

A lead is the deduped acquisition object.

4.18 Cold discovery query strategy

For Apify/maps sources, use local cluster queries.

Bad:

restaurants in India
restaurants in Bangalore
food businesses near me

Good:

cafes in Koramangala Bangalore
restaurants in Indiranagar Bangalore
bakeries in HSR Layout Bangalore
dessert shops in Jayanagar Bangalore
cloud kitchens in Whitefield Bangalore

Why:

better local density
easier scoring
fewer irrelevant results
cleaner local campaigns
better cluster learning

AI Source Planner should generate queries from:

city
area
category
past performance
business density
source quality
4.19 Recommended source run caps

Default cold discovery caps:

max areas per campaign: 5
max categories per area: 5
max results per area-category query: 50–100
max raw leads per campaign: configurable

For long-term system, caps should be dynamic:

trusted source + high conversion history → higher cap
new source / untested area → lower cap
high duplicate source → lower cap
high negative response segment → pause

AI can recommend cap changes, but policy should enforce max daily spend and channel caps.

4.20 Enrichment decision rule

Every lead should get an enrichment decision.

TypeScript
type EnrichmentDecision = {
  action: "enrich" | "skip" | "reject" | "human_review";

  enrichmentTypes: (
    | "website_check"
    | "contact_extraction"
    | "instagram_lookup"
    | "facebook_lookup"
    | "secondary_provider"
  )[];

  reason: string;
  maxCostUsd?: number;
};

Default rules:

Reject first if wrong vertical / duplicate / suppressed.
Skip enrichment if lead score too low.
Run website check if website exists.
Run contact extraction if lead is relevant but missing best channel.
Run secondary provider only if lead is high-fit and contactability is weak.

This keeps cost tied to lead potential.

4.21 Source selection by lead type

Different lead goals need different sources.

Need more cold local leads

Use:

Apify
Outscraper benchmark
Scrap.io later
manual cluster lists
Need more warm/social leads

Use:

Instagram content CTA
Click-to-Instagram ads
Messenger/Page campaigns
Meta Lead Ads
Need more contactability

Use:

website crawl
contact extraction
secondary provider enrichment
manual review
Need to improve conversion

Use:

owned behavioral signals
retargeting buckets
abandoned onboarding events
clicked-but-not-started leads

The AI Source Planner should choose the source based on the current bottleneck.

Example:

If qualified leads are low → run cold discovery.
If contact-ready rate is low → run enrichment.
If onboarding start rate is low → change message/channel/flow.
If onboarding completion is low → product/onboarding feedback issue.
4.22 Source bottleneck diagnosis

The source layer should diagnose where acquisition is failing.

Low raw lead volume

Problem:

not enough source coverage

Action:

expand areas/categories or add provider
High duplicate rate

Problem:

same businesses from repeated queries or bad source overlap

Action:

reduce overlapping queries, improve dedupe, change source
Low qualified rate

Problem:

wrong category/source too broad

Action:

narrow category, better AI Source Planner, change query
Low contact-ready rate

Problem:

contacts missing or invalid

Action:

selective enrichment, different source, website crawl
High negative response rate

Problem:

bad targeting, bad message, wrong channel

Action:

pause source/segment, change offer angle/channel
Low onboarding start rate

Problem:

message/CTA/flow mismatch

Action:

test message angle, channel, onboarding flow route
Low onboarding completion rate

Problem:

onboarding flow mismatch or low-quality leads

Action:

adjust flow router or lead qualification
4.23 Sources to avoid by default

Avoid making these primary lead sources:

Zomato/Swiggy scraping
Google reviews/photos scraping
Instagram mass handle scraping
Facebook group scraping
unverified purchased lead lists
Google Business Profile APIs for lead gen

Reason:

policy risk
poor data quality
brand risk
weak strategic fit

This does not mean never learn from market data. It means do not build the Growth Engine around fragile or high-risk sources.

4.24 Manual import is still important

Even with AI and scraping, support:

manual CSV import
operator-added lead
referral-added lead
founder-added high-value lead

Manual leads often outperform scraped leads because they may be curated.

Manual import fields:

business_name
category
city
area
phone
email
instagram
facebook
website
source_note
recommended_channel
recommended_flow

After import, manual leads still pass:

dedupe
AI scoring
channel router
suppression check

No source should bypass the system.

4.25 Inbound social source flow

For Instagram/Messenger inbound:

message received via webhook
→ identity matched to existing lead or new lead created
→ AI classifies intent
→ lead source = social_inbound
→ channel eligibility = active window
→ AI next-best-action recommends reply/onboarding route

This is not “lead scraping.” It is inbound lead capture.

Instagram and Messenger webhooks support receiving real-time messaging events, which makes this suitable for Growth Engine inbox and reply classification.
Facebook Developers
+1

4.26 Paid lead source flow

For Meta Lead Ads:

lead form submitted
→ webhook creates Growth Lead
→ AI scores
→ channel router selects next step
→ message/flow sent quickly
→ onboarding events feed back

Paid lead forms should be routed fast.

Recommended SLA:

respond within 5 minutes when possible

Why:

lead intent decays quickly after form submission

For paid leads, channel routing should often be:

email + WhatsApp if phone provided and eligibility allows

But the system must still check suppression and channel policy.

4.27 Owned signal source flow

For existing MenuList behavioral signals:

onboarding abandoned
→ Growth Engine creates/updates lead
→ AI classifies drop reason if available
→ Next-best-action chooses channel and message
→ route back to flow or alternate flow

Examples:

started but dropped at phone step
clicked setup link but did not start
business searched but did not create account
business came from referral but did not finish

These should be high-priority because they already interacted with MenuList.

4.28 Source scoring formula

Each source/segment should get a score.

Source Score =
  0.25 × Qualified Rate
+ 0.20 × Contact-Ready Rate
+ 0.25 × Onboarding Completion Rate
+ 0.15 × Cost Efficiency
+ 0.10 × Low Negative Rate
+ 0.05 × Low Duplicate Rate

Where:

Cost Efficiency = normalized inverse of cost per completed onboarding
Low Negative Rate = inverse of negative response rate
Low Duplicate Rate = inverse of duplicate rate

This score lets the AI Source Planner choose where to run next.

Do not use raw lead count in the score except as a minimum sample-size check.

Long-term, source mix should evolve.

Early operating mode
Apify cold discovery

Growth mode
AI Source Planner

4.32 Final source strategy

The Growth Engine should use this source stack:

Primary cold discovery:
Apify Google Maps / maps-source providers

Backup cold discovery:
Outscraper, later Scrap.io

Enrichment:
website crawl, contact extraction, social link detection, selective secondary provider lookup

Warm/inbound:
Instagram DM, Messenger, WhatsApp inbound, email inbound

Paid:
Meta Lead Ads, click-to-WhatsApp, click-to-Instagram, click-to-Messenger, search ads

Owned:
MenuList onboarding drop-offs, flow clicks, customer/business demand signals, referrals

The system should rank every source by:

qualified leads
contact-ready leads
onboarding starts
onboarding completions
cost per completion
negative response risk

The strategic rule:

Use cold sources to create pipeline.
Use warm/inbound sources to capture intent.
Use owned signals to compound.
Use enrichment only when a lead is worth it.
Use AI to decide where source spend and attention should go next.

That is the correct long-term source strategy.
````

````text
Spec 5 — AI Lead Intelligence Layer
5.1 Purpose

The AI Lead Intelligence Layer decides whether a raw business candidate is worth spending acquisition effort on.

It answers:

Is this a real relevant business?
Is this a good MenuList acquisition target?
How strong is the need signal?
Can we reach them?
How risky is contacting them?
Should we enrich, contact, hold, reject, or send to human review?

It does not send messages.

It does not choose final outreach channel.

It does not manage onboarding.

It prepares the lead for the next systems:

Channel Identity Registry
Channel Eligibility Engine
AI Channel Router
Message Generator
Promotion Campaign Builder
5.2 Position in the pipeline

The flow is:

source candidate imported
→ normalize
→ dedupe
→ AI Lead Intelligence
→ channel identity registry
→ channel eligibility
→ channel router
→ outreach / inbox / routing

The AI Lead Intelligence Layer should run after basic normalization and dedupe, but before any outreach decision.

5.3 Core output

For every lead, this layer produces:

fit score
need score
contactability score
intent score
risk score
total score
lead segment
recommended acquisition action
AI explanation
confidence
human review requirement

Example output:

JSON
{
  "fitScore": 92,
  "needScore": 81,
  "contactabilityScore": 78,
  "intentScore": 0,
  "riskScore": 24,
  "totalScore": 83,
  "segment": "A",
  "recommendedAction": "contact",
  "humanReviewRequired": false,
  "explanation": [
    "Relevant cafe in target area",
    "Likely single-location SMB",
    "Phone and website available",
    "Likely need for clean menu link + QR",
    "No major suppression or duplicate risk"
  ],
  "confidence": 0.86
}
5.4 AI workers inside this layer

The AI Lead Intelligence Layer should be composed of narrow AI workers.

Not one big agent.

Use these workers:

1. Business Normalizer
2. Business Fit Classifier
3. Business Scale Detector
4. Need Detector
5. Contactability Analyzer
6. Intent Signal Analyzer
7. Risk Detector
8. Lead Scorer
9. Human Review Decider
10. Intelligence Explainer

Each worker should have:

input schema
output schema
confidence score
allowed data
blocked data
fallback behavior

This keeps AI useful but controlled.

5.5 Worker 1 — Business Normalizer
Purpose

Clean messy source data into a consistent business record.

Input:

TypeScript
type BusinessNormalizerInput = {
  rawBusinessName: string;
  rawCategory?: string;
  rawAddress?: string;
  rawCity?: string;
  rawArea?: string;
  rawWebsite?: string;
  rawPhone?: string;
  rawEmail?: string;
  rawInstagram?: string;
  rawFacebook?: string;
  sourceProvider: string;
  sourceType: string;
};

Output:

TypeScript
type BusinessNormalizerOutput = {
  cleanBusinessName: string;
  normalizedName: string;

  normalizedCategory:
    | "restaurant"
    | "cafe"
    | "bakery"
    | "dessert_shop"
    | "cloud_kitchen"
    | "juice_shop"
    | "tea_shop"
    | "bar_restaurant"
    | "hotel_restaurant"
    | "other_food"
    | "non_food"
    | "unknown";

  normalizedCity?: string;
  normalizedArea?: string;

  cleanedWebsite?: string;
  normalizedDomain?: string;

  cleanedPhoneE164?: string;
  cleanedEmail?: string;
  cleanedInstagramUsername?: string;

  normalizationWarnings: string[];

  confidence: number;
};
What AI should do
clean business names
normalize category
identify obvious non-food businesses
standardize city/area
detect malformed websites
detect malformed social handles
What AI should not do
invent missing contact details
invent location
invent business category when source is too weak

If unsure:

category = unknown
confidence below threshold
5.6 Worker 2 — Business Fit Classifier
Purpose

Decide whether this business is relevant to MenuList acquisition.

Fit is not the same as need.

A business can be relevant but low-need.

Example:

restaurant with strong existing menu system = relevant category, lower need

Input:

TypeScript
type BusinessFitInput = {
  businessName: string;
  category: string;
  city?: string;
  area?: string;
  website?: string;
  sourceContext?: string;
  campaignTarget?: {
    city?: string;
    areas?: string[];
    categories?: string[];
  };
};

Output:

TypeScript
type BusinessFitOutput = {
  isRelevant: boolean;

  fitCategory:
    | "ideal"
    | "good"
    | "maybe"
    | "poor"
    | "reject";

  fitScore: number; // 0-100

  reasons: string[];

  rejectReason?:
    | "wrong_vertical"
    | "outside_target_area"
    | "large_non_target_business"
    | "not_business"
    | "insufficient_data";

  confidence: number;
};
Fit scoring guide
90–100: ideal food SMB in target area
75–89: good food business, likely relevant
55–74: maybe relevant, needs more intelligence
30–54: weak fit
0–29: reject
Ideal leads
single-location cafes
restaurants
bakeries
dessert shops
juice/tea shops
local cloud kitchens
small local food brands
Weak or reject leads
large chains
hotels without clear restaurant focus
liquor-only venues
grocery stores
catering-only businesses
corporate cafeterias
wrong city
non-food businesses
5.7 Worker 3 — Business Scale Detector
Purpose

Detect whether the business is owner-reachable SMB, local chain, franchise, or large chain.

This matters because acquisition motion differs.

Input:

TypeScript
type BusinessScaleInput = {
  businessName: string;
  category: string;
  website?: string;
  city?: string;
  area?: string;
  sourceOccurrences?: {
    sameNameCount?: number;
    areasSeen?: string[];

};

Output:

TypeScript
type BusinessScaleOutput = {
  scale:
    | "single_location_smb"
    | "small_local_chain"
    | "large_chain"
    | "franchise"
    | "unknown";

  scoreImpact: number; // positive or negative

  reasons: string[];

  confidence: number;
};
Scoring logic
single_location_smb → positive
small_local_chain → positive or neutral
large_chain → negative or hold
franchise → human review / lower priority
unknown → neutral
Why this matters

Early acquisition should prioritize:

owner-operated SMBs
small local chains
businesses likely to respond directly

Avoid spending effort on:

large national brands
corporate-managed chains
businesses requiring long approval cycles
5.8 Worker 4 — Need Detector
Purpose

Detect whether the business likely has a MenuList-relevant acquisition need.

This is the most important worker in this layer.

The question is not:

Does this business exist?

The question is:

Is there a clear reason this business may care about MenuList?

Input:

TypeScript
type NeedDetectorInput = {
  businessName: string;
  category: string;
  website?: {
    url?: string;
    status?: "no_website" | "loads" | "down" | "blocked" | "unknown";
    inspectedPages?: {
      url: string;
      title?: string;
      textSnippet?: string;
      detectedLinks?: string[];
    }[];
  };

  social?: {
    instagramUrl?: string;
    facebookUrl?: string;
  };

  sourceSignals?: {
    hasWebsite?: boolean;
    hasMenuUrl?: boolean;
    menuFormat?: "page" | "pdf" | "image" | "instagram_only" | "unknown";
    contactAvailable?: boolean;
  };

  campaignOfferAngles?: string[];
};

Output:

TypeScript
type NeedDetectorOutput = {
  needScore: number; // 0-100

  primaryNeed:
    | "menu_link_qr"
    | "instagram_bio_menu"
    | "whatsapp_menu_link"
    | "google_profile_menu_link"
    | "simple_setup"
    | "unknown"
    | "low_need";

  needSignals: {
    type:
      | "no_website"
      | "weak_website"
      | "no_clear_menu_link"
      | "pdf_menu"
      | "image_menu"
      | "instagram_only"
      | "broken_menu_link"
      | "not_mobile_friendly"
      | "no_qr_share_path"
      | "social_only_presence"
      | "customer_demand_signal"
      | "manual_signal";

    strength: "weak" | "medium" | "strong";
    explanation: string;
    confidence: number;
  }[];

  recommendedOfferAngles: (
    | "menu_link_qr"
    | "instagram_bio_menu"
    | "whatsapp_menu_link"
    | "google_profile_menu_link"
    | "simple_setup"
  )[];

  confidence: number;
};
Need score guide
90–100: very strong MenuList-relevant need
75–89: strong need
55–74: moderate need
30–54: weak need
0–29: low/no need
Strong need signals
no website
no clear menu link
only Instagram presence
menu only as PDF/image
broken or hard-to-use menu page
no obvious QR/shareable customer link
business is highly customer-facing
inbound request/customer demand signal
Weak need signals
clean mobile menu already exists
business has strong direct ordering/menu stack
large chain with centralized digital presence
unclear food relevance
Important messaging note

The system may use these signals internally, but outreach should not say:

Your website is weak.
Your menu is missing.
We saw you do not have X.

Need signals guide message selection. They should not become creepy outbound copy.

5.9 Worker 5 — Contactability Analyzer
Purpose

Judge whether the business is reachable and through which identities.

This worker does not make the final channel decision. It assesses channel quality.

Input:

type ContactabilityOutput = {
  contactabilityScore: number; // 0-100

  availableChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

    channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";

Contactability scoring
phone + likely WhatsApp → strong
valid email → strong
Instagram username only → moderate, often warm/inbound preferred
Messenger identity only → useful if inbound/Page context exists
website only → enrich
no channel → weak
Output action

The worker may recommend:

enrich
contactable
hold
reject

But final channel selection belongs to the Channel Router.

Purpose

Output:

type IntentSignalOutput = {

Intent score examples
0: no known intent
20: cold source lead
40: clicked but no reply
60: replied with question

This score should heavily influence follow-up and retargeting later.

5.11 Worker 7 — Risk Detector
Purpose

Protect MenuList from bad outreach, low-quality leads, channel risk, and policy mistakes.

Input:

TypeScript
type RiskDetectorInput = {
  business: GrowthLeadBusiness;
  identities: GrowthLeadIdentitySummary;
  source: GrowthLeadSource;
  suppressionMatches?: GrowthSuppression[];
  previousInteractions?: GrowthEvent[];
  aiSignals?: {
    fitConfidence?: number;
    needConfidence?: number;
    contactConfidence?: number;
  };
};

Output:

TypeScript
type RiskDetectorOutput = {
  riskScore: number; // 0-100, higher = riskier

  flags: {
    type:
      | "suppressed"
      | "possible_duplicate"
      | "wrong_vertical"
      | "outside_target"
      | "low_confidence"
      | "large_chain"
      | "invalid_contact"
      | "source_policy_risk"
      | "channel_policy_risk"
      | "negative_history"
      | "complaint_history"
      | "spam_risk"
      | "unknown";

    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
    explanation: string;
  }[];

  action:
    | "allow"
    | "allow_with_caution"
    | "human_review"
    | "hold"
    | "reject"
    | "suppress";

  confidence: number;
};
Critical flags

These should override everything:

global suppression
do-not-contact
known complaint
wrong number
unsubscribe
duplicate of converted/suppressed lead
invalid identity
High-risk flags

These should require review:

low confidence business identity
large chain
source policy risk
potential duplicate
negative history
unclear channel eligibility
5.12 Worker 8 — Lead Scorer
Purpose

Combine all worker outputs into one acquisition score and segment.

Input:

TypeScript
type LeadScorerInput = {
  fit: BusinessFitOutput;
  scale: BusinessScaleOutput;
  need: NeedDetectorOutput;
  contactability: ContactabilityOutput;
  intent: IntentSignalOutput;
  risk: RiskDetectorOutput;
  campaignContext?: {
    targetCity?: string;
    targetCategories?: string[];
    currentGoal?: "volume" | "quality" | "test" | "retargeting";
  };
};

Output:

TypeScript
type LeadScorerOutput = {
  totalScore: number; // 0-100

  segment: "A" | "B" | "C" | "REJECT";

  recommendedAction:
    | "contact"
    | "enrich"
    | "hold"
    | "human_review"
    | "reject"
    | "suppress";

  componentScores: {
    fit: number;
    need: number;
    contactability: number;
    intent: number;
    risk: number;
  };

  explanation: string[];

  confidence: number;
};
Recommended scoring formula

Use hybrid rule + AI scoring.

Total Score =
  0.25 × Fit Score
+ 0.25 × Need Score
+ 0.20 × Contactability Score
+ 0.15 × Intent Score
+ 0.15 × Source/Segment Quality
- 0.30 × Risk Score

Clamp to 0–100.

If no source/segment quality exists yet, redistribute weight proportionally.

Segment thresholds
A: 80–100
B: 60–79
C: 40–59
REJECT: below 40 or hard reject
Recommended action rules
A + contactable + low risk → contact
A/B + weak contact → enrich
B + medium risk → human_review
C → hold
REJECT → reject
critical risk → suppress/reject
5.13 Worker 9 — Human Review Decider
Purpose

Decide when the AI is not confident enough to act.

Input:

TypeScript
type HumanReviewInput = {
  leadScore: LeadScorerOutput;
  fitConfidence: number;
  needConfidence: number;
  contactConfidence: number;
  riskFlags: RiskDetectorOutput["flags"];
  sourceRisk: "low" | "medium" | "high";
};

Output:

TypeScript
type HumanReviewOutput = {
  humanReviewRequired: boolean;

  reviewReason?:
    | "low_confidence"
    | "possible_duplicate"
    | "source_risk"
    | "channel_risk"
    | "large_chain"
    | "unclear_fit"
    | "negative_history"
    | "high_value_manual_review";

  suggestedReviewerAction:
    | "approve_contact"
    | "reject"
    | "merge_duplicate"
    | "enrich"
    | "hold"
    | "suppress";

  priority: "low" | "normal" | "high" | "urgent";
};
Review triggers
confidence below 0.70
possible duplicate
source risk high
lead score high but risk medium/high
large chain/franchise
wrong vertical ambiguity
negative or DNC history
AI outputs conflict

Example conflict:

Fit classifier says ideal, Risk detector says wrong_vertical.

That must go to human review.

lead.ai = {

5.16 aiRuns schema for this layer

Every AI decision must be auditable.

TypeScript
type AiRun = {
  id: string;

  flowName:
    | "business_normalizer"
    | "business_fit_classifier"
    | "business_scale_detector"
    | "need_detector"
    | "contactability_analyzer"
    | "intent_signal_analyzer"
    | "risk_detector"
    | "lead_scorer"
    | "human_review_decider"
    | "intelligence_explainer";

  leadId: string;

  modelProvider: "google_ai" | "vertex_ai";
  modelName: string;

  inputHash: string;

  output: Record<string, unknown>;

  confidence: number;

  status:
    | "succeeded"
    | "failed"
    | "needs_human_review";

  cost?: {
    inputTokens?: number;
    outputTokens?: number;
    estimatedUsd?: number;
  };

  latencyMs?: number;

  createdAt: Date;
};

Do not store unnecessarily large prompts forever if not needed. Store input hash and structured output. Keep full prompt only for debugging/evals if required.

5.17 AI policy for this layer

Use aiPolicies.

TypeScript
type AiPolicy = {
  flowName: string;

  enabled: boolean;

  autonomyLevel: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;

  confidenceThresholds: {
    autoAccept: number;
    humanReviewBelow: number;
    rejectBelow: number;
  };

  maxDailyRuns: number;
  maxDailyCostUsd: number;

  allowedActions: string[];
  blockedActions: string[];

  modelRoute: string;

  evalRequired: boolean;
};

Recommended defaults:

Business Normalizer: autonomy 3
Business Fit Classifier: autonomy 2
Business Scale Detector: autonomy 2
Need Detector: autonomy 2
Contactability Analyzer: autonomy 2
Risk Detector: autonomy 1–2
Lead Scorer: autonomy 2
Human Review Decider: autonomy 3
Intelligence Explainer: autonomy 3

Meaning:

AI can normalize/score automatically.
AI cannot bypass suppression or message a lead.
Risky outputs go to review.
5.18 Confidence thresholds

Use consistent thresholds.

>= 0.90: high confidence
0.75–0.89: usable confidence
0.60–0.74: human review
< 0.60: unreliable / reject or re-run

Action policy:

high confidence + low risk → allow next system to proceed
medium confidence → allow but flag
low confidence → human review
very low confidence → reject/hold/re-run

For lead scoring:

A lead requires totalScore >= 80 and confidence >= 0.75

For auto-reject:

hard reject allowed only if confidence >= 0.90

For suppression:

AI can suggest suppression.
System can auto-suppress only on clear DNC/complaint with high confidence.
5.19 Hard rules that override AI

No AI score can override:

global suppression
do-not-contact
unsubscribe
known wrong number
known invalid email
duplicate of suppressed lead
duplicate of converted lead
outside legal/channel policy
blocked source type
admin manual block

Hard rules run before AI and after AI.

Order:

pre-AI hard filters
→ AI intelligence
→ post-AI policy gate
5.20 Intelligence refresh rules

Not every lead needs constant re-analysis.

Run AI intelligence when:

lead first imported
new source data added
new identity added
website inspected
reply received
onboarding feedback received
lead is being considered for campaign
lead has gone stale
operator requests re-score

Staleness policy:

cold uncontacted lead: refresh after 30–60 days
contacted but no response: refresh before retargeting
high-value lead: refresh before each new campaign

Do not re-run AI daily on every lead. Use event-based refresh.

5.21 Batch vs real-time processing

Use real-time AI for:

inbound lead from social/ad
reply classification
operator-requested score
high-value lead review

Use batch AI for:

bulk Apify imports
overnight scoring
large dedupe review
source quality re-scoring
campaign preparation

This keeps cost and latency under control.

5.22 Lead Intelligence Layer APIs

Internal functions:

TypeScript
normalizeLeadCandidate(candidateId): Promise<BusinessNormalizerOutput>

classifyBusinessFit(leadId): Promise<BusinessFitOutput>

detectBusinessScale(leadId): Promise<BusinessScaleOutput>

detectNeed(leadId): Promise<NeedDetectorOutput>

analyzeContactability(leadId): Promise<ContactabilityOutput>

analyzeIntentSignals(leadId): Promise<IntentSignalOutput>

detectRisk(leadId): Promise<RiskDetectorOutput>

scoreLead(leadId): Promise<LeadScorerOutput>

decideHumanReview(leadId): Promise<HumanReviewOutput>

explainLeadIntelligence(leadId): Promise<IntelligenceExplainerOutput>

runFullLeadIntelligence(leadId): Promise<GrowthLeadIntelligence>

Main orchestrator:

TypeScript
runFullLeadIntelligence(leadId)
5.23 Orchestration flow
1. Load lead and source context.
2. Run deterministic hard filters.
3. Normalize business.
4. Classify fit.
5. Detect scale.
6. Analyze need.
7. Analyze contactability.
8. Analyze intent.
9. Detect risk.
10. Score lead.
11. Decide human review.
12. Generate explanation.
13. Update lead.
14. Create growth events.
15. Store aiRuns.

Pseudo-flow:

TypeScript
async function runFullLeadIntelligence(leadId: string) {
  const lead = await getGrowthLead(leadId);

  const hardFilter = runHardFilters(lead);
  if (hardFilter.reject) {
    return rejectLead(leadId, hardFilter.reason);
  }

  const fit = await classifyBusinessFit(leadId);
  const scale = await detectBusinessScale(leadId);
  const need = await detectNeed(leadId);
  const contactability = await analyzeContactability(leadId);
  const intent = await analyzeIntentSignals(leadId);
  const risk = await detectRisk(leadId);

  const score = await scoreLeadWithComponents({
    fit,
    scale,
    need,
    contactability,
    intent,
    risk,
  });

  const review = await decideHumanReview({
    score,
    fitConfidence: fit.confidence,
    needConfidence: need.confidence,
    contactConfidence: contactability.confidence,
    riskFlags: risk.flags,
    sourceRisk: lead.source.sourceQuality?.riskLevel ?? "medium",
  });

  const explanation = await explainLeadIntelligence({
    fit,
    need,
    contactability,
    intent,
    risk,
    score,
  });

  await updateLeadIntelligence(leadId, {
    fit,
    need,
    contactability,
    intent,
    risk,
    score,
    review,
    explanation,
  });

  return getGrowthLead(leadId);
}

5.25 Human review queue

If humanReviewRequired = true, lead enters:

/admin/growth/review

Review reasons:

unclear category
large chain
low confidence
bad source
channel risk
negative history
high-value manual review

Reviewer actions:

approve
reject
merge
suppress
enrich
hold
send to channel router

Every human decision creates:

growthEvent: human_override / human_review_completed

This becomes training/eval data later.

5.26 Lead Intelligence evals

Create eval datasets for each worker.

Business Fit Classifier eval

Dataset:

business name/category/source → correct category and fit

Metrics:

classification accuracy
false reject rate
false accept rate
Need Detector eval

Dataset:

website/menu/social signals → correct need score/primary need

Metrics:

need-score calibration
false high-need rate
false low-need rate
Contactability eval

Dataset:

contact identities → correct available/reachable channel classification

Metrics:

channel availability accuracy
invalid contact detection
Risk Detector eval

Dataset:

risky leads/suppressed/duplicates → correct risk action

Metrics:

risk recall
critical miss rate
false positive rate
Lead Scorer eval

Dataset:

historical leads → actual onboarding outcome

Metrics:

A-segment completion rate
B-segment completion rate
score vs conversion correlation

The most important long-term metric:

Do A leads complete onboarding at materially higher rate than B/C leads?

If not, scoring is bad.

5.27 How the layer improves over time

The Lead Intelligence Layer should learn from downstream outcomes.

Feedback signals:

message reply
flow link click
onboarding started
onboarding completed
converted
negative reply
DNC
bounce
wrong number
human override

Use these to improve:

fit classification
need scoring
contactability scoring
risk thresholds
segment thresholds
source quality weights

Example:

If “Instagram-only cafes” complete onboarding at high rate,
increase need score for similar leads.

Example:

If “cloud kitchens with no website” have high wrong-contact rate,
lower contactability/risk score for that segment.

This is how the system becomes intelligent.

5.28 Common failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Over-contacting low-fit leads

Cause:

fit classifier too loose
source too broad
score threshold too low

Fix:

raise fit threshold
improve source planner
add human review
Failure mode 2 — Rejecting good leads

Cause:

AI too conservative
weak source data
bad category mapping

Fix:

sample rejected leads weekly
run evals
adjust thresholds
Failure mode 3 — High reply but low onboarding

Cause:

need detector or message angle wrong
wrong onboarding flow routing
curiosity but no real intent

Fix:

optimize for onboarding completion, not reply
Failure mode 4 — High DNC/negative rate

Cause:

wrong source
wrong channel
message too aggressive
bad suppression

Fix:

pause segment
lower volume
review message
improve channel eligibility
Failure mode 5 — AI hallucinated reasoning

Cause:

freeform AI output
weak schemas
over-personalization

Fix:

structured outputs
banned claims
evidence-required need signals
human review below confidence threshold
5.29 Final AI Lead Intelligence contract

The AI Lead Intelligence Layer must produce this final contract for every lead:

TypeScript
type LeadIntelligenceContract = {
  leadId: string;

  fitScore: number;
  needScore: number;
  contactabilityScore: number;
  intentScore: number;
  riskScore: number;

  totalScore: number;

  segment: "A" | "B" | "C" | "REJECT";

  recommendedAction:
    | "contact"
    | "enrich"
    | "hold"
    | "human_review"
    | "reject"
    | "suppress";

  primaryNeed:
    | "menu_link_qr"
    | "instagram_bio_menu"
    | "whatsapp_menu_link"
    | "google_profile_menu_link"
    | "simple_setup"
    | "unknown"
    | "low_need";

  availableChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  riskFlags: {
    type: string;
    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
    reason: string;
  }[];

  humanReviewRequired: boolean;
  humanReviewReason?: string;

  explanation: string[];

  confidence: number;

  scoringVersion: string;
  generatedAt: Date;
};

This contract becomes the input for:

Channel Identity Registry
Channel Eligibility Engine
AI Channel Router
Promotion Campaign Builder
5.30 Final principle

The AI Lead Intelligence Layer exists to prevent the Growth Engine from becoming a dumb spam machine.

It should make the system answer:

Should this business be contacted at all?
Why?
What is the likely acquisition need?
How reachable are they?
What are the risks?
How much confidence do we have?
Should AI proceed or should a human review?

Only after this layer approves a lead should the system decide:

where to message
what to say
which flow to route to
````

````text
Spec 6 — Channel Identity Registry
6.1 Purpose

The Channel Identity Registry is the source of truth for how a lead can be contacted across:

email
WhatsApp
Instagram DM
Messenger
optional call/manual contact

It does not decide the final channel by itself. It stores the identities, verification state, confidence, source, policy state, and suppression state. The AI Channel Router later uses this registry to decide:

which channel to use
whether the channel is usable
whether the message should be auto-sent, assisted, template-based, reply-only, or blocked

The registry’s job:

Know where this lead exists.
Know whether that identity is usable.
Know how confident we are.
Know whether we are allowed to use it.
Know when we last used it.
Know whether it is suppressed.
6.2 Core principle

A lead is one business.

A lead may have many identities.

Example:

ABC Cafe
- email: hello@abccafe.com
- phone: +91...
- WhatsApp: +91...
- Instagram username: @abccafe.blr
- Instagram user ID from inbound DM
- Messenger PSID from Facebook Page message
- website domain: abccafe.com

These are not separate leads. They are separate channel identities attached to one growthLead.

6.3 What this registry owns

The registry owns:

contact identities
channel-specific IDs
identity status
identity source
identity confidence
verification state
suppression state
channel policy state
last inbound/outbound activity
identity-to-lead matching
identity dedupe keys

It does not own:

message content
conversation history
campaign strategy
template logic
channel routing decisions
onboarding flow logic
MenuList product state

Messages live in growthMessages.

Conversations live in growthConversations.

This registry only says:

This lead can potentially be reached here, with this confidence, under these constraints.
6.4 Why this matters

Without a Channel Identity Registry, omnichannel growth becomes messy fast.

The same business may appear as:

Google Maps phone
website email
Instagram DM
Messenger Page message
manual CSV row
Meta Lead Ad form

If these do not merge into one acquisition object, the system will:

duplicate leads
message the same business multiple times
ignore channel history
break suppression rules
misattribute conversions
make bad AI channel recommendations

The registry prevents this.

6.5 Primary collections

Use these collections:

growthLeadIdentities
growthIdentityDedupeKeys
growthChannelAccounts
growthIdentityVerificationEvents
growthSuppressions

The main collection is:

growthLeadIdentities/{identityId}

The lead document keeps only a compact summary for fast querying.

6.6 Identity types

Supported identity types:

TypeScript
type GrowthIdentityType =
  | "email"
  | "phone"
  | "whatsapp_phone"
  | "whatsapp_wa_id"
  | "instagram_username"
  | "instagram_user_id"
  | "messenger_psid"
  | "facebook_page"
  | "website_domain"
  | "source_url";

Important distinction:

phone ≠ WhatsApp identity
Instagram username ≠ Instagram messaging user ID
Facebook Page URL ≠ Messenger PSID
website domain ≠ email

A phone number may be WhatsApp-reachable, but that should be stored as a confidence signal, not assumed truth.

Instagram username found from public data is useful for matching, but the system should treat Instagram messaging as more reliable after an inbound DM/webhook identity exists. Meta’s Instagram Messaging API is built for Instagram Professional accounts, and Instagram webhooks can notify your app about messaging events.
Facebook Developers
+1

Messenger should use the Page-scoped ID, or PSID, for the person interacting with your Facebook Page. Meta’s Messenger docs refer to PSID as the Page-scoped ID used for Messenger user/profile interactions and message sending flows.
Facebook Developers
+1

For WhatsApp Cloud API, your own business sender identity is tied to a registered business phone number / phone-number ID; the message API uses the business Phone-Number-ID path for sending messages.
Facebook Developers
+1

  };

    | "unknown"
    | "valid"

    | "suppressed";

      | "apify"
      | "outscraper"

This object is the durable record for each known way to reach or identify the lead.

6.9 Identity statuses

Use two status levels:

identity status
channel status
Identity status

This describes whether the identity itself is valid.

TypeScript
type IdentityStatus =
  | "unknown"
  | "valid"
  | "invalid"
  | "active"
  | "inactive"
  | "bounced"
  | "wrong_contact"
  | "unsubscribed"
  | "suppressed";

Examples:

email bounced → bounced
phone wrong number → wrong_contact
Instagram username no longer exists → invalid
website domain loads → valid
DNC applied → suppressed
Channel identity status

This describes how usable the identity is for messaging.

TypeScript
type ChannelIdentityStatus =
  | "unknown"
  | "available"
  | "inbound_only"
  | "active_window"
  | "template_required"
  | "assisted_only"
  | "blocked"
  | "suppressed"
  | "invalid";

Examples:

WhatsApp phone exists but no opt-in → assisted_only / template_required
Instagram user sent DM recently → active_window
Messenger PSID exists from inbound → active_window or inbound_only
Email valid → available

You also need to store your own sending accounts.

Collection:

growthChannelAccounts/{accountId}

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthChannelAccount = {
  id: string;

  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  status:
    | "active"
    | "paused"

  };

  whatsapp?: {

  };

  };

Why this matters:

The lead identity tells us where the business can be reached.
The channel account tells us which MenuList account sends or receives the message.

Meta webhooks are used to receive real-time notifications for Messenger and Instagram messaging events, so the registry must know which Instagram Business account or Facebook Page generated the inbound identity.
Facebook Developers
+1

6.11 Identity confidence

Every identity should have a confidence score.

0.95–1.00 = directly verified
0.80–0.94 = strong source or delivered successfully
0.60–0.79 = plausible but not verified
0.40–0.59 = weak / needs confirmation
<0.40 = do not use without review

Examples:

Email delivered successfully → high confidence
Email scraped from business website contact page → medium-high confidence
Phone from source provider only → medium confidence
WhatsApp inbound message → high confidence
Instagram username from public source → medium confidence
Instagram user ID from webhook → high confidence
Messenger PSID from inbound webhook → high confidence

The AI Channel Router should prefer high-confidence identities.

6.12 Identity sources and trust ranking

Rank identity sources by trust.

Highest trust
inbound message
onboarding event
owner-submitted form
email reply
operator verified
Medium-high trust
business website contact page
Meta Lead Ad form submission
delivered email
delivered WhatsApp API message
Medium trust
Apify / maps provider phone
manual CSV
social profile link from website
Low trust
AI inference
old source data
unclear directory result
fuzzy matched social handle

Do not treat all contact data equally.

6.13 Identity normalization

Normalize identities before storage.

Email
TypeScript
normalizeEmail(" Hello@ABCcafe.com ") => "hello@abccafe.com"

Rules:

trim
lowercase
basic email validation
remove obvious display-name wrappers
Phone
TypeScript
normalizePhone("98765 43210", "IN") => "+919876543210"

Rules:

strip spaces / punctuation
convert valid Indian 10-digit mobile numbers to +91 format
reject too-short / too-long numbers
store raw and normalized
Website domain
TypeScript
normalizeDomain("https://www.abccafe.com/menu") => "abccafe.com"

Rules:

lowercase
remove protocol
remove www
remove path/query
Instagram username
TypeScript
normalizeInstagram("@ABC.Cafe ") => "abc.cafe"

Rules:

remove @
lowercase
strip URL wrapper
Messenger PSID
store exactly as received from Meta webhook/API

Do not attempt to infer PSID manually.

6.14 Identity dedupe keys

Use:

growthIdentityDedupeKeys/{keyHash}

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthIdentityDedupeKey = {
  id: string; // hash of key
  key: string;

  keyType:
    | "email"
    | "phone"
    | "domain"
    | "instagram_username"
    | "instagram_user_id"
    | "messenger_psid"
    | "facebook_page"
    | "source_url";

  identityId: string;
  leadId: string;

  confidence: number;

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};

Example keys:

email:hello@abccafe.com
phone:+919876543210
domain:abccafe.com
instagram_username:abccafe.blr
instagram_user_id:1784...
messenger_psid:123456...
source_url:hash(...)

Identity dedupe keys prevent:

same email creating multiple leads
same phone creating multiple leads
same Instagram inbound user creating a new duplicate lead
same Messenger PSID appearing as unrelated lead
6.15 Primary identity selection

A lead can have multiple identities per channel.

Example:

emails:
- hello@abccafe.com
- owner@abccafe.com
- booking@abccafe.com

phones:
- landline
- mobile
- WhatsApp number

Instagram:
- @abccafe
- @abccafe.koramangala

The system needs one primary identity per channel.

Selection logic:

1. Not suppressed
2. Valid/active
3. Highest confidence
4. Most recent inbound activity
5. Most recent successful outbound
6. Business-relevant identity type
7. Operator override

Example:

hello@abccafe.com delivered successfully > info@directory.com
WhatsApp inbound phone > phone scraped from source
Instagram user ID from DM > guessed username from source

Store primary identity IDs on the lead summary.

6.16 Identity merge logic

When a new identity arrives, the system must decide:

attach to existing lead
create new lead
send to human review
reject/suppress

Decision order:

1. Exact identity dedupe key match
2. Suppression key match
3. Strong business match
4. Fuzzy AI match
5. Human review
6. New lead
Auto-attach

Allowed when:

same email
same phone
same WhatsApp wa_id
same Instagram user ID
same Messenger PSID
same domain + same business name
Human review

Required when:

same business name but different area
same domain but possibly multi-location
same Instagram username but business name differs
same phone used by multiple branches
same owner contact across multiple businesses
Do not auto-merge
large chain branches
franchise branches
same brand name in different city/area
shared central phone
shared agency email
6.17 Channel policy metadata

The registry stores policy state, not final legal truth.

For each identity:

TypeScript
policy: {
  canUseForOutbound: boolean;

  sendMode:
    | "auto_send"
    | "assisted_send"
    | "template_required"
    | "reply_only"
    | "blocked"
    | "unknown";

  reasonIfBlocked?: string;

  optInStatus:
    | "unknown"
    | "not_required"
    | "required"
    | "confirmed"
    | "blocked";

  customerWindowExpiresAt?: Date;

  lastPolicyCheckedAt?: Date;
}

Examples:

email → auto_send if not unsubscribed/suppressed
WhatsApp cold lead → assisted_send or template_required
WhatsApp inbound within window → active_window
Instagram inbound within window → reply_only / active_window
Messenger inbound within window → reply_only / active_window
DNC → blocked

WhatsApp template messages are the message type used outside the customer-service window, so the registry must distinguish between active-window messaging and template-required messaging.
Facebook Developers

6.18 Activity tracking

Identity activity should be updated on every inbound/outbound event.

TypeScript
activity: {
  lastInboundAt?: Date;
  lastOutboundAt?: Date;
  lastUsedAt?: Date;
  lastClickedAt?: Date;
  lastFailedAt?: Date;
}

Use this to determine:

best active channel
follow-up channel
active conversation windows
identity freshness
identity decay

Example:

Lead has email and WhatsApp, but replied yesterday on Instagram.
Next action should probably continue Instagram if policy allows.

The identity registry enables that logic.

6.19 Identity verification events

Collection:

growthIdentityVerificationEvents/{eventId}

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthIdentityVerificationEvent = {
  id: string;

  identityId: string;
  leadId: string;

  type:
    | "format_validated"
    | "email_sent"
    | "email_delivered"

    | "email_unsubscribed"

    | "instagram_replied"
    | "messenger_replied"
    | "operator_verified"

This gives you a history of why an identity is trusted or blocked.

6.20 Suppression integration

Every identity must check suppression.

Suppression keys:

lead:{leadId}
email:{normalizedEmail}
phone:{e164}
domain:{normalizedDomain}
instagram_user_id:{id}
instagram_username:{username}
messenger_psid:{psid}
business_name_area:{normalizedName}:{area}:{city}

Suppression effects:

email unsubscribe → block email identity
wrong number → block phone / WhatsApp identity
DNC → suppress all identities for the lead
complaint → global suppression
converted → suppress acquisition outreach

Default rule:

DNC on one channel suppresses acquisition contact across all channels.
6.21 Identity lifecycle

Identity lifecycle:

discovered
→ normalized
→ deduped
→ attached to lead
→ confidence scored
→ policy checked
→ primary candidate selected
→ used or held
→ verified / failed / suppressed
→ refreshed or retired

Statuses:

unknown
valid
active
invalid
wrong_contact
suppressed

Retirement rules:

bounced email → stop email
wrong WhatsApp number → stop phone/WhatsApp
Instagram username changed → mark inactive
lead converted → suppress acquisition contact
DNC → global suppression
6.22 Identity freshness

Identities decay over time.

Suggested freshness windows:

email: recheck after bounce or 180 days unused
phone: recheck if wrong-number risk or 180 days unused
website/domain: refresh every 90–180 days
Instagram username: refresh if profile lookup fails or 90 days unused
Messenger PSID: remains usable only within platform policy and conversation context
WhatsApp active window: expires by policy window

Store:

TypeScript
freshness: {
  lastConfirmedAt?: Date;
  staleAfter?: Date;
  freshnessStatus: "fresh" | "aging" | "stale" | "unknown";
}

This helps avoid old bad outreach.

6.23 Channel account matching

For inbound messages, the system must know which MenuList account received the message.

Examples:

WhatsApp Business phone number ID
Instagram Business account ID
Facebook Page ID
email inbox address

Inbound flow:

provider webhook received
→ identify channel account
→ extract sender identity
→ match sender identity to lead
→ create/update conversation
→ update identity registry
→ send to reply classifier

This matters because the same sender identity may behave differently across accounts/pages.

6.24 Matching inbound messages to leads

Matching priority:

1. exact channel identity match
2. exact phone/email/domain match
3. explicit tracking code or flow link
4. source/campaign tracking params
5. business name mentioned in message
6. username/profile similarity
7. AI fuzzy match
8. human review
9. create new lead

For Instagram/Messenger inbound, exact user ID / PSID should dominate. For email, normalized email dominates. For WhatsApp, phone/wa_id dominates.

6.25 Identity conflict handling

Conflicts happen.

Examples:

same phone appears on two businesses
same email used by multiple branches
same Instagram account represents a group
same Facebook Page manages multiple locations
website domain belongs to chain

Conflict object:

TypeScript
type IdentityConflict = {
  identityId: string;

  conflictType:
    | "identity_linked_to_multiple_leads"
    | "shared_branch_contact"
    | "chain_contact"
    | "agency_contact"
    | "possible_wrong_match";

  involvedLeadIds: string[];

  recommendedAction:
    | "keep_shared"
    | "split"
    | "merge"
    | "human_review"
    | "suppress_identity";

  confidence: number;

  createdAt: Date;
};

Default:

Do not auto-merge when one identity may represent multiple branches.
Send to review.
6.26 Dashboard display

On the lead page, show an identity panel.

Channel identities

Email:
hello@abccafe.com
Status: valid
Confidence: 0.82
Source: website crawl
Last used: never
Suppression: no

WhatsApp:
+91...
Status: assisted/template required
Confidence: 0.78
Source: Apify
Last inbound: none

@abccafe
Status: known
Confidence: 0.65
Source: website

Messenger:
none

Actions:

mark primary
mark invalid

refresh

remove identity

The operator should know immediately which channels are real and usable.

6.27 Work queue support

The registry should support queues like:

A leads with usable WhatsApp identity
A leads with valid email
Inbound Instagram leads without matched business
Messenger conversations needing lead match
Leads with identity conflict
Leads with no contact path but high fit
Suppressed identities
Bounced emails
Wrong numbers

Required indexes should support these queues.

6.28 Suggested indexes

For Firestore-style storage, prepare indexes around matching and queues.

Firestore stores data in documents organized into collections and is optimized for large collections of small documents, so this identity registry should keep each identity as its own small document rather than embedding unlimited identities inside a lead document.
Firebase

Recommended indexes:

growthLeadIdentities:
- leadId ASC, type ASC
- valueHash ASC
- type ASC, status ASC
- channel ASC, status ASC
- channel ASC, policy.sendMode ASC
- suppression.isSuppressed ASC, channel ASC
- activity.lastInboundAt DESC
- activity.lastOutboundAt DESC

growthIdentityDedupeKeys:
- keyHash as document ID
- leadId ASC

growthIdentityVerificationEvents:
- identityId ASC, occurredAt DESC
- leadId ASC, occurredAt DESC

Firestore supports indexing and composite indexes for queried fields, so indexes should be created only for actual dashboard and matching queries.
Firebase

6.29 Identity quality score

Each identity should get a quality score.

Identity Quality Score =
  source trust
+ format validity
+ verification history
+ recent successful activity
+ direct inbound evidence
- bounce/failure history
- age/staleness
- suppression risk

Example:

WhatsApp inbound yesterday → 95
Email from website crawl, not yet sent → 75
Phone from maps source only → 60
Instagram username from old CSV → 45
Bounced email → 0
DNC identity → blocked

This score becomes input for the Channel Router.

6.30 Primary channel signal

The identity registry should not choose the final outreach channel, but it can expose a signal:

TypeScript
type IdentityChannelSignal = {
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";

  availability: "available" | "possible" | "inbound_only" | "blocked" | "unknown";

  qualityScore: number;

  policySendMode:
    | "auto_send"
    | "assisted_send"
    | "template_required"
    | "reply_only"
    | "blocked"
    | "unknown";

  reason: string;
};

The Channel Router consumes this.

Example:

JSON
{
  "channel": "whatsapp",
  "availability": "possible",
  "qualityScore": 78,
  "policySendMode": "assisted_send",
  "reason": "Phone available and likely WhatsApp-reachable, but no inbound/opt-in evidence."
}
6.31 Error cases to handle
Same identity, multiple leads

Do not duplicate outreach. Create conflict and route to review.

Identity suppressed but lead not suppressed

Block only that identity/channel unless suppression reason is DNC/complaint.

Inbound message from unknown identity

Create new lead or unmatched conversation, then AI/human match.

Instagram username known but no user ID

Can use for research/matching, but not as strong messaging identity.

Messenger PSID exists but no business name

Create conversation and ask clarifying question or use AI to infer from profile/message.

Email bounced

Mark email identity bounced, leave other channels eligible.

Wrong WhatsApp number

Suppress phone/WhatsApp identity; do not suppress entire lead unless confirmed.

6.32 Final Channel Identity Registry contract

Every lead should expose this final contract to the Channel Router:

TypeScript
type ChannelIdentityContract = {
  leadId: string;

  identities: {
    channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";
    identityId: string;
    displayValue: string;
    status: string;
    qualityScore: number;
    confidence: number;

    policy: {
      sendMode:
        | "auto_send"
        | "assisted_send"
        | "template_required"
        | "reply_only"
        | "blocked"
        | "unknown";

      canUseForOutbound: boolean;
      reasonIfBlocked?: string;
      customerWindowExpiresAt?: Date;
    };

    lastInboundAt?: Date;
    lastOutboundAt?: Date;
    isSuppressed: boolean;
    sourceProvider: string;
  }[];

  primaryByChannel: {
    email?: string;
    whatsapp?: string;
    instagram?: string;
    messenger?: string;
    call?: string;
  };

  conflicts: {
    type: string;
    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high";
    requiresHumanReview: boolean;
  }[];

  bestAvailableChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  generatedAt: Date;
};

This is the exact handoff to:

Channel Eligibility Engine
AI Channel Router
Next-Best-Action Engine
Unified Inbox
6.33 Final principle

The Channel Identity Registry is what prevents omnichannel growth from becoming chaotic.

It gives the system one disciplined answer to:

Where does this lead exist?
How confident are we?
Can we use this identity?
What happened last time?
Is it blocked?
Which identity is primary?
Does this identity create a duplicate or conflict?

Without this layer, AI channel routing will be unreliable.

With this layer, the Growth Engine can intelligently decide:

email this lead
prepare WhatsApp
reply on Instagram
continue Messenger
hold for enrichment
suppress completely
````

````text
Spec 7 — Channel Eligibility and Policy Engine
7.1 Purpose

The Channel Eligibility and Policy Engine is the hard gate before any outreach happens.

It answers:

Can we message this lead on this channel right now?
If yes, how?
If no, why not?
What must happen before we can message?

It does not choose the best channel. That is the AI Channel Router’s job.

It does not write the message. That is the Message Generator’s job.

It decides whether a proposed channel action is allowed, blocked, assisted, template-required, reply-only, or needs human review.

Core principle:

AI recommends.
Eligibility engine permits or blocks.

AI must never bypass this layer.

7.2 Why this layer is necessary

Once the system integrates:

email
WhatsApp
Instagram DM
Messenger

the same outreach logic cannot apply to every channel.

Email can be used for controlled cold outreach with unsubscribe, bounce, and sender-domain controls.

WhatsApp has stricter commercial messaging rules, template requirements, and quality/account risk.

Instagram and Messenger are strongest for inbound/warm conversations and must respect response-window constraints.

India also has an active regulatory framework around unsolicited commercial communication through TRAI’s TCCCPR structure, with the 2026 third-amendment consultation explicitly focused on making the commercial-communication framework more effective against UCC.
Press Information Bureau
+1

So the Growth Engine needs a deterministic policy layer, not only AI judgment.

7.3 Position in the system

The flow should be:

Lead Intelligence Layer
→ Channel Identity Registry
→ Channel Eligibility Engine
→ AI Channel Router
→ Message Generator
→ Channel Execution Layer

The Channel Eligibility Engine consumes:

lead state
channel identities
suppression records
conversation windows
template status
channel account health
campaign caps
daily caps
previous interactions

It outputs:

eligible channels
blocked channels
send mode per channel
policy reason
human-review requirement
7.4 Core output

For each lead and channel, output this:

TypeScript
type ChannelEligibilityResult = {
  leadId: string;

  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";

  eligible: boolean;

  sendMode:
    | "auto_send"
    | "assisted_send"
    | "template_required"
    | "reply_only"
    | "human_review"
    | "hold"
    | "blocked";

  reason:
    | "eligible_email"
    | "eligible_assisted_whatsapp"
    | "eligible_whatsapp_template"
    | "eligible_active_conversation_window"
    | "eligible_reply_only"
    | "suppressed"
    | "do_not_contact"
    | "unsubscribed"
    | "invalid_identity"
    | "missing_identity"
    | "channel_window_expired"
    | "template_not_approved"
    | "daily_cap_reached"
    | "campaign_cap_reached"
    | "channel_account_unhealthy"
    | "policy_risk"
    | "human_review_required"
    | "unknown";

  blockers: {
    type:
      | "suppression"
      | "missing_identity"
      | "invalid_identity"
      | "policy"
      | "template"
      | "rate_limit"
      | "account_health"
      | "campaign_rule"
      | "human_review";

    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
    message: string;
  }[];

  requirements: {
    type:
      | "needs_template"
      | "needs_human_approval"
      | "needs_opt_in"
      | "needs_active_window"
      | "needs_valid_identity"
      | "needs_unsubscribe_footer"
      | "needs_suppression_check"
      | "needs_sender_health_check";

    message: string;
  }[];

  confidence: number;

  checkedAt: Date;
};

The Channel Router should only choose among channels where eligible = true or sendMode is actionable.

7.5 Send modes

Use these send modes consistently.

auto_send

The system can send automatically.

Use for:

email outreach
email follow-ups
low-risk reply emails
some approved-template sends later

Only if:

suppression passes
identity is valid
daily/campaign caps pass
message template is approved internally
channel account is healthy
assisted_send

The system prepares the message, but a human/operator sends or approves it.

Use for:

cold WhatsApp outreach
high-value leads
medium-risk leads
uncertain identities
first-time campaigns
sensitive replies

This should be the default for WhatsApp cold acquisition until you have clear compliant template flows and channel-quality confidence.

template_required

The channel can be used only through an approved template.

Use for:

WhatsApp Business Platform outbound outside active customer window

WhatsApp template messages are WhatsApp Business Account assets used for template messages via the Cloud API or Marketing Messages API, and template messaging is the correct structure for business-initiated WhatsApp messages outside the customer-service window.
Facebook Developers
+1

reply_only

The system can reply only because the lead initiated the conversation.

Use for:

Instagram inbound DM
Messenger inbound message
WhatsApp active customer window

Meta’s Messenger Platform and Instagram Messaging policy states that businesses generally have up to 24 hours to respond to a user, and Instagram Messaging API is intended for Instagram Professional accounts at scale.
Facebook Developers
+1

human_review

The system is not confident enough.

Use when:

identity conflict
possible duplicate
unclear suppression
policy ambiguity
high-risk campaign
angry/negative reply
large-chain/corporate business
hold

No outreach now, but the lead may be usable later.

Use when:

lead needs enrichment
channel missing
low score
waiting for active window
cooldown active
blocked

No outreach allowed.

Use when:

do-not-contact
global suppression
unsubscribed email
wrong number
invalid identity
channel account restricted
template rejected
campaign stopped
7.6 Eligibility decision order

The engine must run checks in this order.

1. Global suppression
2. Lead status
3. Identity availability
4. Identity validity
5. Channel-specific policy
6. Conversation-window state
7. Template status
8. Campaign/channel caps
9. Channel account health
10. Human-review triggers
11. Final send mode

This order matters.

Example:

If lead is do_not_contact, do not check whether WhatsApp template exists.
Suppression wins.
7.7 Hard blockers

These block all outbound unless an admin explicitly overrides.

global do_not_contact
complaint history
manual block
converted business suppressed from acquisition
duplicate of suppressed lead
known wrong contact
known invalid identity
channel account disabled/restricted

These should return:

TypeScript
eligible: false
sendMode: "blocked"

AI must not override these.

7.8 Lead-level status rules

Eligibility depends on lead status.

TypeScript
type LeadEligibilityStatusRule = {
  status: GrowthLeadStatus;
  outboundAllowed: boolean;
  reason?: string;
};

Recommended:

Lead status	Outbound allowed?	Notes
raw_imported	No	Not qualified yet
normalized	No	Needs intelligence/scoring
duplicate	No	Must merge/reject
rejected	No	No outreach
suppressed	No	No outreach
qualified	Maybe	Needs channel routing
ready_to_contact	Yes	If channel eligible
contacted	Follow-up only	Respect caps/windows
engaged	Yes	Prefer same active channel
interested	Yes	Route to onboarding
routed_to_onboarding	Retarget only	If not started/completed
onboarding_started	Help/retarget only	Product-flow dependent
onboarding_completed	No acquisition outreach	Suppress promos unless lifecycle rules
converted	No acquisition outreach	Move out of growth acquisition
not_interested	Usually no	Cooldown or suppress
do_not_contact	No	Global block
7.9 Email eligibility

Email is the most automation-friendly outbound channel.

Eligible if:

lead has valid email identity
email not bounced
email not unsubscribed
email not suppressed
lead not DNC
campaign email cap not reached
sender domain/account healthy
message includes required unsubscribe/identity footer
template is internally approved

Email should return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "auto_send"

or:

TypeScript
sendMode: "human_review"

if risk is elevated.

For commercial email, the FTC’s CAN-SPAM guide states that the law covers commercial messages, including B2B email, gives recipients the right to stop future emails, and requires commercial senders to comply with requirements for accurate headers, non-deceptive subject lines, identification, and opt-out handling.
Federal Trade Commission

Email blocked cases
unsubscribed
bounced repeatedly
invalid format
complaint
suppressed domain
daily cap reached
sender account paused
missing unsubscribe handling
Email eligibility result example
JSON
{
  "channel": "email",
  "eligible": true,
  "sendMode": "auto_send",
  "reason": "eligible_email",
  "blockers": [],
  "requirements": [
    {
      "type": "needs_unsubscribe_footer",
      "message": "Commercial email must include opt-out handling."
    }
  ],
  "confidence": 0.93
}
7.10 WhatsApp eligibility

WhatsApp should be treated as high-value but higher-risk.

The system should support two WhatsApp modes:

assisted WhatsApp
WhatsApp Business Platform API
Assisted WhatsApp

Use when:

phone exists
lead is A/B quality
not suppressed
not wrong number
operator approval is acceptable
campaign cap available

Return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "assisted_send"

This means:

AI drafts message
operator opens WhatsApp / approves
operator manually sends or confirms send
system logs it
WhatsApp API/template

Use when:

approved template exists
business/account is healthy
identity is valid
policy requirements pass
campaign cap available

Return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "template_required"

or later:

TypeScript
sendMode: "auto_send"

only for approved, policy-safe, template-based use.

WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy governs use of WhatsApp Business Services and says violations may result in limits or removal of access; this makes account-quality protection a product requirement, not an afterthought.
WhatsApp for Business

WhatsApp active conversation window

If the lead has recently messaged MenuList on WhatsApp, the system may be able to reply inside the customer-service window.

Return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "reply_only"

or:

TypeScript
sendMode: "auto_send"

only if the response is allowed by policy and campaign rules.

WhatsApp blocked cases
phone invalid
wrong number
DNC
global suppression
template rejected/not approved
account quality unhealthy
outside active window and no approved template
daily WhatsApp cap reached
campaign cap reached
WhatsApp eligibility example
JSON
{
  "channel": "whatsapp",
  "eligible": true,
  "sendMode": "assisted_send",
  "reason": "eligible_assisted_whatsapp",
  "blockers": [],
  "requirements": [
    {
      "type": "needs_human_approval",
      "message": "Cold WhatsApp outreach should be assisted unless an approved template and eligibility rule apply."
    }
  ],
  "confidence": 0.82
}
7.11 Instagram DM eligibility

Instagram should mostly be a warm/inbound channel.

Eligible if:

Instagram identity exists
conversation was initiated by the user/business
active response window exists
not suppressed
message is a reply or allowed campaign response
connected Instagram Professional account is healthy

Return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "reply_only"

or:

TypeScript
sendMode: "human_review"

for ambiguous cases.

Do not make cold Instagram DM blasting the default. The Instagram Messaging API supports messaging solutions for Instagram Professional accounts at scale, but the safer growth posture is to treat it as inbound/warm unless a specific compliant campaign mechanism is in place.
Facebook Developers
+1

Instagram blocked cases
no user ID / no usable conversation identity
outside response window
suppressed user
invalid username
not connected to MenuList Instagram Professional account
account restricted
mass-cold-DM campaign attempt
Instagram eligibility example
JSON
{
  "channel": "instagram",
  "eligible": true,
  "sendMode": "reply_only",
  "reason": "eligible_active_conversation_window",
  "blockers": [],
  "requirements": [],
  "confidence": 0.91
}
7.12 Messenger eligibility

Messenger should be treated similarly to Instagram: strong for inbound, Page, and ad-driven conversations.

Eligible if:

Messenger PSID/thread exists
lead initiated conversation or is inside response window
not suppressed
Page account is connected and healthy
message is a reply or allowed flow

Return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "reply_only"

or:

TypeScript
sendMode: "human_review"

for ambiguous cases.

Meta’s Messenger/IG messaging policy uses a standard 24-hour response window for businesses to respond to users, so the Growth Engine must track customerWindowExpiresAt for Messenger conversations.
Facebook Developers

Messenger blocked cases
no PSID/thread
outside response window
suppressed user
Page account disconnected
account restricted
cold outbound attempt without permitted context
Messenger eligibility example
JSON
{
  "channel": "messenger",
  "eligible": false,
  "sendMode": "blocked",
  "reason": "channel_window_expired",
  "blockers": [
    {
      "type": "policy",
      "severity": "high",
      "message": "Messenger conversation window expired; wait for user interaction or use another eligible channel."
    }
  ],
  "requirements": [
    {
      "type": "needs_active_window",
      "message": "User must re-engage before Messenger reply is allowed."
    }
  ],
  "confidence": 0.95
}
7.13 Call/manual contact eligibility

Optional, but useful for high-value leads.

Eligible if:

valid phone exists
not DNC
not wrong number
lead is high score
operator assigned
daily manual-call cap available

Return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "assisted_send"

Meaning:

AI prepares talking points
human calls
human logs outcome

Calls should remain manual/high-value, not automated robocalls.

7.14 Channel eligibility matrix
Channel	Cold outbound	Warm/inbound reply	Default send mode	Main blocker
Email	Yes	Yes	auto_send	unsubscribe/bounce/suppression
WhatsApp	Limited/controlled	Yes	assisted_send or template_required	template/policy/account quality
Instagram DM	Not default	Yes	reply_only	no active window / no inbound
Messenger	Not default	Yes	reply_only	no active window / no PSID
Call	Manual only	Manual only	assisted_send	DNC/wrong number
7.15 Policy state stored on conversation

For every conversation, store:

TypeScript
type ConversationPolicyState = {
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  canSendNow: boolean;

  sendMode:
    | "auto_send"
    | "assisted_send"
    | "template_required"
    | "reply_only"
    | "human_review"
    | "blocked";

  customerWindowExpiresAt?: Date;

  requiresTemplate?: boolean;
  allowedTemplateIds?: string[];

  reasonIfBlocked?: string;

  lastCheckedAt: Date;
};

This prevents the system from recalculating everything from scratch on every UI render.

But before actual sending, eligibility must be recalculated.

7.16 Template eligibility

For template-based channels, the engine must check template status.

Use:

TypeScript
type ChannelTemplateEligibility = {
  templateId: string;
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  status:
    | "draft"
    | "internal_approved"
    | "provider_submitted"
    | "provider_approved"
    | "provider_rejected"
    | "paused"
    | "disabled";

  category?: "marketing" | "utility" | "authentication" | "service" | "reply";

  canUse: boolean;
  reasonIfBlocked?: string;

  version: number;
};

For WhatsApp API sends, require:

provider_approved

For email, require:

internal_approved

For Instagram/Messenger replies, templates are internal reply patterns, not necessarily provider-approved templates, but policy window still matters.

7.17 Campaign caps

The eligibility engine must check campaign-level caps.

TypeScript
type CampaignCapState = {
  campaignId: string;

  maxTotalContactsPerDay: number;
  maxEmailPerDay: number;
  maxWhatsAppPerDay: number;
  maxInstagramRepliesPerDay: number;
  maxMessengerRepliesPerDay: number;

  sentToday: {
    total: number;
    email: number;
    whatsapp: number;
    instagram: number;
    messenger: number;
  };

  negativeRateToday?: number;
  dncRateToday?: number;
  bounceRateToday?: number;

  paused: boolean;
  pauseReason?: string;
};

Eligibility should return blocked if caps are exceeded.

Example blocker:

JSON
{
  "type": "rate_limit",
  "severity": "medium",
  "message": "Campaign WhatsApp daily cap reached."
}
7.18 Channel account health

The engine must check account health.

TypeScript
type ChannelAccountHealth = {
  accountId: string;
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  status:
    | "healthy"
    | "warning"
    | "restricted"
    | "disabled"
    | "unknown";

  metrics?: {
    bounceRate?: number;
    complaintRate?: number;
    unsubscribeRate?: number;
    negativeReplyRate?: number;
    deliveryFailureRate?: number;
    qualityRating?: "green" | "yellow" | "red" | "unknown";
  };

  canSend: boolean;
  reasonIfBlocked?: string;
};

Examples:

email bounce spike → reduce or block email sends
WhatsApp quality warning → pause API sends
Instagram restricted → block replies/sends
Messenger webhook disconnected → block Messenger actions

This prevents growth from damaging the channels.

7.19 Suppression rules

Suppression must be checked before channel eligibility.

Suppression keys:

lead
phone
email
domain
instagram_user_id
instagram_username
messenger_psid
business_name_area
campaign

Suppression scopes:

global
campaign
channel
identity

Default effects:

Suppression reason	Scope	Effect
do_not_contact	global	block all outreach
complaint	global	block all outreach
unsubscribe	email	block email
wrong_number	phone/WhatsApp	block phone + WhatsApp
invalid_email	email	block email
not_interested	campaign/cooldown	block or delay
converted	acquisition	stop acquisition outreach
manual_block	configured	as set by admin

Result:

TypeScript
sendMode: "blocked"
reason: "suppressed"
7.20 Cooldown rules

Not all “no” responses are permanent.

Use cooldowns.

TypeScript
type CooldownRule = {
  reason: "not_interested" | "no_reply" | "low_intent" | "campaign_pause";
  durationDays: number;
  scope: "lead" | "channel" | "campaign";
};

Recommended:

not_interested → 60–90 day cooldown or global suppression depending tone
no reply after max follow-ups → 30–60 day cooldown
clicked but did not start → shorter retargeting window
DNC/complaint → permanent global suppression

Eligibility should return:

TypeScript
sendMode: "hold"
reason: "policy_risk" or "human_review_required"

when cooldown is active.

7.21 Active conversation windows

For WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger, store:

TypeScript
customerWindowExpiresAt: Date

Update when:

user sends inbound message
allowed event resets window
platform webhook indicates inbound interaction

Eligibility logic:

TypeScript
if (now < customerWindowExpiresAt) {
  sendMode = "reply_only" or "auto_send";
} else {
  sendMode = "template_required" or "blocked";
}

Exact platform-specific rules should be kept in channel adapters, not hardcoded everywhere.

7.22 Channel adapter interface

Each channel should implement a policy adapter.

TypeScript
type ChannelPolicyAdapter = {
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";

  evaluate(input: ChannelEligibilityInput): Promise<ChannelEligibilityResult>;

  getAccountHealth(accountId: string): Promise<ChannelAccountHealth>;

  validateTemplate?(templateId: string): Promise<ChannelTemplateEligibility>;

  getWindowState?(conversationId: string): Promise<ConversationPolicyState>;
};

Adapters:

EmailPolicyAdapter
WhatsAppPolicyAdapter
InstagramPolicyAdapter
MessengerPolicyAdapter
CallPolicyAdapter

This keeps the system extensible.

7.23 Main eligibility API

Use one main function:

TypeScript
async function evaluateLeadChannelEligibility(
  input: ChannelEligibilityInput
): Promise<LeadChannelEligibilitySummary>

Input:

TypeScript
type ChannelEligibilityInput = {
  leadId: string;

  requestedChannels?: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  campaignId?: string;
  templateId?: string;
  conversationId?: string;

  action:
    | "cold_outbound"
    | "follow_up"
    | "reply"
    | "send_onboarding_link"
    | "retarget"
    | "manual_contact";

  now: Date;
};

Output:

TypeScript
type LeadChannelEligibilitySummary = {
  leadId: string;

  results: ChannelEligibilityResult[];

  eligibleChannels: {
    channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";
    sendMode: ChannelEligibilityResult["sendMode"];
    scoreModifier?: number;
  }[];

  blockedChannels: {
    channel: string;
    reason: string;
    blockers: ChannelEligibilityResult["blockers"];
  }[];

  globalBlock?: {
    blocked: boolean;
    reason?: string;
  };

  recommendedSafeChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  generatedAt: Date;
};

The AI Channel Router consumes this object.

Example 1 — A lead with valid email and phone
JSON
{

Example 3 — DNC lead
JSON
````
