````text
7.25 Integration with AI Channel Router

The Channel Router receives only eligible possibilities.

Input to router:

TypeScript
type ChannelRouterInput = {
  leadId: string;
  leadIntelligence: LeadIntelligenceContract;
  identityContract: ChannelIdentityContract;
  eligibility: LeadChannelEligibilitySummary;
  campaignContext?: GrowthCampaignContext;
};

The router must not select a blocked channel.

Rule:

TypeScript
if (!eligibility.recommendedSafeChannels.includes(channel)) {
  throw new Error("Channel not eligible");
}

This should be enforced in code.

7.26 Integration with Message Generator

The Message Generator should receive eligibility constraints.

Example:

TypeScript
type MessageGenerationConstraints = {
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";
  sendMode: "auto_send" | "assisted_send" | "template_required" | "reply_only";

  bannedClaims: string[];
  requiredFooter?: string;
  maxLength?: number;
  templateId?: string;
  providerTemplateRequired?: boolean;
};

Examples:

Email → include unsubscribe footer
WhatsApp template → use approved template variables only
Instagram reply → keep within reply context
Messenger reply → keep within active conversation context
7.27 Integration with Channel Execution Layer

Before sending, run eligibility again.

Sequence:

1. Channel Router recommends channel.
2. Message Generator drafts message.
3. Human/system queues send.
4. Before actual send, Eligibility Engine re-checks.
5. If still eligible, Channel Execution Layer sends/prepares.
6. If no longer eligible, block and update task.

This prevents race conditions like:

lead got suppressed after message was drafted
daily cap got reached
conversation window expired
template got paused
email bounced in meantime
7.28 Promotion campaign eligibility

For promotion campaigns, eligibility runs at two levels.

Campaign-level eligibility

Before campaign starts:

Are selected channels healthy?
Are templates approved?
Are send caps configured?
Is suppression active?
Are stop rules configured?
Lead-level eligibility

Before each message:

Can this lead receive this message now?

Promotion campaign cannot run if campaign-level eligibility fails.

Example:

WhatsApp promotion campaign blocked because required template is not provider-approved.
7.29 Stop rules

Eligibility must support automatic campaign pauses.

Pause campaign if:

negative response rate exceeds threshold
DNC rate exceeds threshold
email bounce rate exceeds threshold
WhatsApp account health warning appears
template paused/rejected
Instagram/Messenger webhook disconnected
delivery failure rate spikes
complaint detected

When paused:

TypeScript
sendMode: "blocked"
reason: "campaign_cap_reached" or "channel_account_unhealthy"

depending on cause.

7.30 Dashboard output

In the lead dashboard, show a channel eligibility panel.

Example:

Channel Eligibility

Email
Status: Eligible
Mode: Auto-send
Reason: Valid email, no suppression, email cap available.

WhatsApp
Status: Eligible
Mode: Assisted send
Reason: Phone exists, no suppression, no active opt-in/template route.

Instagram
Status: Blocked
Reason: No inbound conversation / no usable user ID.

Messenger
Status: Blocked
Reason: No Messenger identity.

For each blocker, show:

what blocks it
how to unblock it
whether human override exists

Example:

WhatsApp API blocked:
Template not approved.
Action: submit/approve template or use assisted send.
7.31 Admin controls

Admin should be able to configure:

daily caps by channel
campaign caps
negative-rate pause threshold
DNC behavior
not-interested cooldown
email sender account
WhatsApp template rules
Instagram/Messenger reply policy
autonomy level per channel
human approval thresholds

Example config:

TypeScript
type ChannelEligibilityConfig = {
  email: {
    autoSendEnabled: boolean;
    maxDailySends: number;
    requireUnsubscribeFooter: boolean;
    blockOnBounce: boolean;
  };

  whatsapp: {
    assistedSendEnabled: boolean;
    apiSendEnabled: boolean;
    maxDailySends: number;
    requireApprovedTemplateForColdApi: boolean;
    blockOnQualityWarning: boolean;
  };

  instagram: {
    replyOnlyByDefault: boolean;
    maxDailyReplies: number;
    requireActiveWindow: boolean;
  };

  messenger: {
    replyOnlyByDefault: boolean;
    maxDailyReplies: number;
    requireActiveWindow: boolean;
  };

  suppression: {
    globalDncBlocksAllChannels: boolean;
    notInterestedCooldownDays: number;
    convertedSuppressesAcquisition: boolean;
  };
};
7.32 Human override policy

Human override should be limited.

Allowed override:

hold → assisted_send
human_review → assisted_send
template_required → assisted_send, if using manual channel

Not allowed override without admin:

do_not_contact
complaint
unsubscribe for email
wrong number
global suppression
channel account disabled
template rejected for API send

Human overrides must create an event:

TypeScript
type HumanOverrideEvent = {
  leadId: string;
  channel: string;
  originalSendMode: string;
  overriddenSendMode: string;
  reason: string;
  operatorId: string;
  occurredAt: Date;
};

This prevents silent policy drift.

7.33 Events created by this engine

Create events:

channel_eligibility_checked
channel_blocked
channel_eligible
send_mode_assigned
campaign_paused_by_policy
human_override_required
human_override_applied
suppression_blocked_send
template_blocked_send
cap_blocked_send

Example:

TypeScript
type ChannelEligibilityEvent = {
  id: string;
  leadId: string;
  campaignId?: string;
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";
  result: "eligible" | "blocked" | "human_review" | "hold";
  sendMode: string;
  reason: string;
  blockers?: ChannelEligibilityResult["blockers"];
  createdAt: Date;
};

These events feed analytics and audits.

7.34 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — AI selects blocked channel

Fix:

Router cannot select outside eligibility.recommendedSafeChannels.
Failure mode 2 — Message drafted but send later becomes invalid

Fix:

Re-check eligibility immediately before execution.
Failure mode 3 — WhatsApp overuse creates account risk

Fix:

assisted send default
daily caps
quality-health checks
template requirements
negative-rate pause rules
Failure mode 4 — Instagram/Messenger used as cold channels

Fix:

reply_only default
active-window requirement
manual approval for exceptions
Failure mode 5 — Email domain gets damaged

Fix:

bounce thresholds
complaint thresholds
unsubscribe handling
domain health check
daily ramp controls
Failure mode 6 — DNC not respected cross-channel

Fix:

global suppression checked before all channel evaluation.
7.35 Final eligibility contract

The Channel Eligibility and Policy Engine must produce this final contract:

TypeScript
type EligibilityContract = {
  leadId: string;

  globalAllowed: boolean;
  globalBlockReason?: string;

  channelResults: {
    channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";
    eligible: boolean;
    sendMode:
      | "auto_send"
      | "assisted_send"
      | "template_required"
      | "reply_only"
      | "human_review"
      | "hold"
      | "blocked";

    reason: string;

    blockers: {
      type: string;
      severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
      message: string;
    }[];

    requirements: {
      type: string;
      message: string;
    }[];

    expiresAt?: Date;
    checkedAt: Date;
  }[];

  eligibleChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  safeForAutoSend: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger")[];

  requiresHumanApproval: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  blockedChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  generatedAt: Date;
};

This contract becomes mandatory input to:

AI Channel Router
Message Generator
Channel Execution Layer
Promotion Campaign Builder
Next-Best-Action Engine
7.36 Final principle

The Channel Eligibility Engine is the safety and permission layer of the Growth Engine.

It exists so the system can be aggressive in intelligence but disciplined in execution.

The correct behavior is:

AI can be ambitious in finding and recommending.
Policy engine must be conservative in allowing outbound.

This gives MenuList the advantage of AI-led omnichannel growth without turning the system into a spam engine or channel-risk machine.
````

````text
Spec 8 — AI Channel Router
8.1 Purpose

The AI Channel Router decides the best outreach path for each lead.

It answers:

Should we contact this lead now?
Which channel should we use first?
Which channel should be backup?
Should the message be automated, assisted, reply-only, or held?
Which message angle should we use?
Which existing MenuList onboarding flow should we route to?
What should happen next if they reply, click, ignore, or drop?

It is the decision brain between:

Lead Intelligence
→ Channel Identity
→ Channel Eligibility
→ Message Generation
→ Channel Execution

Important boundary:

The Channel Router recommends.
The Channel Eligibility Engine permits or blocks.
The Channel Execution Layer sends/prepares.

The router should never bypass eligibility, suppression, channel policy, or caps.

8.2 Core principle

The router should not use simplistic rules like:

if phone exists → WhatsApp
if email exists → email
if Instagram exists → DM

That is too crude.

Instead, it should score each possible channel using:

lead quality
lead need
available identities
channel eligibility
contact confidence
previous behavior
source history
campaign goal
message angle fit
onboarding flow fit
channel risk
experiment strategy

The final output should be:

JSON
{
  "primaryChannel": "whatsapp",
  "backupChannel": "email",
  "sendMode": "assisted_send",
  "messageAngle": "menu_link_qr",
  "onboardingFlowId": "restaurant_quick_start",
  "nextBestAction": "prepare_whatsapp_message",
  "reason": "A-score cafe with valid phone, strong MenuList need, and WhatsApp likely highest response channel. Email is available as fallback.",
  "confidence": 0.88
}

That is the router’s job.

8.3 Position in the system

The routing pipeline:

1. Lead is imported / captured
2. Lead Intelligence scores it
3. Channel Identity Registry identifies reachable identities
4. Channel Eligibility Engine determines allowed send modes
5. AI Channel Router chooses best route
6. Message Generator drafts message
7. Channel Execution Layer sends/prepares
8. Unified Inbox captures replies
9. Next-Best-Action Engine updates route

The Channel Router must always consume the latest Eligibility Contract. It cannot choose a channel that is blocked.

Meta’s WhatsApp documentation says template messages are the only type that can be sent to WhatsApp users outside a customer service window, and Meta’s Messenger/Instagram policy describes a 24-hour standard messaging window after user actions. These constraints mean the router must treat WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger differently from email.
Facebook Developers
+1

8.4 What the router owns

The Channel Router owns:

primary channel recommendation
backup channel recommendation
send mode recommendation
offer/message angle
existing onboarding flow recommendation
routing reason
confidence score
fallback route
hold/contact decision

It does not own:

suppression checks
policy permission
template approval
message sending
message content generation
conversation storage
onboarding UX
product conversion logic
8.5 Router input contract

The router should receive one fully prepared input object.

    primaryNeed:
      | "menu_link_qr"

8.7 Channel scoring model

The router should score each eligible channel.

Channel Route Score =
  Lead-Channel Fit
+ Identity Quality
+ Policy Eligibility
+ Historical Performance
+ Intent Continuity
+ Message Angle Fit
+ Onboarding Flow Fit
+ Experiment Value
- Channel Risk
- Suppression/Cooldown Penalty

Each channel receives a score from 0–100.

TypeScript
type ChannelRouteScore = {
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call";

  score: number;

  components: {
    leadChannelFit: number;
    identityQuality: number;
    policyEligibility: number;
    historicalPerformance: number;
    intentContinuity: number;
    messageAngleFit: number;
    onboardingFlowFit: number;
    experimentValue: number;
    riskPenalty: number;
  };

  sendMode: ChannelRouterOutput["sendMode"];

  reason: string;
};

Recommended scoring weights:

Lead-channel fit:        20
Identity quality:        15
Policy eligibility:      20
Historical performance:  15
Intent continuity:       15
Message angle fit:        5
Onboarding flow fit:      5
Experiment value:         5
Risk penalty:           -30 max

Policy eligibility is heavily weighted because a theoretically high-converting channel is useless if it is blocked or risky.

8.8 Channel-specific routing logic
Email

Email should be favored when:

valid email exists
lead is cold or lower-risk
campaign is scalable
WhatsApp is not eligible
business appears more formal
previous email clicked/replied
retargeting is needed

Default send mode:

auto_send

unless human review is required.

Email should not be favored when:

email bounced
unsubscribed
domain suppressed
high complaint risk
low fit / low need
better active inbound channel exists

Use email for:

cold outreach
fallback outreach
retargeting clicked-but-not-started leads
formal follow-ups
WhatsApp

WhatsApp should be favored when:

lead is A-score
valid Indian mobile/WhatsApp-likely phone exists
business is local SMB
business category is restaurant/cafe/bakery/dessert/food
message is simple and direct
operator-assisted or approved-template path is available

Default send mode:

assisted_send

for cold acquisition.

Use template_required or API send only when:

approved template exists
policy allows it
channel account is healthy
campaign cap allows it
suppression checks pass

WhatsApp should not be favored when:

phone confidence is low
wrong-number risk exists
DNC/negative history exists
daily cap reached
template not approved for API send
account quality unhealthy

The router should recognize WhatsApp as high-response but high-care. WhatsApp’s template rules and customer-window structure make it different from email.
Facebook Developers
+1

Instagram DM

Instagram should be favored when:

lead came from Instagram inbound
lead recently messaged MenuList
conversation window is active
business is Instagram-heavy
offer angle is Instagram bio/menu link
lead has interacted with MenuList social campaign

Default send mode:

reply_only

Instagram should not be the default cold channel.

Do not favor Instagram when:

only a public username exists
no inbound conversation exists
response window expired
lead is cold and no permitted campaign context exists
identity confidence is low

Instagram is best for:

warm inbound
social CTA campaigns
comment/profile-driven leads
replying to business questions
routing social leads into onboarding

Meta describes Instagram Messaging API as a way to build messaging solutions for Instagram Professional accounts at scale, but the Growth Engine should still treat Instagram as primarily warm/inbound unless there is a specific compliant campaign context.
Facebook Developers

Messenger

Messenger should be favored when:

lead came from Facebook Page/Messenger inbound
click-to-Messenger campaign generated the lead
active conversation window exists
business interacted through Facebook

Default send mode:

reply_only

Messenger should not be favored when:

no PSID/thread exists
no active window exists
lead is cold
Page/account is disconnected
identity is weak

Messenger is best for:

Facebook Page conversations
click-to-Messenger ads
warm replies
helping interested leads enter onboarding
Call / manual contact

Call should be favored only when:

lead is high-value
phone is valid
lead is A-score
previous message got partial interest
operator is available
business likely responds better to direct call

Default send mode:

assisted_send

Call is not a mass channel.

Use it for:

high-value local businesses
follow-up after reply/click
manual founder-led acquisition
8.9 Decision types

The router can return different decision types.

contact_now

Use when:

lead is qualified
eligible channel exists
no prior outreach conflict
campaign allows sending
score/confidence high enough

Example:

A-score cafe, WhatsApp assisted eligible, email backup.
follow_up

Use when:

lead was contacted
follow-up window is due
no reply yet
not suppressed
channel remains eligible

Follow-up channel may be same or different.

Example:

Email sent 3 days ago, no click, valid WhatsApp exists → prepare assisted WhatsApp.
reply

Use when:

lead sent inbound message
conversation window is active
AI reply classifier detects question/interest

Example:

Instagram inbound asks “What is this?” → reply on Instagram with approved answer and flow link.
route_to_onboarding

Use when:

lead is interested
has asked for link/details
clicked and re-engaged
inbound social lead requests setup

The output must include:

onboardingFlowId
channel
message action
tracking plan
hold

Use when:

lead is not ready
need/channel confidence is weak
cooldown active
campaign cap reached
waiting for enrichment
enrich

Use when:

lead is relevant but contact/channel info is weak
website/social/contact enrichment could help

Example:

Good cafe, website exists, no email/phone found → run website contact extraction.
human_review

Use when:

AI confidence low
identity conflict
possible duplicate
medium/high risk
large chain ambiguity
blocked channel but high-value lead
suppress

Use when:

DNC
complaint
wrong contact with high confidence
unsubscribe
converted and acquisition should stop
reject

Use when:

wrong vertical
irrelevant
closed
duplicate
no useful source/contact and low score
8.10 Offer/message angle selection

The router should choose an offer angle based on need signals and channel.

Allowed offer angles:

TypeScript
type OfferAngle =
  | "menu_link_qr"
  | "instagram_bio_menu"
  | "whatsapp_menu_link"
  | "google_profile_menu_link"
  | "simple_setup"
  | "local_restaurant_setup"
  | "help_complete_onboarding"
  | "reply_to_question";
Angle selection logic
menu_link_qr

Use when:

generic strong MenuList need
restaurant/cafe/bakery/dessert
phone/email available
no specific channel-driven angle

Most common default.

instagram_bio_menu

Use when:

business is Instagram-heavy
Instagram is main public presence
lead came from Instagram
no strong website/menu link

Good for:

Instagram DM
email to Instagram-heavy businesses
whatsapp_menu_link

Use when:

business likely uses WhatsApp with customers
phone/WhatsApp is main reachable channel
business is small/local

Good for:

WhatsApp-assisted outreach
google_profile_menu_link

Use when:

lead likely cares about Google profile/discovery
business has public listing/contact but no clear menu path

Use carefully. Do not say “we scraped your Google listing.” The angle should be:

MenuList link can be used wherever customers look for your menu.
simple_setup

Use when:

lead is lower-tech
short message needed
cold outreach should be minimal
local_restaurant_setup

Use when:

campaign is cluster-based
local density/social proof matters

Example:

We’re helping local cafes/restaurants in Koramangala set up clean menu links + QR.

Use only if true.

help_complete_onboarding

Use when:

lead already started existing MenuList onboarding and dropped

This is retargeting, not cold acquisition.

8.11 Existing onboarding flow selection

The router must select the correct existing MenuList onboarding flow.

It should not create a new flow.

Input:

TypeScript
type AvailableOnboardingFlow = {
  id: string;
  name: string;

  intendedFor: {
    categories?: string[];
    channels?: string[];
    offerAngles?: string[];
    leadSegments?: ("A" | "B" | "C")[];
    intentStages?: string[];
  };

  performance?: {
    startRate?: number;
    completionRate?: number;
    conversionRate?: number;
    dropRate?: number;
  };

  active: boolean;
};

Router output:

TypeScript
onboardingFlow: {
  recommendedFlowId: string;
  reason: string;
}

Flow selection rules:

Use the flow with the highest expected completion probability for this lead/channel/angle.
Do not route to inactive flows.
Do not route to flows outside campaign allowed list.
If flow performance is unknown, use default flow for segment/category.
If lead previously dropped from one flow, consider alternate flow or help message.

The flow router should optimize for:

onboarding completion

not just link clicks.

8.12 Router decision algorithm

Use a hybrid system:

deterministic gates
+ AI reasoning
+ performance data
+ experiment policy

Recommended sequence:

1. Check lead recommendedAction from intelligence.
2. If suppress/reject/hold, respect it unless admin override.
3. Read eligibility contract.
4. Remove blocked channels.
5. Score each eligible channel.
6. Select best primary channel.
7. Select backup channel.
8. Select message angle.
9. Select onboarding flow.
10. Decide send mode.
11. Create fallback plan.
12. Return structured decision.

Pseudo-code:

TypeScript
async function routeLead(input: ChannelRouterInput): Promise<ChannelRouterOutput> {
  if (input.intelligence.recommendedAction === "suppress") {
    return suppressDecision(input);
  }

  if (input.intelligence.recommendedAction === "reject") {
    return rejectDecision(input);
  }

  if (input.intelligence.recommendedAction === "enrich") {
    return enrichDecision(input);
  }

  const eligibleChannels = input.eligibility.channelResults
    .filter(result => result.eligible)
    .filter(result => result.sendMode !== "blocked");

  if (eligibleChannels.length === 0) {
    return holdOrHumanReview(input);
  }

  const channelScores = scoreEligibleChannels({
    input,
    eligibleChannels,
  });

  const primary = selectPrimaryChannel(channelScores);
  const backup = selectBackupChannel(channelScores, primary);

  const messageAngle = selectMessageAngle({
    input,
    primaryChannel: primary.channel,
  });

  const onboardingFlow = selectOnboardingFlow({
    input,
    primaryChannel: primary.channel,
    messageAngle,
  });

  return {
    leadId: input.leadId,
    decision: decideAction(input, primary),
    primaryChannel: primary.channel,
    backupChannel: backup?.channel,
    sendMode: primary.sendMode,
    messageAngle,
    onboardingFlow,
    nextBestAction: mapToNextBestAction(primary.channel, primary.sendMode),
    fallbackPlan: buildFallbackPlan(input, primary, backup),
    reasoning: buildReasoning(input, primary, backup, messageAngle),
    riskNotes: collectRiskNotes(input),
    confidence: calculateRoutingConfidence(input, primary),
    requiresHumanApproval: shouldRequireHumanApproval(input, primary),
    generatedAt: input.now,
  };
}
8.13 Hard routing rules

These should override AI.

Suppression
If global suppression or DNC exists → suppress / blocked.
Rejected lead
If lead status is rejected/duplicate → no route.
No eligible channel
If no eligible channel → enrich, hold, or human_review.
Instagram/Messenger cold outreach
Do not route cold leads to Instagram/Messenger outbound by default.

Use Instagram/Messenger mainly when:

inbound conversation exists
ad/social campaign generated interaction
reply window is active
WhatsApp cold API send
Do not route cold WhatsApp API send unless approved template + eligibility pass.

Assisted WhatsApp is acceptable if configured.

Email unsubscribe/bounce
Never route email if unsubscribed/bounced/suppressed.
Converted lead
Do not route acquisition messages to converted leads.
8.14 Soft routing preferences

These are not hard rules, but strong defaults.

A-score leads
prefer high-response channels
WhatsApp assisted if phone strong
email fallback
manual call optional for high-value
B-score leads
email first if available
WhatsApp assisted only if strong phone + low risk
enrich if channel weak
C-score leads
hold or enrich
do not contact unless campaign requires volume/test
Inbound social leads
reply on same channel first
route directly to onboarding if intent is clear
Clicked but not started
follow up through same channel if eligible
or email if original channel no longer eligible
Started but dropped
use help_complete_onboarding angle
same channel if possible
8.15 Fallback plans

Every route should include fallback logic.

Examples:

WhatsApp primary + email backup
JSON
[
  {
    "condition": "no_reply",
    "action": "draft_email",
    "channel": "email",
    "delayHours": 72
  },
  {
    "condition": "whatsapp_not_sent",
    "action": "draft_email",
    "channel": "email",
    "delayHours": 0
  }
]
Email primary + WhatsApp backup
JSON
[
  {
    "condition": "email_bounce",
    "action": "prepare_whatsapp",
    "channel": "whatsapp",
    "delayHours": 0
  },
  {
    "condition": "no_reply",
    "action": "prepare_whatsapp",
    "channel": "whatsapp",
    "delayHours": 96
  }
]
Instagram inbound
JSON
[
  {
    "condition": "window_expired",
    "action": "wait",
    "delayHours": 0
  }
]

Fallbacks make the system operationally useful instead of a one-shot recommendation engine.

8.16 Experiment integration

The router should support controlled exploration.

Campaign context may say:

exploit best channel
explore channel variants
test offer angle
test onboarding flow
manual-only

Experiment examples:

WhatsApp vs email for A-score cafes
menu_link_qr vs instagram_bio_menu angle
quick-start flow vs generic flow
short message vs detailed message

Router should respect experiment assignment.

TypeScript
type RouterExperimentPolicy = {
  experimentId: string;
  variantId: string;

  forcedChannel?: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";
  forcedOfferAngle?: OfferAngle;
  forcedOnboardingFlowId?: string;

  allowOverrideIfRisky: boolean;
};

If an experiment forces a channel that eligibility blocks, eligibility wins.

Eligibility > experiment assignment.
8.17 Performance feedback

The router should learn from outcomes.

For each route, later measure:

reply
click
onboarding start
onboarding completion
conversion
negative reply
DNC
bounce/failure

Router performance metrics:

completion rate by recommended channel
completion rate by backup channel
negative rate by channel
completion rate by offer angle
flow completion by router decision
human override rate
AI confidence calibration

The router should eventually answer:

For this lead type, channel X works 2.1x better than channel Y.

That is the long-term advantage.

8.18 Confidence scoring

Router confidence should combine:

lead intelligence confidence
identity confidence
eligibility clarity
channel performance sample size
message angle confidence
onboarding flow confidence
risk level

Suggested formula:

Router Confidence =
  0.25 × Lead Intelligence Confidence
+ 0.20 × Identity Confidence
+ 0.20 × Eligibility Confidence
+ 0.15 × Historical Performance Confidence
+ 0.10 × Flow Fit Confidence
+ 0.10 × Low Risk Confidence

Confidence interpretation:

>= 0.90: safe to queue/action according to send mode
0.75–0.89: usable
0.60–0.74: human review recommended
< 0.60: hold/human review
8.19 Human approval rules

Router should set:

TypeScript
requiresHumanApproval: boolean

Human approval required if:

sendMode = assisted_send
sendMode = human_review
confidence < threshold
risk flag medium/high
lead is high-value but ambiguous
first run of new campaign
message angle is experimental
channel is WhatsApp cold outreach
Instagram/Messenger action is not a direct reply

Human approval not required for:

routine email sends
low-risk email follow-ups
reply inside active window with approved response
AI recommendations that only hold/enrich/reject low-value leads

Exact autonomy depends on policy config.

8.20 Router AI prompt contract

The router prompt should be strict.

System instruction summary:

You are the routing brain for MenuList Growth Engine.
Your job is to choose the safest and most effective acquisition route.
You must never choose a blocked channel.
You must respect suppression, channel eligibility, and campaign caps.
You must optimize for completed MenuList onboarding, not replies or message volume.
Return only valid JSON matching the schema.

Router must consider:

lead score
need
contactability
risk
identity quality
eligibility
history
campaign goal
available flows
channel performance

Router must not:

invent channel availability
bypass blocked channels
recommend cold Instagram/Messenger DM by default
recommend WhatsApp API send without eligibility/template
route to inactive onboarding flow
ignore suppression
optimize for raw message volume

Because router outputs affect live messaging, use structured outputs. Gemini supports schema-constrained outputs, and function calling can be used when the router needs to consult allowed tools such as getChannelPerformance, getAvailableOnboardingFlows, or getExperimentAssignment.
Google AI for Developers
+1

8.21 Router tools

Allowed tools:

getLeadIntelligence(leadId)
getChannelIdentityContract(leadId)
getEligibilityContract(leadId)
getChannelPerformance(segment)
getAvailableOnboardingFlows()
getExperimentAssignment(leadId, campaignId)
getRecentConversationSummary(leadId)

Not allowed tools:

sendMessage()
createSuppression()
modifyOnboardingFlow()
changePricing()
changeCampaignCaps()

The router recommends; execution systems act.

8.23 Dashboard output

On lead page, show:

AI Channel Route

Primary: WhatsApp
Mode: Assisted send
Backup: Email
Angle: Menu link + QR
Flow: restaurant_quick_start

The operator should understand the route in 10 seconds.

8.24 Work queues produced by router

Router outputs feed work queues.

Email auto-send queue
WhatsApp assisted queue
WhatsApp template queue
Instagram reply queue
Messenger reply queue
Human review queue
Enrichment queue
Hold/cooldown queue
Retargeting queue

Example:

primaryChannel = whatsapp
sendMode = assisted_send
nextBestAction = prepare_whatsapp
→ appears in WhatsApp Assisted Queue
primaryChannel = email
sendMode = auto_send
nextBestAction = draft_email
→ appears in Email Auto-send Queue
8.25 Router modes

Use three router modes.

Mode 1 — Conservative
AI recommends only.
Most outreach requires human approval.

Use for:

new campaigns
new channels
new message angles
high-risk segments
Mode 2 — Assisted
AI routes and queues.
Email can auto-send.
WhatsApp remains assisted.
Instagram/Messenger replies are queued for approval unless low-risk.

Recommended default.

Mode 3 — Autonomous with guardrails
AI routes and execution layer sends low-risk messages automatically.
Human handles exceptions.

Use only after metrics/evals prove reliability.

Router mode can be configured per:

campaign
channel
lead segment
source
operator policy

8.27 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Router optimizes for reply rate

Fix:

Optimize for onboarding starts/completions, not replies.
Failure mode 2 — Router overuses WhatsApp

Fix:

WhatsApp cap, assisted-send default, negative-rate guardrails.
Failure mode 3 — Router sends cold Instagram/Messenger

Fix:

Eligibility blocks unless inbound/warm context exists.
Failure mode 4 — Router ignores backup channels

Fix:

Require fallback plan for every contact route.
Failure mode 5 — Router routes to wrong onboarding flow

Fix:

Flow performance feedback + flow eligibility metadata.
Failure mode 6 — Router decisions are not explainable

Fix:

Structured reasoning field required.
Operator dashboard shows why.
8.28 Router evaluation

Create evaluation datasets.

Eval set 1 — Historical routing

Input:

lead intelligence + identities + eligibility

Expected:

best channel based on actual outcomes

Metric:

router selected winning/acceptable channel
Eval set 2 — Policy safety

Input:

blocked/suppressed/expired-window leads

Expected:

router does not route to blocked channel

Metric:

zero critical policy violations
Eval set 3 — Channel fit

Input:

local SMB with phone/email/social

Expected:

reasonable primary + backup channel

Metric:

human acceptance rate
Eval set 4 — Onboarding flow routing

Input:

lead/channel/angle

Expected:

flow with highest historical completion

Metric:

flow selection accuracy / downstream completion rate

Key real-world metric:

AI-routed leads should complete onboarding at higher rate than random/manual baseline.
8.29 Router KPIs

Track:

routing decisions made
human approval rate
human override rate
completion rate by routed channel
negative rate by routed channel
fallback success rate
onboarding flow completion by router output
router confidence vs actual outcome
policy block rate
wrong-channel override rate

Important:

high human override rate = bad router
high negative rate = bad channel/message/targeting
low completion despite high click = wrong flow/message

8.31 Final principle

The AI Channel Router is where the Growth Engine becomes intelligent.

Lead sourcing gives you possible businesses.

Lead intelligence tells you who is worth contacting.

Channel identity tells you where they exist.

Eligibility tells you what is allowed.

The Channel Router decides:

what path gives this lead the highest probability of completing MenuList onboarding with the lowest channel risk?

That is the routing question.

The router should optimize for:

completed onboarding
not replies
not clicks
not message volume
````

````text
Spec 9 — Existing MenuList Onboarding Flow Router
9.1 Purpose

The Existing MenuList Onboarding Flow Router decides which already-built MenuList onboarding flow a lead should enter.

It answers:

Which existing MenuList flow should this lead be sent to?
What tracking URL should be generated?
What context should be passed to the flow?
What events should come back to the Growth Engine?
How do we measure whether this route worked?

It does not build onboarding flows.

It does not modify onboarding UX.

It does not manage product activation.

It only routes leads into the correct existing flow and learns from outcomes.

9.2 Core boundary

The clean boundary is:

Growth Engine owns:
- selecting flow
- generating tracked URL
- attaching campaign/channel/message attribution
- recording route event
- receiving onboarding outcome events
- learning which flow works for which lead type

MenuList Product owns:
- onboarding UX
- onboarding state
- menu/business setup
- product activation
- account/business creation
- internal onboarding validation

The Growth Engine should treat onboarding flows as black boxes with metadata and events.

9.3 Why this router matters

If MenuList already has multiple onboarding flows, sending every lead to the same flow is wasteful.

Different leads need different entry points.

Examples:

Cold email lead → lower-friction setup flow
WhatsApp lead → mobile-first flow
Instagram lead → social-friendly flow
High-intent inbound lead → direct setup flow
Clicked but did not start → shorter restart flow
Started but dropped → resume/help flow
Large/local chain → manual-assisted flow

The router’s job is to choose the path most likely to produce:

completed onboarding

not just:

link click
9.4 Core principle

The onboarding flow router should optimize for:

expected onboarding completion probability

not:

the newest flow
the prettiest flow
the most generic flow
the easiest URL

The router should learn:

which flow converts best for which lead segment, source, channel, message angle, and intent stage.
9.5 Position in the system

The flow is:

Lead Intelligence Layer
→ Channel Identity Registry
→ Channel Eligibility Engine
→ AI Channel Router
→ Onboarding Flow Router
→ Message Generator
→ Channel Execution Layer
→ Existing MenuList Onboarding
→ Feedback Events
→ Growth Engine Learning Loop

The Channel Router chooses:

channel + message angle + send mode

The Onboarding Flow Router chooses:

flow + URL + tracking context

These are related but separate decisions.

9.6 What this router owns

The Onboarding Flow Router owns:

flow registry
flow eligibility
flow selection
flow URL generation
tracking parameter generation
handoff payload
route event creation
flow performance feedback
flow-level experiment assignment
drop-off retargeting classification

It does not own:

flow screen design
form fields
business creation
menu creation
pricing
account creation
post-onboarding product state
9.7 Onboarding Flow Registry

Create a registry of all existing MenuList onboarding flows.

Collection:

growthOnboardingFlows

This is not the actual product flow implementation. It is metadata used by the Growth Engine.

TypeScript
type GrowthOnboardingFlow = {
  id: string;

  name: string;

  status:
    | "active"
    | "paused"
    | "deprecated"
    | "experimental"
    | "internal_only";

  baseUrl: string;

  description?: string;

  intendedFor: {
    leadSegments?: ("A" | "B" | "C")[];

    categories?: (
      | "restaurant"
      | "cafe"
      | "bakery"
      | "dessert_shop"
      | "cloud_kitchen"
      | "other_food"
      | "unknown"
    )[];

    channels?: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

    offerAngles?: OfferAngle[];

    intentStages?: (
      | "cold"
      | "engaged"
      | "interested"
      | "clicked"
      | "started_dropped"
      | "inbound"
      | "retargeting"
    )[];

    businessScale?: (
      | "single_location_smb"
      | "small_local_chain"
      | "large_chain"
      | "franchise"
      | "unknown"
    )[];
  };

  constraints: {
    requiresPhone?: boolean;
    requiresEmail?: boolean;
    requiresInstagram?: boolean;
    requiresExistingBusinessId?: boolean;
    requiresHumanAssistance?: boolean;
    mobileOptimized?: boolean;
    supportsPrefill?: boolean;
    supportsResume?: boolean;
    supportsTrackingParams?: boolean;
  };

  prefillFields?: {
    businessName?: boolean;
    city?: boolean;
    area?: boolean;
    phone?: boolean;
    email?: boolean;
    instagram?: boolean;
    sourceCampaign?: boolean;
  };

  performance: {
    routedCount: number;
    clickRate?: number;
    startRate?: number;
    completionRate?: number;
    dropRate?: number;
    conversionRate?: number;

    byChannel?: Record<string, FlowPerformanceSnapshot>;
    bySegment?: Record<string, FlowPerformanceSnapshot>;
    byOfferAngle?: Record<string, FlowPerformanceSnapshot>;
  };

  priority: number;

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};

The Growth Engine should only route to flows where:

status = active or experimental

unless explicitly overridden.

9.11 Flow eligibility

Before scoring flows, remove ineligible flows.

A flow is ineligible if:

status is paused/deprecated
campaign blocks the flow
flow requires phone but no phone exists
flow requires email but no email exists
flow requires Instagram but no Instagram identity exists
flow is not suitable for lead category
flow is not suitable for channel
flow is not suitable for intent stage
flow requires human assistance but no operator path exists

Pseudo-code:

TypeScript
function isFlowEligible(
  flow: GrowthOnboardingFlow,
  input: OnboardingFlowRouterInput
): boolean {
  if (!["active", "experimental"].includes(flow.status)) return false;

  if (input.campaignContext?.blockedFlowIds?.includes(flow.id)) return false;

  if (
    input.campaignContext?.allowedFlowIds &&
    !input.campaignContext.allowedFlowIds.includes(flow.id)
  ) {
    return false;
  }

  if (
    flow.intendedFor.channels?.length &&
    input.channelRoute.primaryChannel &&
    !flow.intendedFor.channels.includes(input.channelRoute.primaryChannel)
  ) {
    return false;
  }

  if (
    flow.intendedFor.categories?.length &&
    !flow.intendedFor.categories.includes(input.lead.business.category as any)
  ) {
    return false;
  }

  if (
    flow.intendedFor.leadSegments?.length &&
    !flow.intendedFor.leadSegments.includes(input.intelligence.segment)
  ) {
    return false;
  }

  return true;
}

Eligibility is deterministic. AI should not override hard ineligibility.

9.12 Flow scoring model

Each eligible flow gets a score.

Flow Fit Score =
  Lead Segment Fit
+ Category Fit
+ Channel Fit
+ Offer Angle Fit
+ Intent Stage Fit
+ Historical Completion Performance
+ Prefill Support
+ Mobile Fit
- Drop/Failure History Penalty
- Flow Risk Penalty

Suggested weights:

Lead segment fit:              15
Category fit:                  10
Channel fit:                   20
Offer angle fit:               15
Intent stage fit:              15
Historical completion:         20
Prefill/mobile support:         5
Drop/failure penalty:         -20 max

Flow should be selected by expected completion, not just metadata match.

9.13 Expected completion score

Long-term, calculate:

Expected Completion Score =
  base flow completion rate
× channel-flow multiplier
× segment-flow multiplier
× offer-angle multiplier
× lead intent multiplier
× drop-history penalty

Example:

restaurant_quick_start base completion: 18%
WhatsApp multiplier: 1.3
A-lead multiplier: 1.4
menu_link_qr multiplier: 1.1
intent cold multiplier: 0.8

Expected completion ≈ 18% × 1.3 × 1.4 × 1.1 × 0.8

The router can use this over time once there is enough data.

Before enough data, use rule-based flow fit.

9.14 Flow selection rules
Cold outbound lead

Use flows optimized for:

low friction
mobile
clear value
minimal steps
prefill support

Avoid:

long signup flows
flows requiring account creation too early
complex business setup flows
WhatsApp lead

Prefer:

mobile-first flow
short flow
flow with phone prefill
flow that can be reopened easily
Email lead

Prefer:

web-friendly flow
clear explanation
flow that can handle more context
Instagram lead

Prefer:

mobile-first flow
Instagram/social-context flow
flow with Instagram prefill if available
Messenger lead

Prefer:

mobile-first flow
Page/social-context flow
simple setup path
Started but dropped

Prefer:

resume flow if possible
help-complete flow
shorter alternate flow
manual-assisted flow if high-value
High-value / ambiguous lead

Prefer:

manual-assisted flow
or human review before routing
9.15 Existing route reuse

Do not create multiple routing links unnecessarily.

If a lead already has an active route to the same flow and campaign, reuse it.

TypeScript
type GrowthLeadRoute = {
  id: string;

  leadId: string;
  flowId: string;

  status:
    | "created"
    | "clicked"
    | "started"
    | "completed"
    | "dropped"
    | "expired"
    | "revoked";

  trackingUrl: string;

  attribution: GrowthAttribution;

  createdAt: Date;
  expiresAt?: Date;
};

Reuse if:

same lead
same flow
same campaign
route not expired
route not completed
route not revoked

Create a new route if:

new campaign
new flow
previous route expired
previous flow dropped and alternate flow selected
previous route attribution should be separated
9.16 Tracking URL strategy

Do not send raw onboarding URLs directly.

Send tracked URLs.

Example:

https://menulist.com/g/r/abc123

or:

https://menulist.com/start?gclid_internal=route_abc123

Recommended:

short tracking route → redirects to actual onboarding flow

Why:

short links are cleaner in WhatsApp/DM
tracking is centralized
flow URL can change later
clicks are recorded before redirect
routing attribution is preserved

Route collection:

growthLeadRoutes/{routeId}

9.22 Feedback handling

On event:

flow_link_clicked

Update:

route.status = clicked
route.stats.clickCount += 1
route.stats.firstClickedAt / lastClickedAt
lead.status = engaged, if earlier state
growthEvent = flow_link_clicked
onboarding_started

Update:

route.status = started
route.stats.startedAt
lead.status = onboarding_started
lead.onboardingFeedback.currentState = started
growthEvent = onboarding_started
onboarding_step_completed

Update:

append event
keep lead status
use for drop analysis
onboarding_dropped

Update:

route.status = dropped
route.stats.droppedAt
lead.onboardingFeedback.currentState = dropped
lead.onboardingFeedback.drop = step/reason
create retargeting opportunity
onboarding_completed

Update:

route.status = completed
route.stats.completedAt
lead.status = onboarding_completed
lead.onboardingFeedback.currentState = completed
growthEvent = onboarding_completed
converted

Update:

route.status = converted
lead.status = converted
suppress acquisition outreach
growthEvent = lead_converted

9.25 Drop-off retargeting

If onboarding sends onboarding_dropped, the Growth Engine should create a retargeting state.

Examples:

flow started, dropped at phone step
flow started, dropped at menu/upload step
flow started, dropped at business info step
flow clicked, never started

The Growth Engine should not fix the product flow. It should decide the next acquisition action.

Possible actions:

send help message
route to shorter flow
route to manual-assisted flow
follow up through same channel
hold if low intent
human review if high-value

This is handled later by the Next-Best-Action Engine, but the Flow Router should store enough context.

9.26 Resume behavior

If a lead already started onboarding and dropped, the router should check whether the product flow supports resume.

Flow constraint:

TypeScript
supportsResume: boolean

If true:

send resume link

If false:

route to alternate flow or manual-assisted flow

Decision:

TypeScript
decision: "resume_existing_flow" | "route_to_flow"

This helps reduce drop-off without creating new onboarding logic inside Growth Engine.

9.27 Flow experiment integration

The router should support experiments.

Example experiment:

For A-score WhatsApp cafe leads:
Variant A → restaurant_quick_start
Variant B → whatsapp_quick_start
Metric → onboarding completion rate

Experiment assignment should happen before flow selection if campaign config requires it.

But hard rules apply:

Eligibility > experiment
Flow active status > experiment
Suppression > experiment

Experiment policy object:

TypeScript
type FlowExperimentPolicy = {
  experimentId: string;
  variantId: string;

  forcedFlowId?: string;

  allowRouterOverrideIfIneligible: boolean;

  successMetric:
    | "onboarding_start_rate"
    | "onboarding_completion_rate"
    | "conversion_rate"
    | "cost_per_completion";
};
9.28 Human approval rules

Flow routing usually can be automated.

Human approval required if:

recommended flow requires human assistance
lead is high-value but ambiguous
flow confidence is low
lead previously dropped multiple times
large chain/franchise
experiment flow is risky
no clearly eligible flow

Human approval not required for:

standard cold A/B leads to default active flow
inbound leads to matching active flow
retargeting to same/resume flow with high confidence
9.29 AI flow routing prompt contract

If using AI for flow selection, the prompt should be strict.

System instruction summary:

You choose from existing MenuList onboarding flows only.
You cannot create new flows.
You cannot modify flows.
You must respect flow eligibility, campaign restrictions, and active/deprecated status.
You optimize for completed onboarding, not clicks.
Return only valid JSON matching the schema.

The AI must not:

invent flow IDs
route to inactive flows
ignore previous drop-off
ignore channel context
select a flow outside campaign allowed list
make product promises

The AI can:

rank eligible flows
explain fit
choose fallback flow
recommend human review

9.34 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Every lead routed to generic flow

Fix:

Flow registry + performance-based selection.
Failure mode 2 — Router optimizes for clicks

Fix:

Optimize for onboarding completion.
Failure mode 3 — Flow mismatch by channel

Example:

Instagram lead sent to desktop-heavy form.

Fix:

Channel-fit metadata and performance feedback.
Failure mode 4 — Duplicate routing links

Fix:

reuse active routes when appropriate.
Failure mode 5 — No attribution

Fix:

route ID required for every growth-generated onboarding link.
Failure mode 6 — Growth system starts owning onboarding

Fix:

strict boundary: Growth routes; Product onboards.

9.37 Final principle

The Onboarding Flow Router exists to make growth traffic land in the right product entry point.

The Growth Engine should not say:

“Here is a generic link for everyone.”

It should say:

“This specific lead, from this source, on this channel, with this offer angle, should enter this existing MenuList onboarding flow because it has the highest expected completion probability.”

That is the difference between messaging leads and building a real acquisition system.
````

````text
Spec 10 — Offer Angles and Positioning Library
10.1 Purpose

The Offer Angles and Positioning Library defines what the Growth Engine says to a lead before routing them into an existing MenuList onboarding flow.

It answers:

Why should this business care?
What outcome are we promising?
Which angle fits this lead, channel, and campaign?
What claims are allowed?
What claims are banned?
Which onboarding flow should this angle route into?
How do we test which angle converts?

This is not the message template system. Templates are channel-specific wording.

This is the strategic layer above templates.

Offer angle = the reason to care.
Template = the exact message.
Onboarding flow = where the lead goes after clicking/replying.
10.2 Core boundary

The positioning library belongs to the Growth Engine.

It owns:

acquisition angles
lead-facing value proposition
CTA direction
message framing
allowed claims
banned claims
angle-to-channel fit
angle-to-flow mapping
experiment variants
angle performance tracking

It does not own:

MenuList product positioning globally
onboarding flow UX
pricing
post-onboarding activation
menu creation
business verification
product feature design

It only decides:

What do we say to get this business into the right MenuList onboarding flow?
10.3 Core positioning principle

For SMB restaurants/cafes, do not lead with abstract infrastructure language.

Do not say:

business truth layer
canonical public info infrastructure
authority layer
distributed public business record

Those are useful internally, not for acquisition.

Lead with a simple owner-facing outcome:

clean customer-facing menu link + QR

The owner-facing acquisition promise should be:

MenuList helps restaurants create a clean menu link + QR that customers can open from WhatsApp, Instagram, Google, or in-store.

That is concrete.

The internal strategic meaning remains:

MenuList acquires and routes businesses into customer-facing business truth infrastructure.

But the outbound wedge must stay simple.

10.4 What an offer angle is

An offer angle is a reusable acquisition frame.

Example:

menu_link_qr

Meaning:

Position MenuList as a clean digital menu link and QR for customer use.

Same angle can be expressed differently by channel:

Email version
WhatsApp version
Instagram DM version
Messenger version
Follow-up version

But the underlying reason to care is the same.

10.5 Core offer angle object

Use this schema.

TypeScript
type OfferAngle = {
  id:
    | "menu_link_qr"
    | "whatsapp_menu_link"
    | "instagram_bio_menu"
    | "google_profile_menu_link"
    | "simple_setup"
    | "local_restaurant_setup"

    | "customer_request"
    | "help_complete_onboarding"
    | "reactivation";

  name: string;

  status: "active" | "paused" | "experimental" | "deprecated";

  oneLinePromise: string;

  idealFor: {
    categories?: string[];
    leadSegments?: ("A" | "B" | "C")[];
    channels?: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];
    needSignals?: string[];
    intentStages?: string[];
    businessScale?: string[];
  };

  avoidFor: {
    categories?: string[];
    channels?: string[];
    riskFlags?: string[];
    statuses?: string[];
  };

  allowedClaims: string[];

  bannedClaims: string[];

  primaryCTA:
    | "start_onboarding"
    | "reply_yes"
    | "send_menu"
    | "open_setup_link"
    | "resume_onboarding"
    | "ask_question";

  recommendedFlowIds: string[];

  defaultTemplateFamily: string;

    sent: number;

    onboardingStarts: number;
    onboardingCompletions: number;

  };

  priority: number;

10.20 Angle scoring model

Each angle should receive a score.

Angle Score =
  Need Fit
+ Channel Fit
+ Lead Segment Fit
+ Intent Stage Fit
+ Flow Fit
+ Historical Performance
+ Campaign Strategy Fit
- Risk Penalty

Suggested weights:

Need fit:                25
Channel fit:             20
Intent stage fit:        15
Flow fit:                15
Historical performance:  15
Campaign strategy fit:   10
Risk penalty:           -30 max

Example:

Instagram inbound lead:
instagram_bio_menu scores high.
menu_link_qr scores medium.
google_profile_menu_link scores low.

10.23 Angle-to-template relationship

Do not hardcode full message copy into offer angles.

Use this hierarchy:

Offer angle
  → template family
      → channel-specific template
          → AI-safe personalization
              → final message

Example:

menu_link_qr
  → template family: "clean_menu_link_qr"
      → whatsapp_initial_v1
      → email_initial_v1
      → instagram_reply_v1
      → messenger_reply_v1

The offer angle decides what the message is about.

The template decides how it is said.

The AI generator fills safe variables.

Every promotion campaign should be able to test angles.

type OfferAngleExperiment = {

10.28 AI offer selector prompt contract

The AI selecting the offer angle should follow a strict contract.

System instruction summary:

You select one approved MenuList acquisition offer angle for a lead.
You cannot invent new angles.
You must respect campaign allowed angles.
You must not use banned claims.
You optimize for onboarding completion, not replies.
Return valid JSON only.

Inputs:

lead intelligence
channel route
identity context
lead history
campaign context
available offer angles
flow map
angle performance

Output:

selected angle
fallback angle
reason
CTA
recommended flow IDs
confidence
human approval requirement

The AI must not:

invent product features
promise free/limited/exclusive unless allowed
use customer request angle without a real demand signal
use local campaign angle if not true
use Google angle in a way that implies scraping/official integration
10.29 Human approval triggers

Require human approval if:

angle = customer_request and demand signal confidence is low
angle = early_access_setup and campaign is not configured for it
angle = local_restaurant_setup and cluster claim is weak
angle = google_profile_menu_link and message may imply Google management
angle = reactivation after prior not_interested
lead has medium/high risk flags
AI confidence < 0.75

No approval needed for:

menu_link_qr on standard A/B leads
simple_setup on low-risk WhatsApp-assisted queue
instagram_bio_menu for inbound Instagram leads
help_complete_onboarding for started/dropped leads with active route

Depending on your autonomy settings.

10.30 Angle-specific failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Too many angles

Symptom:

hard to learn which message works
small sample sizes
operator confusion

Fix:

keep active angles under 6–8
deprecate weak angles
Failure mode 2 — Over-personalization

Symptom:

message feels creepy
negative replies increase

Fix:

ban source-specific claims
use soft, generic customer-facing value
Failure mode 3 — Optimizing for replies

Symptom:

high reply rate, low onboarding completion

Fix:

rank angles by onboarding completion
Failure mode 4 — Misleading claims

Symptom:

owners challenge accuracy
trust damage

Fix:

evidence requirement
banned claims
human approval for sensitive angles
Failure mode 5 — Wrong flow for angle

Symptom:

clicks but low starts/completions

Fix:

angle-to-flow mapping + flow performance feedback
10.31 Recommended active angle set

Start with these as active:

menu_link_qr
whatsapp_menu_link
instagram_bio_menu
simple_setup
help_complete_onboarding
customer_request, only when real signal exists

Keep these experimental/conditional:

google_profile_menu_link
local_restaurant_setup
early_access_setup
reactivation

Reason:

The active set covers most acquisition needs without creating copy chaos.

10.33 Final principle

Offer angles are how the Growth Engine translates MenuList’s product value into a lead-specific reason to act.

The system should not say:

“Here is a generic MenuList pitch.”

It should say:

“This business, from this source, on this channel, with this need signal, should hear this specific acquisition angle and be routed to this existing onboarding flow.”

The best default remains:

clean menu link + QR for customers

Everything else is a more specific version of that core wedge.
````

````text
Spec 11 — Message Template System
11.1 Purpose

The Message Template System controls what the Growth Engine says across:

email
WhatsApp
Instagram DM
Messenger

It exists so AI can personalize messages without creating chaos, false claims, policy risk, or off-brand outreach.

It answers:

Which template should be used?
Which channel version should be used?
Which variables are allowed?
What claims are banned?
Does this message require approval?
Can AI rewrite it?
Can it be sent automatically?
How do we measure performance?

This layer sits between:

Offer Angle
→ Message Template
→ AI Message Generator
→ Channel Execution
11.2 Core boundary

The template system owns:

template families
channel-specific templates
message variables
template approval state
versioning
AI rewrite rules
banned claims
required compliance text
template performance
experiment variants

It does not own:

lead scoring
channel eligibility
channel selection
onboarding flow design
conversation state
actual message sending
MenuList product/onboarding behavior

The template system only controls the message content and rules around it.

11.3 Core principle

Do not let AI write outreach from scratch every time.

Use this hierarchy:

Offer Angle
  → Template Family
    → Channel Template
      → AI-safe personalization
        → Rendered Message
          → Eligibility check
            → Send / queue / human approval

AI can adapt, shorten, and personalize inside boundaries.

AI must not invent:

new claims
new offers
new onboarding flows
new pricing
new guarantees
new product capabilities
11.4 Template system architecture

Use four levels.

Level 1 — Offer angle

Example:

menu_link_qr

Meaning:

The message should position MenuList as a clean menu link + QR for customers.
Level 2 — Template family

Example:

clean_menu_link_qr_initial

Meaning:

Initial outreach message for the menu link + QR angle.
Level 3 — Channel template

Examples:

email_clean_menu_link_qr_initial_v1
wa_clean_menu_link_qr_initial_v1
ig_clean_menu_link_qr_reply_v1
msgr_clean_menu_link_qr_reply_v1
Level 4 — Rendered message

Example:

Hi ABC Cafe, Danny from MenuList here.

We help restaurants create a clean menu link + QR that customers can open from WhatsApp, Instagram, or in-store.

You can start here:
https://...
11.5 Template object

Collection:

growthMessageTemplates

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthMessageTemplate = {
  id: string;

  name: string;

  status:
    | "draft"
    | "internal_review"
    | "internal_approved"
    | "provider_submitted"
    | "provider_approved"
    | "provider_rejected"

  channel:
    | "email"
    | "whatsapp"
    | "instagram"
    | "messenger";

  type:
    | "cold_initial"
    | "follow_up_1"
    | "follow_up_2"
    | "reply_to_question"
    | "price_answer"
    | "send_onboarding_link"
    | "clicked_not_started"
    | "started_not_completed"
    | "reactivation"
    | "dnc_confirmation";

  offerAngle:
    | "menu_link_qr"
    | "whatsapp_menu_link"
    | "instagram_bio_menu"
    | "google_profile_menu_link"
    | "simple_setup"
    | "local_restaurant_setup"
    | "early_access_setup"
    | "customer_request"
    | "help_complete_onboarding"
    | "reactivation";

  templateFamily: string;

  subject?: string; // email only

  body: string;

  variables: TemplateVariable[];

  aiPersonalization: {
    allowed: boolean;
    mode: "none" | "light" | "rewrite_with_guardrails";
    maxChangeLevel: "none" | "small" | "medium";
  };

  allowedClaims: string[];

  };

    metaTemplateCategory?: "marketing" | "utility" | "authentication";
    providerTemplateId?: string;

11.6 Template variables

Variables must be explicit and safe.

TypeScript
type TemplateVariable = {
  key:
    | "business_name"
    | "sender_name"
    | "flow_url"
    | "short_flow_url"
    | "city"
    | "area"
    | "category"
    | "menu_example_url"
    | "reply_keyword"
    | "support_contact"
    | "unsubscribe_url";

  required: boolean;

  source:
    | "lead"
    | "route"
    | "campaign"
    | "operator"
    | "system";

  fallback?: string;

  allowedInChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger")[];
};

Allowed variables:

business_name
sender_name
flow_url
short_flow_url
city
area
category
menu_example_url
reply_keyword
support_contact
unsubscribe_url

Blocked variables:

rating
review_count
google_maps_url
scraped_source
owner_name, unless owner provided it
competitor_name
estimated_revenue
negative website/menu claims

Reason:

The message should feel useful, not creepy.
11.7 Template statuses

Use strict statuses.

draft
→ internal_review
→ internal_approved
→ provider_submitted, if needed
→ provider_approved, if needed
→ active/sendable

Status meanings:

Status	Meaning
draft	Editable, cannot send
internal_review	Needs approval
internal_approved	Can be used for email/manual/DM replies depending channel
provider_submitted	Submitted to Meta/provider
provider_approved	Can be used for provider-template sends
provider_rejected	Cannot send through provider API
paused	Temporarily disabled
deprecated	Retired, not used in new campaigns

For WhatsApp API sends, provider approval matters. WhatsApp templates must be categorized, and Meta’s template docs list categories such as authentication, marketing, and utility.
Facebook Developers
+1

11.8 Channel-specific template rules
Email

Email templates can be more explanatory.

Required:

clear sender identity
accurate subject
plain CTA
unsubscribe/opt-out handling
reply-to address

The FTC’s CAN-SPAM guide says commercial email must avoid false or misleading header information, avoid deceptive subject lines, and provide a way recipients can opt out of future emails.
Federal Trade Commission
+1

Email templates should support:

subject
plain text body
light HTML body, optional
unsubscribe footer
tracking link
reply-to inbox

Default email send mode:

auto_send, if eligibility allows
WhatsApp

WhatsApp templates must be short, direct, and high-trust.

Two WhatsApp modes:

assisted WhatsApp message
WhatsApp Business Platform template

For assisted WhatsApp:

internal_approved is enough
operator sends manually

For API template send:

provider_approved is required

WhatsApp Business Platform templates are the provider-approved format used for template messages, and template category is part of template management.
Facebook Developers
+1

WhatsApp templates should avoid:

long explanations
multiple links
pressure language
ambiguous opt-in assumptions

Default WhatsApp cold mode:

assisted_send
Instagram DM

Instagram templates should be reply-oriented and short.

Use mainly for:

inbound/warm conversations
comment/profile CTA responses
social campaign replies

Meta’s Messenger/Instagram messaging policy uses a standard 24-hour response window after user interaction, so Instagram templates should be treated as reply-window messaging unless a specific approved campaign context exists.
Facebook Developers

Instagram templates should avoid:

cold DM blasting
long sales copy
aggressive follow-up
claims based on scraped profile data

Default Instagram mode:

reply_only
Messenger

Messenger templates should behave like Instagram: short, reply-oriented, and flow-link focused.

Use for:

Facebook Page messages
Click-to-Messenger campaigns
inbound replies
warm retargeting inside policy window

Meta’s Messenger/Instagram policy states businesses have up to 24 hours to respond to a user, so Messenger templates must respect the active conversation window.
Facebook Developers

Default Messenger mode:

reply_only
11.9 Template families

Use a small set of template families.

1. clean_menu_link_qr
2. whatsapp_menu_link
3. instagram_bio_menu
4. simple_setup
5. local_restaurant_setup
6. customer_request
7. onboarding_resume
8. reactivation
9. objection_response
10. dnc_confirmation

Do not create too many families. Too many templates will make testing noisy.

11.22 AI personalization levels

Use three levels.

Level 0 — No AI rewrite

Template is rendered exactly.

Use for:

DNC confirmation
provider-approved WhatsApp templates
sensitive compliance messages
Level 1 — Light personalization

AI can adjust:

greeting
business name placement
shortening
channel tone

AI cannot change:

offer angle
CTA
claims
flow URL
pricing language

Use for:

most outreach
Level 2 — Rewrite with guardrails

AI can rewrite structure while preserving allowed claims.

Use for:

reply handling
objection responses
human-approved campaigns

Requires:

message safety check
confidence threshold
possibly human approval
11.23 Message safety check

Before sending, run a safety/guardrail check.

TypeScript
type MessageSafetyCheck = {
  safeToSend: boolean;

  violations: {
    type:
      | "banned_claim"
      | "missing_required_element"
      | "unsupported_claim"
      | "too_aggressive"
      | "policy_risk"
      | "wrong_channel_tone"
      | "missing_unsubscribe"
      | "template_mismatch";

    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
    text?: string;
    explanation: string;
  }[];

  correctedMessage?: string;

  requiresHumanApproval: boolean;
};

Hard block if:

banned claim
missing unsubscribe in email
WhatsApp provider template mismatch
DNC message includes promotional link
unsupported customer-request claim
11.24 Rendering pipeline

The rendering pipeline should be deterministic.

1. Channel Router selects channel + offer angle.
2. Flow Router creates tracking URL.
3. Template Selector chooses template.
4. Variable Resolver fills variables.
5. AI Personalizer adjusts message if allowed.
6. Safety Check validates message.
7. Channel Eligibility re-checks.
8. Message queued/sent/prepared.
9. Message logged.

Pseudo-code:

TypeScript
async function renderGrowthMessage(input: RenderGrowthMessageInput) {
  const template = await selectTemplate(input);

  assertTemplateUsable(template, input.channel, input.sendMode);

  const variables = await resolveTemplateVariables(input);

  const rendered = renderTemplate(template, variables);

  const personalized = template.aiPersonalization.allowed
    ? await personalizeMessageWithAi(rendered, template, input)
    : rendered;

  const safety = await runMessageSafetyCheck(personalized, template, input);

  if (!safety.safeToSend) {
    return {
      status: "blocked",
      safety,
    };
  }

  return {
    status: "ready",
    message: safety.correctedMessage ?? personalized,
    templateId: template.id,
    variables,
    safety,
  };
}
11.25 Template selection logic

Inputs:

TypeScript
type TemplateSelectionInput = {
  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";
  sendMode:
    | "auto_send"
    | "assisted_send"
    | "template_required"
    | "reply_only"
    | "human_review";

  offerAngle: OfferAngle["id"];

  messageType:
    | "cold_initial"
    | "follow_up_1"
    | "follow_up_2"
    | "reply_to_question"
    | "send_onboarding_link"
    | "clicked_not_started"
    | "started_not_completed"
    | "reactivation"
    | "dnc_confirmation";

  campaignId?: string;
  experimentId?: string;
  variantId?: string;
};

Selection order:

1. If experiment variant forces template, use that if eligible.
2. If WhatsApp API template_required, select provider_approved template.
3. Select active template matching channel + offerAngle + messageType.
4. Prefer template with strongest completion performance for segment.
5. Fallback to default template family.
6. If no template exists, route to human review.
11.26 Provider template handling for WhatsApp

WhatsApp API templates need exact provider-approved structure.

For those templates:

AI rewrite disabled
variables limited to provider-approved placeholders
message body must match approved provider template
buttons/URLs must match allowed structure

Schema extension:

TypeScript
type WhatsAppProviderTemplate = {
  metaTemplateName: string;
  language: string;
  category: "marketing" | "utility" | "authentication";

  components: {
    type: "HEADER" | "BODY" | "FOOTER" | "BUTTONS";
    text?: string;
    variables?: string[];
  }[];

  providerStatus:
    | "draft"
    | "submitted"
    | "approved"
    | "rejected"
    | "paused";

  lastSyncedAt?: Date;
};

Do not use WhatsApp API send if:

providerStatus !== approved

Assisted WhatsApp can use internal templates, but should still pass safety checks.

11.27 Email footer / unsubscribe

Email template should include:

{{unsubscribe_footer}}

Example footer:

To stop receiving messages from MenuList, reply “unsubscribe” or click here: {{unsubscribe_url}}.

If you add a physical address later, keep it in a central footer block.

The FTC CAN-SPAM guide requires commercial email to avoid deceptive headers/subject lines and provide recipients a way to opt out, so this should be enforced at template-render time rather than left to the AI.

11.33 Versioning

Never edit an approved template in place.

Use:

templateId base + version

Example:

wa_menu_link_qr_initial_v1
wa_menu_link_qr_initial_v2

Rules:

approved templates are immutable
new changes create new version
old versions remain for attribution
deprecated versions not used for new sends
historical messages retain template version

This is necessary for experiment accuracy and debugging.

11.38 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — AI invents claims

Fix:

allowed/banned claim lists

structured output

Failure mode 2 — Too many templates

Fix:

template families
active template cap
deprecate weak variants
Failure mode 3 — High reply rate, low onboarding

Fix:

optimize by onboarding completion, not reply
Failure mode 4 — WhatsApp provider template mismatch

Fix:

disable AI rewrite for provider-approved WhatsApp templates
Failure mode 5 — Email compliance missing

Fix:

required unsubscribe footer enforced at render time
Failure mode 6 — Same message used across all channels

Fix:

channel-specific templates and tone rules

11.40 Final principle

The Message Template System should make outreach scalable without making it generic or risky.

The system should not let AI randomly “write a message.”

It should say:

This lead has this offer angle.
This channel requires this tone and policy.
This approved template family fits.
These variables are safe.
This AI personalization is allowed.
This safety check passed.
This message can now be sent, queued, or approved.

That is how MenuList gets high-volume AI-assisted messaging without sacrificing trust, compliance, or attribution.
````
