The Objection Handler may call:

getApprovedObjectionResponses()
getPricingPolicy()
getExamplePolicy()

getConversationSummary()
getAvailableOnboardingRoute()

It may not call:

sendMessage()
createSuppression()
changePricing()
modifyOnboardingFlow()
changeLeadScore()

It can recommend actions only.

17.29 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — AI invents pricing

Fix:

pricing policy gate
human review when unconfigured
guardrail blocks price claims
Failure mode 2 — AI argues with negative lead

Fix:

negative/DNC response library
no-pitch DNC rule
Failure mode 3 — AI sends link after DNC

Fix:

DNC hard block
suppression before message generation
Failure mode 4 — AI over-explains

Fix:

channel-specific length limits
short approved responses
Failure mode 5 — AI makes creepy claims

Fix:

source-data leakage guardrail
banned claim detector
Failure mode 6 — AI routes product issue incorrectly

Fix:

onboarding_issue → product/support handoff or human review

17.31 Final principle

The Objection Handler should make the Growth Engine feel responsive without becoming pushy or unsafe.

It should turn:

random replies
pricing questions
not interested messages
wrong numbers
trust concerns
setup questions

into:

approved response
safe next action
correct suppression
or human review

The rule is simple:

Answer clearly when safe.
Route when interested.
Suppress when asked.
Escalate when uncertain.
Never argue.
Never invent.

Spec 18 — Next-Best-Action Engine
18.1 Purpose

The Next-Best-Action Engine decides what should happen next for every lead, conversation, campaign, and promotion.

It answers:

What should the Growth Engine do now?
Should we message?
Should we wait?
Should we follow up?
Should we change channel?
Should we route to onboarding?
Should we suppress?
Should a human review?
Should we enrich the lead?
Should we stop?

This is the operational brain of the system.

The AI Channel Router answers:

Where should we message this lead?

The Objection Handler answers:

How should we respond to this objection?

The Next-Best-Action Engine answers:

Given everything that has happened so far, what is the highest-leverage next step?
18.2 Core principle

The system should not run as a static sequence like:

message 1
→ wait 3 days
→ message 2
→ wait 7 days
→ message 3

That is too crude.

Instead, it should be event-driven:

lead imported
lead scored
message sent
message replied
message clicked
email bounced
WhatsApp wrong number
Instagram window expiring
onboarding started
onboarding dropped
DNC received
campaign risk increased

Every event can change the next best action.

The engine should continuously decide:

best action now, based on current state

not blindly execute pre-written sequences.

18.3 What this engine owns

The Next-Best-Action Engine owns:

next action recommendations
action prioritization
follow-up timing
channel switching decisions
retargeting decisions
lead hold/wait decisions
human review routing
suppression recommendations
enrichment recommendations
onboarding route recommendations
campaign pause recommendations
action queues
action scheduling

It does not own:

message content
actual sending
channel eligibility rules
lead scoring
pricing policy
onboarding UX
product activation
MenuList product workflows

It orchestrates actions using outputs from other systems.

18.4 Position in the system

The Next-Best-Action Engine sits above the execution and inbox layers.

Lead Source
→ AI Lead Intelligence
→ Channel Identity Registry
→ Channel Eligibility Engine
→ AI Channel Router
→ Message Template / Guardrails
→ Channel Execution
→ Unified Inbox
→ Reply Classifier
→ Objection Handler
→ Next-Best-Action Engine
→ Action Queues

It consumes all system events and decides what should happen next.

18.5 Core input

The engine needs a complete lead/conversation context.

TypeScript
type NextBestActionInput = {
  leadId: string;

  lead: {
    status: GrowthLeadStatus;
    segment?: "A" | "B" | "C" | "REJECT";
    score?: number;
    riskScore?: number;

    business: {
      name: string;
      category?: string;
      city?: string;
      area?: string;
      scale?: string;
    };
  };

  intelligence: {
    totalScore?: number;
    needScore?: number;
    contactabilityScore?: number;
    intentScore?: number;
    riskScore?: number;
    primaryNeed?: string;
    recommendedAction?: string;
    confidence?: number;
  };

  identities: ChannelIdentityContract;

  eligibility: EligibilityContract;

  conversations: ConversationContract[];

  latestMessage?: MessageContract;

  latestReplyClassification?: FinalInboundClassification;

  latestObjectionDecision?: FinalObjectionHandlingDecision;

  onboardingFeedback?: {
    currentState:
      | "not_routed"
      | "routed"
      | "clicked"
      | "started"
      | "dropped"
      | "completed"
      | "converted";

    flowId?: string;
    routeId?: string;
    lastEventAt?: Date;
    dropStep?: string;
    dropReason?: string;
  };

  campaignContext?: {
    campaignId?: string;
    goal?:
      | "cold_acquisition"
      | "promotion"
      | "retargeting"
      | "reactivation"
      | "inbound_response";

    allowedActions?: NextBestActionType[];
    blockedActions?: NextBestActionType[];
    maxFollowUps?: number;
    cooldownRules?: CooldownRule[];
    experimentId?: string;
    variantId?: string;
  };

  history: {
    outboundCount: number;
    inboundCount: number;
    followUpCount: number;

    lastContactedAt?: Date;
    lastInboundAt?: Date;
    lastClickedAt?: Date;
    lastRoutedAt?: Date;
    lastOnboardingStartedAt?: Date;
    lastOnboardingCompletedAt?: Date;
    lastNegativeAt?: Date;

    previousChannelsUsed: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger")[];
    previousOfferAnglesUsed: OfferAngle[];
    previousFlowIdsUsed: string[];
  };

  policy: {
    isSuppressed: boolean;
    suppressionReason?: string;
    canContact: boolean;
    reasonIfBlocked?: string;
  };

  now: Date;
};
18.6 Core output

The engine returns one primary next action, plus optional fallback actions.

type NextBestActionOutput = {
  leadId: string;

  action:
    | "send_initial_message"
    | "send_follow_up"
    | "reply_to_inbound"
    | "send_onboarding_flow"
    | "change_channel"

    | "retarget_started_not_completed"

    | "suppress_lead"
    | "mark_not_interested"

    | "reject_lead";

    | "auto_send"
    | "assisted_send"

    | "hold"
    | "blocked";

  };

    reason: string;
  };

    offerAngle?: OfferAngle;

  };

  message?: {
    templateFamily?: string;

      | "cold_initial"
      | "follow_up_1"
      | "follow_up_2"

      | "send_onboarding_link"
      | "clicked_not_started"

  }[];

  reasoning: string[];

  riskFlags: {
    type: string;
    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
    reason: string;
  }[];

  confidence: number;

  generatedAt: Date;
  aiRunId?: string;
};
18.7 Action taxonomy

Use a fixed action taxonomy.

TypeScript
type NextBestActionType =
  | "send_initial_message"
  | "send_follow_up"
  | "reply_to_inbound"
  | "send_onboarding_flow"
  | "change_channel"
  | "route_to_onboarding"
  | "resume_onboarding"
  | "retarget_clicked_not_started"
  | "retarget_started_not_completed"
  | "enrich_lead"
  | "human_review"
  | "suppress_lead"
  | "mark_not_interested"
  | "close_conversation"
  | "wait"
  | "reject_lead";

The system should not let AI invent new action labels. New labels require system-level schema changes.

18.8 Action meanings
send_initial_message

Use when:

lead is qualified
lead is ready to contact
no prior outbound exists
eligible channel exists
campaign allows contact

Example:

A-score cafe, email and WhatsApp available, no prior outreach.
send_follow_up

Use when:

lead was contacted
no reply yet
follow-up is due
max follow-up count not reached
channel eligible
not suppressed

Example:

Email sent 3 days ago, no click/reply, follow-up 1 due.
reply_to_inbound

Use when:

lead sent inbound message
classifier/objection handler produced reply path
channel response window is active or email reply is allowed

Example:

Instagram DM says “send details”.
send_onboarding_flow

Use when:

lead is interested
lead asks for link
lead asks how to start
lead is warm enough to route
flow router selected existing flow

This action sends a tracked link to an existing MenuList onboarding flow.

change_channel

Use when:

primary channel failed
email bounced
WhatsApp wrong number
Instagram/Messenger window expired
no reply after follow-ups
better eligible channel exists

Example:

Email bounced, but phone exists → prepare WhatsApp assisted.
route_to_onboarding

Use when:

lead should be routed into existing flow
route needs to be created/reused
message may or may not be sent yet

This is often a precursor to send_onboarding_flow.

resume_onboarding

Use when:

lead started onboarding
flow supports resume
lead dropped or did not complete
resume link exists or can be generated
retarget_clicked_not_started

Use when:

lead clicked a Growth Engine link
no onboarding_started event arrived within configured delay
lead not suppressed
channel eligible
retarget_started_not_completed

Use when:

lead started onboarding
no completion
drop event exists or time threshold passed
enrich_lead

Use when:

lead seems relevant
contact identity is weak or missing
best channel unavailable
enrichment could improve route

Example:

Good restaurant lead, website exists, no email/phone → run website contact extraction.
human_review

Use when:

low confidence
pricing question without policy
angry reply
DNC ambiguity
identity conflict
policy uncertainty
high-value lead
suppress_lead

Use when:

DNC
complaint
unsubscribe
wrong contact
global/manual suppression condition

Scope depends on context:

global
channel
identity
campaign
mark_not_interested

Use when:

lead says not interested
lead says not now
lead declines without DNC

This usually triggers a cooldown, not necessarily permanent suppression.

close_conversation

Use when:

conversation is resolved
max follow-ups reached
lead converted
wrong contact handled
no further action
wait

Use when:

not enough time has passed
window/cooldown active
campaign paused
lead is not high priority
reject_lead

Use when:

wrong vertical
duplicate
closed business
no contact path and low score
suppression/risk makes it unusable
18.9 Decision priority order

The engine should evaluate actions in this order.

1. Suppression / DNC / complaint
2. Wrong contact / identity invalidation
3. Inbound message needing reply
4. Interested lead needing onboarding route/link
5. Onboarding started but not completed
6. Clicked but not started
7. Follow-up due
8. Initial outreach
9. Enrichment needed
10. Wait / hold / close

This prevents the system from doing dumb things like sending a follow-up to someone who just said “don’t contact me.”

18.10 Hard action rules

These override AI.

DNC
If DNC or global suppression → suppress_lead.

No follow-up. No channel switch. No onboarding link.

Unsubscribe
If email unsubscribe → suppress email identity.

If wording is broad, escalate to global suppression.

Wrong number
If wrong number → suppress phone/WhatsApp identity.

Do not suppress full lead unless necessary.

Converted
If converted → close acquisition conversations and suppress acquisition outreach.
Rejected / duplicate
If lead is rejected or duplicate → no outreach.
No eligible channel
If no channel eligible → enrich, hold, or human_review.
Pricing ambiguity
If lead asks price and no pricing policy → human_review.
Angry / complaint
human_review or suppress depending classifier confidence and policy.
18.11 Priority scoring

Every next action gets a priority score.

Priority Score =
  Lead Value
+ Intent Strength
+ Time Urgency
+ Conversion Proximity
+ Channel Window Urgency
+ Campaign Priority
- Risk Penalty

Suggested weights:

Lead value:              20
Intent strength:         25
Time urgency:            15
Conversion proximity:    20
Channel window urgency:  10
Campaign priority:       10
Risk penalty:           -30 max
Priority levels
0–39: low
40–64: normal
65–84: high
85–100: urgent
Urgent examples
DNC needs suppression
A-score lead asks “send link”
Instagram/Messenger window expiring soon
lead started onboarding and asked for help
angry/complaint reply
High examples
interested reply
clicked but not started
started but not completed
price question from A lead
Normal examples
follow-up due
B lead awaiting first outreach
email reply with generic question
Low examples
C lead
cold no-reply not yet due
weak lead needing enrichment
18.12 Timing logic

Every action needs execution timing.

TypeScript
type ActionTiming = {
  executeAt: Date;
  expiresAt?: Date;
  reason: string;
};

Examples:

Immediate
DNC suppression
interested reply
active-window social reply
pricing/human-review escalation
Delayed
follow-up after 48–72 hours
retarget click-not-started after 24–48 hours
reactivation after cooldown
Wait
cooldown active
too soon after last contact
campaign paused
channel cap reached

Timing should be configurable per campaign/channel.

18.13 Follow-up policy

The engine should not spam.

Default follow-up logic:

initial message
→ follow-up 1 after 2–3 days if no reply/click/start
→ follow-up 2 after 5–7 days if still no reply/start
→ close or cooldown

But event-driven overrides:

clicked but did not start → softer retarget
started but did not complete → help/continue message
replied → no generic follow-up
negative → stop
DNC → suppress

Recommended default:

TypeScript
type FollowUpPolicy = {
  maxFollowUps: 2;

  initialNoReplyDelayHours: 72;
  secondNoReplyDelayHours: 168;

  clickedNotStartedDelayHours: 24;
  startedNotCompletedDelayHours: 24;

  notInterestedCooldownDays: 60;
  noReplyCooldownDays: 30;
};
18.14 Retargeting buckets

The engine should create retargeting states.

TypeScript
type RetargetingBucket =
  | "clicked_not_started"
  | "started_not_completed"
  | "replied_not_routed"
  | "asked_price_not_started"
  | "interested_no_click"
  | "not_now_cooldown"
  | "no_reply_after_followups"
  | "reactivation_candidate";

Each bucket maps to an action.

Bucket	Default action
clicked_not_started	soft follow-up
started_not_completed	resume/help message
replied_not_routed	send onboarding flow
asked_price_not_started	pricing answer/human review
interested_no_click	resend link or change channel
not_now_cooldown	wait
no_reply_after_followups	close/cooldown
reactivation_candidate	reactivation message
18.15 Channel-switch logic

Changing channel should be deliberate.

Switch from email to WhatsApp if
email bounced
email no reply after follow-ups
lead is A-score
phone/WhatsApp identity strong
WhatsApp eligible
campaign allows assisted send
Switch from WhatsApp to email if
WhatsApp wrong number
WhatsApp not sent
operator skipped
no reply and email exists
WhatsApp cap reached
Switch from Instagram/Messenger to email/WhatsApp if
social window expired
lead shared email/phone
lead asked for details but no active window
Stay on same channel if
lead recently replied there
active conversation window exists
lead asks a direct question
channel is converting

The engine should prioritize continuity when there is active intent.

18.16 Lead enrichment action

enrich_lead should be recommended only when there is a reason.

Good enrichment cases:

A/B fit score
no usable channel
website exists but email/phone missing
Instagram profile likely exists
manual high-value lead
source data incomplete

Bad enrichment cases:

C/Reject lead
suppressed lead
wrong vertical
large chain not targeted
already converted

Enrichment types:

website_contact_extraction
social_identity_lookup
secondary_provider_lookup
manual_review

The engine should include:

TypeScript
enrichment?: {
  types: string[];
  maxCostUsd?: number;
  reason: string;
};
18.17 Human review action

human_review should be specific, not generic.

Review reasons:

low_ai_confidence
pricing_question
angry_reply
dnc_ambiguous
identity_conflict
policy_uncertain
high_value_lead
large_chain
message_safety_warning
wrong_business
onboarding_problem

Output should include:

what human should decide
suggested options

Example:

JSON
{
  "action": "human_review",
  "priority": {
    "level": "urgent",
    "score": 92,
    "reasons": ["Lead asked pricing; no approved pricing policy configured."]
  },

18.18 Wait action

wait is a valid action.

Use when:

too soon after last message
campaign/channel cap reached
cooldown active
lead score low
no action is better than spam
waiting for onboarding event
waiting for reply window

Every wait action should include:

until when
what trigger should wake it up

Example:

TypeScript
timing: {
  executeAt: addHours(now, 48),
  reason: "Wait 48h after flow link click before retargeting."
}
18.19 Close conversation action

Use when no further action is useful.

Close reasons:

converted
onboarding_completed
not_interested
do_not_contact
wrong_contact
no_reply_after_followups
campaign_ended
superseded_by_other_channel
manual_close

Closing a conversation does not delete history.

It removes it from active queues.

18.23 Action status lifecycle
queued
→ ready
→ in_progress
→ completed

Alternative states:

waiting
cancelled
failed
expired

Examples:

follow-up due next week → waiting
DNC arrived before follow-up → cancelled
message generation failed → failed
social window expired → expired

The system should cancel stale or invalid actions automatically.

18.24 Action cancellation rules

Cancel pending actions if:

lead suppressed
lead converted
conversation closed
channel becomes blocked
identity becomes invalid
campaign paused
better action supersedes it
follow-up no longer relevant

Example:

follow-up queued for tomorrow
lead replies today
→ cancel follow-up
→ create reply_to_inbound action

This is essential for not sending dumb follow-ups.

18.25 Action deduplication

Avoid duplicate actions.

Deduplicate by:

leadId
conversationId
action
channel
executeAt time window
campaignId

Examples:

Do not create three follow-up actions for same lead.
Do not create multiple send_onboarding_flow actions after one inbound reply.
Do not create multiple human_review items for same unresolved issue.

Use idempotency keys:

nba:{leadId}:{conversationId}:{action}:{triggerEventId}
18.26 Next-best-action algorithm

Use hybrid rules + AI.

1. Load current state.
2. Apply hard blocks.
3. Check high-priority event types.
4. Generate possible actions.
5. Score possible actions.
6. Remove ineligible actions.
7. Choose best action.
8. Build fallback plan.
9. Queue action or execute if low-risk.
10. Log decision.

Pseudo-code:

TypeScript
async function decideNextBestAction(input: NextBestActionInput) {
  const hard = runHardActionRules(input);

  if (hard) return hard;

  const candidates = generateCandidateActions(input);

  const eligibleCandidates = candidates.filter(candidate =>
    passesActionEligibility(candidate, input)
  );

  if (eligibleCandidates.length === 0) {
    return buildWaitOrHumanReview(input);
  }

  const scored = scoreActions(eligibleCandidates, input);

  const best = selectHighestValueAction(scored);

  const output = await refineWithAiIfNeeded(best, input);

  const validated = validateNextBestAction(output, input);

  await queueOrApplyAction(validated);

  return validated;
}

AI should refine/reason, not override hard rules.

Candidate actions come from current state.

If email bounced

Candidates:

human_review
If wrong number

Candidates:

change_channel
enrich_lead
close_conversation
If no reply and follow-up due

18.28 Action scoring

Each candidate action gets a score.

Action Score =
  Expected Conversion Lift
+ Intent Alignment
+ Lead Value
+ Timing Urgency
+ Channel Feasibility
+ Learning Value
- Risk Penalty
- Cost Penalty

Suggested weights:

Expected conversion lift: 30
Intent alignment:         20
Lead value:               15
Timing urgency:           15
Channel feasibility:      10
Learning value:            5
Cost penalty:             -5
Risk penalty:            -30 max

The highest score wins, unless hard rules override.

18.29 Expected conversion lift

The engine should eventually estimate:

P(onboarding_completed | action, lead, channel, flow, template)

Early system can use heuristic weights.

Long-term, use historical performance:

lead segment
source
channel
offer angle
template
onboarding flow
intent stage

Example:

A-score WhatsApp interested lead asking for link:
send_onboarding_flow has high expected lift.

C-score cold lead after two no-replies:
send_follow_up has low expected lift.
18.30 Campaign context

Next-best-action should respect campaign rules.

Campaign may specify:

allowed actions
blocked actions
max follow-ups
allowed channels
target onboarding flow
cooldown policy
experiment assignment
stop rules

If campaign says:

no WhatsApp follow-ups

NBA cannot choose WhatsApp follow-up.

If campaign says:

max 2 follow-ups

NBA must close/wait after follow-up 2.

18.31 Experiment integration

NBA can assign or respect experiments.

Example:

Clicked-not-started retargeting:
Variant A: email follow-up
Variant B: WhatsApp assisted follow-up
Variant C: wait 48h

NBA must record:

experimentId
variantId
action chosen
outcome

Hard rules override experiments.

Example:

experiment wants WhatsApp follow-up
eligibility blocks WhatsApp
→ choose fallback or exclude lead from variant
18.32 Human approval levels

Each action has an autonomy level.

TypeScript
type ActionAutonomyLevel =
  | "suggest_only"
  | "draft_only"
  | "queue_for_approval"
  | "auto_execute_with_guardrails"
  | "auto_execute";

Recommended defaults:

Action	Default autonomy
send_initial_message email	auto_execute_with_guardrails
send_initial_message WhatsApp	queue_for_approval
reply_to_inbound simple	auto_execute_with_guardrails
reply_to_inbound pricing	queue_for_approval
send_onboarding_flow interested lead	auto/approval depending channel
suppress_lead DNC exact	auto_execute
suppress_lead ambiguous	queue_for_approval
change_channel	queue_for_approval or auto for email fallback
human_review	auto queue
enrich_lead	auto_execute_with_guardrails
close_conversation after max follow-ups	auto_execute_with_guardrails

18.36 AI prompt contract

System instruction summary:

You choose the next best acquisition action for MenuList Growth Engine.
You must optimize for completed existing MenuList onboarding, not replies or message volume.
You must respect suppression, eligibility, channel policy, campaign caps, and lead status.
You cannot send messages, create suppressions, or modify onboarding.
You output one primary action and optional fallbacks.
Return only valid JSON.

18.41 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — NBA sends follow-up after DNC

Fix:

hard suppression rule
pre-execution eligibility re-check
pending action cancellation
Failure mode 2 — NBA over-follows up

Fix:

max follow-up policy
cooldowns
negative-rate monitoring
Failure mode 3 — NBA optimizes for clicks

Fix:

reward onboarding completion, not clicks
Failure mode 4 — NBA ignores channel windows

Fix:

eligibility contract required
channel window urgency scoring
Failure mode 5 — NBA creates duplicate actions

Fix:

action idempotency keys
pending-action dedupe
Failure mode 6 — NBA fails to act on interested leads

Fix:

urgent priority for interested/send_link intents
inbox SLA alerts
Failure mode 7 — NBA routes everything to human

Fix:

improve classifier confidence
approved response library
more auto-action rules

18.43 Final principle

The Next-Best-Action Engine is what makes the Growth Engine adaptive.

Without it, the system becomes:

static sequences
manual follow-ups
missed interested replies
unnecessary messages
late DNC handling
poor retargeting

With it, the system becomes:

event-driven
state-aware
channel-aware
policy-aware
conversion-oriented

The engine’s core question is always:

What action gives this lead the highest chance of completing MenuList onboarding, with the lowest channel risk, given everything we know right now?

Next spec item: Follow-up and retargeting logic.

Spec 19 — Follow-Up and Retargeting Logic
19.1 Purpose

The Follow-Up and Retargeting Logic decides how the Growth Engine continues after the first contact.

It answers:

When should we follow up?
Which channel should we use?
When should we stop?
When should we change channel?
When should we route again to onboarding?
When should we suppress, cool down, or close?

This layer prevents the system from becoming either:

too passive → missed interested leads
too aggressive → spam / channel risk / brand damage

The goal is controlled persistence.

19.2 Core distinction

There are four different actions that people often mix together.

Follow-up

Used after outbound contact when there is no meaningful response.

Example:

Email sent → no reply after 3 days → send follow-up.
Retargeting

Used after the lead showed some behavior but did not complete the desired action.

Example:

Clicked onboarding link → did not start → send soft reminder.
Recovery

Used when the lead started an existing MenuList onboarding flow but did not complete.

Example:

Onboarding started → dropped → send resume/help message.
Reactivation

Used after an old lead went cold and a cooldown period has passed.

Example:

Lead replied “not now” 60 days ago → retry softly.

These should be separate because the message, timing, and channel strategy are different.

19.3 What this layer owns

It owns:

follow-up timing
retargeting buckets
cooldown logic
max-contact rules
channel switching after no reply
clicked-not-started recovery
started-not-completed recovery
old-lead reactivation
follow-up suppression checks
follow-up campaign rules
follow-up performance measurement

It does not own:

message generation
channel eligibility
lead scoring
onboarding UX
product onboarding state
menu creation
pricing
final message sending

It produces recommended actions. Execution still goes through:

Eligibility Engine
Message Templates
Message Guardrails
Channel Execution
19.4 Core principle

Follow-up should be state-based, not sequence-based.

Bad:

Day 0 message
Day 3 follow-up
Day 7 follow-up
Day 14 follow-up

Better:

What happened after the first message?
- no reply
- clicked
- replied
- asked price
- started onboarding
- dropped
- DNC
- wrong number

Each state gets a different response.

The system should not blindly follow up if the lead has moved to another state.

19.5 Main retargeting buckets

Use these buckets:

TypeScript
type RetargetingBucket =
  | "no_reply_after_initial"
  | "no_reply_after_followup_1"
  | "clicked_not_started"
  | "replied_not_routed"
  | "interested_no_click"
  | "asked_price_not_started"
  | "started_not_completed"
  | "onboarding_dropped"
  | "not_now_cooldown"
  | "no_reply_after_max_followups"
  | "reactivation_candidate"
  | "channel_failed"
  | "wrong_contact"
  | "suppressed";

Each bucket should map to one preferred next action.

19.6 Bucket definitions and default actions
no_reply_after_initial

Condition:

initial outbound sent
no reply
no click
no onboarding start
follow-up 1 due

Default action:

send_follow_up

Recommended timing:

48–72 hours after initial message

Channel:

same channel or backup channel depending performance
no_reply_after_followup_1

Condition:

initial + follow-up 1 sent
no reply
no click
no onboarding start
follow-up 2 due

Default action:

send_final_follow_up

Recommended timing:

5–7 days after first message

Then stop.

clicked_not_started

Condition:

flow link clicked
no onboarding_started event after configured delay

Default action:

retarget_clicked_not_started

Recommended timing:

24–48 hours after click

Message tone:

soft reminder

Do not say:

I saw you clicked.

Say:

Sharing the setup link again in case useful:
{{flow_url}}
replied_not_routed

Condition:

lead replied positively or asked details
but no onboarding route/link has been sent

Default action:

send_onboarding_flow

Timing:

immediate

Priority:

high or urgent

This is one of the most valuable buckets.

interested_no_click

Condition:

lead was sent onboarding flow link
lead seemed interested
but did not click

Default action:

soft follow-up or change channel

Timing:

24–72 hours depending channel
asked_price_not_started

Condition:

lead asked pricing/free question
answer was sent or human handled
but onboarding did not start

Default action:

pricing-specific follow-up

or:

human review

Do not automate pricing follow-up unless pricing policy is configured.

started_not_completed

Condition:

onboarding_started event exists
no onboarding_completed event after threshold

Default action:

resume_onboarding or help_complete_onboarding

Timing:

12–24 hours after drop/stall

Message:

Sharing the setup link again in case useful:
{{flow_url}}

If resume is supported:

Continue here:
{{resume_url}}
onboarding_dropped

Condition:

product emits onboarding_dropped event

Default action:

help message, resume route, alternate flow, or human review

If drop step is known:

tailor help message without sounding creepy

Avoid:

We saw you dropped at step X.

Use:

Sharing the setup link again in case you need it.
not_now_cooldown

Condition:

lead said “not now” or similar

Default action:

cooldown

Recommended cooldown:

30–90 days depending campaign

No immediate follow-up unless they re-engage.

no_reply_after_max_followups

Condition:

max follow-ups reached
no reply/click/start

Default action:

close_conversation

Optional:

reactivation_candidate after cooldown
reactivation_candidate

Condition:

old lead
not suppressed
cooldown expired
still potentially valuable
new campaign/message/offer available

Default action:

reactivation message

Use a low-pressure tone.

channel_failed

Condition:

email bounced
WhatsApp wrong number
provider failure
template blocked
social window expired

Default action:

change_channel

or:

suppress_identity

depending on failure.

wrong_contact

Condition:

wrong number / wrong email / wrong business

Default action:

suppress identity

Then:

enrich lead if lead still valuable
suppressed

Condition:

DNC / complaint / unsubscribe / global block

Default action:

no action
cancel pending actions
close conversations
19.7 Follow-up policy object

Use a configurable policy per campaign.

TypeScript
type FollowUpPolicy = {
  id: string;

  campaignId?: string;

  maxFollowUps: number;

  timing: {
    initialNoReplyFollowUpHours: number;
    secondNoReplyFollowUpHours: number;

    clickedNotStartedDelayHours: number;
    interestedNoClickDelayHours: number;
    startedNotCompletedDelayHours: number;

    notNowCooldownDays: number;
    noReplyCooldownDays: number;
    reactivationCooldownDays: number;
  };

  channelRules: {
    allowEmailFollowUp: boolean;
    allowWhatsAppFollowUp: boolean;
    allowInstagramFollowUp: boolean;
    allowMessengerFollowUp: boolean;

    allowChannelSwitch: boolean;

    preferredFallbackOrder: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger")[];
  };

  stopRules: {
    stopOnReply: boolean;
    stopOnClick?: boolean;
    stopOnOnboardingStart: boolean;
    stopOnOnboardingCompletion: boolean;
    stopOnNegative: boolean;
    stopOnDnc: boolean;
    stopOnWrongContact: boolean;
    stopOnMaxFollowUps: boolean;
  };

  riskControls: {
    maxNegativeRate?: number;
    maxDncRate?: number;
    maxBounceRate?: number;
  };

  status: "active" | "paused" | "deprecated";

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};

Default recommendation:

maxFollowUps = 2
initial follow-up = 72h
second follow-up = 7d
clicked-not-started = 24–48h
started-not-completed = 24h
not-now cooldown = 60d
no-reply cooldown = 30–60d
19.8 Channel-specific follow-up rules
Email

Email can handle more automated follow-up.

Use for:

cold no-reply follow-up
clicked-not-started retargeting
reactivation
backup after WhatsApp not sent

Default:

auto-send allowed if eligibility and guardrails pass

Stop if:

unsubscribe
bounce
complaint
DNC
WhatsApp

WhatsApp follow-up should be more conservative.

Use for:

A-score leads
interested leads
reply continuation
manual/assisted follow-up
high-value retargeting

Default:

assisted or template-based

Avoid:

bulk repeated WhatsApp follow-ups

Stop immediately on:

wrong number
DNC
negative reply
no response after configured limit
Instagram DM

Use follow-up mainly when:

lead initiated conversation
active response window exists
lead asked for details
lead clicked but did not start and IG is still eligible

Do not use Instagram as generic cold retargeting.

Default:

reply-only / warm only
Messenger

Same as Instagram.

Use when:

lead came through Facebook/Page/Messenger
conversation window is active
lead is warm

Default:

reply-only / warm only
19.9 Channel switching rules

Follow-up should sometimes switch channels.

Email → WhatsApp

Switch if:

email no reply after follow-up
lead is A-score
phone/WhatsApp identity is strong
WhatsApp eligible
campaign allows WhatsApp assisted
WhatsApp → Email

Switch if:

WhatsApp not sent
wrong number
no reply after assisted outreach
email exists and eligible
WhatsApp cap reached
Instagram/Messenger → Email/WhatsApp

Switch if:

social window expired
lead shared phone/email
lead is interested but cannot be replied to on social
Stay on same channel

Stay if:

lead replied there recently
conversation window active
lead has clear intent
channel is performing well

Rule:

continuity beats channel switching when there is active intent.
19.10 Follow-up message families

Use specific template families:

no_reply_followup
final_followup
clicked_not_started
started_not_completed
reactivation
price_followup
channel_switch_followup
No-reply follow-up
Hi {{business_name}}, sharing the MenuList setup link again in case useful:

{{flow_url}}
Final follow-up
Last message from my side. If you want to set up a clean MenuList menu link + QR later, you can use this link:

{{flow_url}}
Clicked-not-started
Sharing the MenuList setup link again in case useful:

{{flow_url}}
Started-not-completed
Sharing the MenuList setup link again in case you need it:

{{flow_url}}
Reactivation
Sharing the MenuList setup link again in case it’s useful for your restaurant:

{{flow_url}}

Keep follow-ups shorter than initial messages.

19.11 What follow-ups must not say

Never say:

I saw you clicked
You abandoned the form
Why didn’t you complete
Last chance
Limited time
Your competitors are joining
You are losing customers
We noticed your website/menu issue

Use soft language:

sharing again
in case useful
no problem
last message from my side

Follow-ups should reduce friction, not pressure.

19.12 Retargeting event triggers

Retargeting triggers come from events.

message_clicked
flow_link_clicked
onboarding_started
onboarding_dropped
onboarding_not_completed_after_threshold
reply_classified_interested
price_question_answered
email_bounced
wrong_number
window_expired
cooldown_expired

Each trigger can create or update a growthActionQueue item.

19.13 Retargeting action object
TypeScript
type RetargetingAction = {
  id: string;

  leadId: string;
  conversationId?: string;

  bucket: RetargetingBucket;

  action:
    | "send_follow_up"
    | "send_onboarding_flow"
    | "resume_onboarding"
    | "change_channel"
    | "wait"
    | "human_review"
    | "close"
    | "suppress_identity";

  channel?: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  executeAt: Date;
  expiresAt?: Date;

  reason: string;

  priority: {
    level: "low" | "normal" | "high" | "urgent";
    score: number;
  };

  status:
    | "scheduled"
    | "ready"
    | "completed"
    | "cancelled"
    | "expired";

  createdFromEventId?: string;

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};

This can be represented as a specialized growthActionQueue item.

19.14 Follow-up deduplication

Do not create duplicate follow-ups.

Dedupe key:

leadId + conversationId + bucket + campaignId

Rules:

one active follow-up per conversation per bucket
cancel old follow-up if lead replies
cancel old follow-up if onboarding starts
cancel old follow-up if suppression created
cancel old follow-up if campaign paused

Example:

Lead clicked link.
clicked_not_started follow-up scheduled.
Lead starts onboarding before follow-up fires.
→ cancel follow-up.
19.15 Stop rules

Stop all follow-up if:

DNC
complaint
unsubscribe for email
wrong number for that channel
onboarding completed
converted
global suppression
campaign stopped
max follow-ups reached
manual stop

Stop channel-specific follow-up if:

email bounced
WhatsApp wrong number
Instagram/Messenger window expired
identity suppressed
channel account unhealthy

Stop does not always mean suppress globally.

19.16 Cooldown rules

Use cooldowns to avoid over-contacting.

TypeScript
type CooldownRule = {
  reason:
    | "not_interested"
    | "not_now"
    | "no_reply_after_followups"
    | "low_intent"
    | "campaign_pause"
    | "manual_cooldown";

  durationDays: number;

  scope:
    | "lead"
    | "channel"
    | "campaign"
    | "identity";

  canOverrideWithInbound: boolean;
};

Recommended defaults:

not_now: 60 days
not_interested: 90 days or suppress depending tone
no_reply_after_followups: 30–60 days
low_intent: 30 days
manual cooldown: custom

Inbound reply should usually override cooldown.

DNC never expires unless manually removed by admin.

19.17 Follow-up eligibility check

Before executing any follow-up:

lead not suppressed
conversation not closed
channel still eligible
identity still valid
campaign still active
max follow-ups not reached
no newer inbound message
no onboarding start/completion
message guardrails pass
send caps available

If any fail:

cancel or reschedule

This check must happen immediately before sending/preparing.

19.18 Timing by lead state
Cold no reply
Follow-up 1: 72h
Follow-up 2: 7d
Then close/cooldown
Clicked, not started
Retarget: 24–48h
Optional second: 5–7d if high-value
Started, not completed
Recovery: 12–24h
Optional human review for A leads
Asked price
After approved answer: 48–72h if no start
Not now
Cooldown: 60d
Reactivation
After 60–90d
only if lead remains high quality and not suppressed
19.19 Timing by channel
Email
72h follow-up
7d final
30–60d reactivation
WhatsApp
less frequent
manual/assisted
avoid repeated unanswered messages

Suggested:

one WhatsApp follow-up max unless lead replied
Instagram/Messenger
respond while window active
avoid follow-up outside active/warm context

If window expired:

switch channel if eligible
or wait for re-engagement
19.20 Priority scoring for follow-ups
Follow-Up Priority =
  lead score
+ intent strength
+ recency
+ channel window urgency
+ completion proximity
- negative risk
- follow-up count penalty

High priority:

clicked not started
started not completed
interested but no click
A lead asking question
active social window expiring

Low priority:

cold no-reply after first email
B/C lead with no click
old low-score lead
19.21 Reactivation logic

Reactivation should be selective.

Eligible if:

cooldown expired
lead not suppressed
lead segment A or strong B
new offer/message/flow available
source still relevant
channel eligible
no negative/complaint history

Not eligible if:

DNC
complaint
wrong contact only identity
converted
rejected
low score
bad previous negative sentiment

Reactivation message should be soft:

Sharing the MenuList setup link again in case it’s useful for your restaurant:

{{flow_url}}

No urgency.

19.22 Follow-up state on lead

Add compact follow-up summary to lead.

TypeScript
type GrowthLeadFollowUpState = {
  currentBucket?: RetargetingBucket;

  followUpCount: number;
  maxFollowUps: number;

  lastFollowUpAt?: Date;
  nextFollowUpAt?: Date;

  cooldownUntil?: Date;
  cooldownReason?: string;

  stopped: boolean;
  stoppedReason?:
    | "converted"
    | "do_not_contact"
    | "not_interested"
    | "max_followups"
    | "manual_stop"
    | "campaign_paused"
    | "channel_blocked";

  reactivationEligibleAt?: Date;
};

This helps queue filtering.

19.23 Follow-up state on conversation

Conversation-specific follow-up state:

TypeScript
type ConversationFollowUpState = {
  bucket?: RetargetingBucket;

  followUpCount: number;

  nextActionId?: string;

  nextFollowUpAt?: Date;

  lastFollowUpMessageId?: string;

  closedReason?: string;
};

Lead-level state gives overall status. Conversation-level state gives channel-specific follow-up.

19.24 Relationship with NBA Engine

The Next-Best-Action Engine decides if a follow-up should happen.

The Follow-Up Logic provides:

bucket definitions
timing policies
stop rules
cooldowns
channel rules
message families

NBA uses these rules to create action queue items.

So:

Follow-Up Logic = policy and state machine
Next-Best-Action = action selection engine
19.25 Relationship with Channel Router

Follow-up can use the same or different channel.

When bucket requires channel choice, call AI Channel Router again with updated history.

Examples:

no reply after email → router may choose WhatsApp backup
clicked from email → router may choose email again
Instagram window expired → router may choose email/WhatsApp

Do not assume original channel remains best.

19.26 Relationship with Message Templates

Each bucket maps to template families.

TypeScript
type FollowUpTemplateMap = {
  bucket: RetargetingBucket;

  channel: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  templateFamily:
    | "no_reply_followup"
    | "final_followup"
    | "clicked_not_started"
    | "started_not_completed"
    | "reactivation"
    | "price_followup"
    | "channel_switch_followup";
};

Message Generator still renders and guardrails still validate.

19.27 Relationship with onboarding feedback

Existing MenuList onboarding emits:

flow_link_clicked
onboarding_started
onboarding_dropped
onboarding_completed
converted

These events drive retargeting.

Rules:

flow_link_clicked → maybe clicked_not_started after delay
onboarding_started → cancel cold follow-ups
onboarding_dropped → started_not_completed / onboarding_dropped
onboarding_completed → close acquisition follow-up
converted → suppress acquisition outreach

The Growth Engine reacts. It does not control onboarding.

19.28 Follow-up dashboard

Add views:

/admin/growth/followups

Tabs:

Due Now
Scheduled
Clicked Not Started
Started Not Completed
Reactivation
Cooldown
Stopped

Columns:

lead
bucket
channel
next action
execute at
priority
last message
lead score
campaign
reason

Actions:

approve
send now
reschedule
change channel
cancel
suppress
close
19.29 Retargeting dashboard

Add:

/admin/growth/retargeting

Views:

Clicked Not Started
Started Not Completed
Asked Price
Interested No Click
Old Warm Leads
Reactivation Candidates

Metrics:

bucket size
actions sent
onboarding starts
onboarding completions
negative rate
cost per completion

This helps you see where leads leak.

19.30 Follow-up analytics

Track:

follow-ups scheduled
follow-ups sent
follow-ups cancelled
follow-ups skipped
follow-up reply rate
follow-up click rate
follow-up onboarding start rate
follow-up onboarding completion rate
negative rate after follow-up
DNC rate after follow-up
completion rate by bucket
completion rate by follow-up number

Key insight:

If follow-up 2 produces low completion and high negative rate, remove it.

The system should learn where persistence stops being useful.

19.31 Follow-up stop/scale rules
Continue / scale if
follow-up improves onboarding completion
negative rate stays low
DNC rate stays low
cost per completion acceptable
Stop / reduce if
follow-up creates negative replies
completion lift is low
channel health weakens
operators are overloaded

Every follow-up type should justify itself with conversion data.

19.32 Example flows
Example 1 — Cold email no reply
Day 0: email initial sent
Day 3: no reply/click → email follow-up
Day 7: no reply/click → final email
Day 10: close + 45d cooldown
Example 2 — Cold email clicked, not started
Day 0: email sent
Day 1: link clicked
Day 2: no onboarding start → soft reminder
Day 5: still no start → WhatsApp assisted if eligible and A-score
Then close/cooldown
Example 3 — WhatsApp A lead no reply
Day 0: WhatsApp assisted sent
Day 3: no reply → email fallback if available
Day 7: no reply → close/cooldown

Avoid repeated WhatsApp pressure.

Example 4 — Instagram inbound
Inbound DM: “send details”
AI replies with flow link
24h: clicked not started → if window active, soft follow-up
Window expired → switch to email/WhatsApp only if identity available
Example 5 — Started onboarding, dropped
onboarding_started
no completed event after 24h
→ send resume/help message
if high-score and still no completion
→ human review / assisted follow-up
Example 6 — DNC
Inbound: “stop messaging”
→ cancel all pending actions
→ suppress globally
→ send DNC confirmation if appropriate
→ close all conversations

No follow-up ever.

19.33 AI prompt contract for retargeting

If AI is used to decide retargeting action, prompt must state:

You decide follow-up/retargeting action for MenuList Growth Engine.
Optimize for completed onboarding, not replies.
Respect DNC, suppression, max follow-ups, cooldowns, and channel eligibility.
Never recommend follow-up after do-not-contact.
Use soft, non-creepy language for clicked/dropped leads.
Return valid JSON only.

AI must not:

invent urgency
mention click tracking directly
pressure the lead
ignore channel windows
override cooldowns
19.34 Follow-up templates must be softer than initial outreach

Follow-up copy should be:

shorter
less explanatory
less promotional
low-pressure

Never add more selling pressure in later messages.

Better:

Sharing this again in case useful.

Not:

You really should complete this.
19.35 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Follow-up after DNC

Fix:

hard suppression check
pending action cancellation
pre-execution eligibility check
Failure mode 2 — Too many follow-ups

Fix:

max follow-up policy
bucket-level caps
negative-rate monitoring
Failure mode 3 — Creepy retargeting

Fix:

do not mention click/drop tracking
soft copy only
Failure mode 4 — Wrong channel follow-up

Fix:

re-run channel router before retargeting
Failure mode 5 — Retargeting low-quality leads

Fix:

minimum lead score / segment threshold
Failure mode 6 — Follow-up creates negative replies

Fix:

campaign pause thresholds
template performance monitoring
19.36 Final follow-up contract

Every scheduled follow-up/retargeting action should produce:

TypeScript
type FinalFollowUpDecision = {
  leadId: string;
  conversationId?: string;

  bucket: RetargetingBucket;

  action:
    | "send_follow_up"
    | "send_final_follow_up"
    | "retarget_clicked_not_started"
    | "retarget_started_not_completed"
    | "resume_onboarding"
    | "change_channel"
    | "wait"
    | "close"
    | "suppress_identity"
    | "human_review";

  channel?: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

  executeAt: Date;
  expiresAt?: Date;

  templateFamily:
    | "no_reply_followup"
    | "final_followup"
    | "clicked_not_started"
    | "started_not_completed"
    | "reactivation"
    | "price_followup"
    | "channel_switch_followup";

  flowRoute?: {
    routeId?: string;
    flowUrl?: string;
    onboardingFlowId?: string;
  };

  stopConditions: (
    | "reply_received"
    | "flow_clicked"
    | "onboarding_started"
    | "onboarding_completed"
    | "converted"
    | "negative_reply"
    | "do_not_contact"
    | "suppression_created"
    | "campaign_paused"
  )[];

  priority: {
    level: "low" | "normal" | "high" | "urgent";
    score: number;
    reasons: string[];
  };

  requiresHumanApproval: boolean;

  reasoning: string[];

  confidence: number;

  generatedAt: Date;
};
19.37 Final principle

Follow-up and retargeting should make the Growth Engine persistent without making it annoying.

The rule:

Follow up when behavior suggests recoverable intent.
Stop when behavior suggests disinterest or risk.
Switch channels when the current channel fails.
Retarget softly when the lead showed intent.
Never pressure.
Never ignore suppression.
Never optimize for message volume.

The best follow-up system is not the one that sends the most messages.

It is the one that recovers the most onboarding completions with the least channel and brand risk.

Next spec item: Promotion campaign builder.

Spec 20 — Promotion Campaign Builder
20.1 Purpose

The Promotion Campaign Builder is the system for creating, controlling, launching, testing, and learning from acquisition campaigns across:

email
WhatsApp
Instagram DM
Messenger

It lets MenuList run structured lead-acquisition campaigns such as:

Bangalore cafe outreach
Indiranagar dessert shop promotion
Instagram inbound setup campaign
Clicked-but-not-started retargeting
A-score restaurant WhatsApp-assisted campaign
Old warm lead reactivation

It is not a broadcast tool.

It is not a CRM campaign module.

It is not an ads manager replacement.

It is the Growth Engine’s campaign control layer.

20.2 Core principle

A promotion campaign must be a controlled acquisition system.

Every campaign must define:

who we target
why we target them
which channels we use
what offer angle we use
which existing onboarding flow we route to
how much volume is allowed
what AI can do
what humans must approve
what stop rules protect us
what success metric decides scale/pause

The campaign should not be:

select leads
send message
hope

It should be:

audience
→ eligibility
→ AI routing
→ guarded messages
→ channel execution
→ inbox handling
→ onboarding attribution
→ learning loop
20.3 What the campaign builder owns

It owns:

campaign creation
audience definition
segment filters
channel mix
offer angle selection
onboarding flow routing policy
message template selection
experiment setup
send caps
budget caps
AI autonomy level
approval workflow
stop rules
campaign scheduling
campaign status
campaign analytics
campaign recommendations

It does not own:

lead sourcing logic itself
message execution internals
channel provider APIs
onboarding UX
product activation
pricing logic
business verification
MenuList product workflows

It configures and coordinates other systems.

20.4 Campaign types

Use a fixed campaign type taxonomy.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignType =
  | "cold_acquisition"
  | "warm_inbound"
  | "retargeting"
  | "reactivation"
  | "social_inbound"
  | "paid_lead_followup"
  | "local_cluster"
  | "experiment"
  | "manual_priority";
cold_acquisition

For leads sourced from Apify, Outscraper, manual CSV, etc.

Example:

Bangalore cafes with A-score and phone/email.
warm_inbound

For leads who already messaged, replied, clicked, or engaged.

Example:

Instagram DMs asking about MenuList.
retargeting

For leads who clicked, started onboarding, or replied but did not complete.

Example:

Clicked setup link but did not start onboarding.
reactivation

For old leads whose cooldown expired.

Example:

Not-now leads from 60 days ago.
social_inbound

For Instagram/Messenger campaigns designed to create inbound conversations.

Example:

DM “MENU” campaign from Instagram content.
paid_lead_followup

For Meta Lead Ads, click-to-WhatsApp, click-to-Instagram, etc.

Example:

Businesses submitted a Meta lead form.
local_cluster

For area-specific cluster acquisition.

Example:

Koramangala cafes and bakeries.
experiment

For controlled tests of channels, templates, offer angles, or onboarding flows.

manual_priority

For handpicked high-value leads.

20.5 Campaign object

Collection:

growthCampaigns

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaign = {
  id: string;

  name: string;

  type:
    | "cold_acquisition"
    | "warm_inbound"
    | "retargeting"
    | "reactivation"
    | "social_inbound"
    | "paid_lead_followup"
    | "local_cluster"
    | "experiment"
    | "manual_priority";

  status:
    | "draft"
    | "review"
    | "approved"
    | "scheduled"
    | "running"
    | "paused"
    | "completed"
    | "stopped"
    | "archived";

  objective: {
    primaryMetric:
      | "onboarding_start_rate"
      | "onboarding_completion_rate"
      | "cost_per_completed_onboarding"
      | "qualified_leads_contacted"
      | "interested_replies"
      | "flow_link_clicks";

    optimizationTarget:
      | "completed_onboardings"
      | "onboarding_starts"
      | "qualified_interest"
      | "learning"
      | "reactivation";

    description?: string;
  };

  audience: GrowthCampaignAudience;

  sourcePolicy: GrowthCampaignSourcePolicy;

  channelPolicy: GrowthCampaignChannelPolicy;

  offerPolicy: GrowthCampaignOfferPolicy;

  onboardingPolicy: GrowthCampaignOnboardingPolicy;

  messagePolicy: GrowthCampaignMessagePolicy;

  aiPolicy: GrowthCampaignAiPolicy;

  limits: GrowthCampaignLimits;

  schedule: GrowthCampaignSchedule;

  experiments?: GrowthCampaignExperimentConfig;

  stopRules: GrowthCampaignStopRules;

  stats: GrowthCampaignStats;

  createdBy: string;
  approvedBy?: string;

  createdAt: Date;
  approvedAt?: Date;
  startedAt?: Date;
  completedAt?: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};
20.6 Audience definition

The campaign builder needs a powerful but controlled audience selector.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignAudience = {
  include: {
    leadSegments?: ("A" | "B" | "C")[];

    statuses?: GrowthLeadStatus[];

    categories?: string[];

    cities?: string[];
    areas?: string[];

    businessScale?: (
      | "single_location_smb"
      | "small_local_chain"
      | "large_chain"
      | "franchise"
      | "unknown"
    )[];

    sourceProviders?: string[];
    sourceRunIds?: string[];

    channelsAvailable?: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

    primaryNeeds?: OfferAngle[];

    minLeadScore?: number;
    maxRiskScore?: number;

    intentStages?: (
      | "cold"
      | "engaged"
      | "interested"
      | "clicked"
      | "started_dropped"
      | "reactivation_candidate"
    )[];

    retargetingBuckets?: RetargetingBucket[];

    lastActivityAfter?: Date;
    lastActivityBefore?: Date;
  };

  exclude: {
    statuses?: GrowthLeadStatus[];

    suppressed?: boolean;

    converted?: boolean;

    doNotContact?: boolean;

    previousCampaignIds?: string[];

    contactedWithinDays?: number;

    categories?: string[];

    sourceProviders?: string[];

    riskFlags?: string[];

    channelsUsedRecently?: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger")[];
  };

  estimatedSize?: number;
  lockedAudienceSnapshotId?: string;
};

Core audience rule:

Every campaign audience must exclude suppressed and do-not-contact leads by default.

No campaign should override that without admin-level intervention.

20.7 Audience preview

Before launching a campaign, the system must show an audience preview.

Preview should include:

estimated leads
A/B/C split
city/area distribution
category distribution
available channel distribution
suppression exclusions
recently contacted exclusions
risk flags
expected contact-ready count
estimated cost

Example:

Audience preview:
- 1,240 matching leads
- 680 A-score
- 420 B-score
- 140 C-score
- 710 have WhatsApp/phone
- 530 have email
- 80 have Instagram
- 212 excluded due to recent contact
- 37 excluded due to suppression

The campaign should not launch until the preview is accepted.

20.8 Audience snapshot

When a campaign launches, create a snapshot.

Collection:

growthCampaignAudienceSnapshots

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignAudienceSnapshot = {
  id: string;

  campaignId: string;

  leadIds: string[];

  counts: {
    total: number;
    bySegment: Record<string, number>;
    byChannel: Record<string, number>;
    byCategory: Record<string, number>;
    byArea: Record<string, number>;
  };

  filtersUsed: GrowthCampaignAudience;

  createdAt: Date;
};

Why snapshot?

Campaign results must be measured against the actual audience selected at launch time.

If leads change later, attribution remains clean.

For very large campaigns, store snapshot pages/chunks instead of one huge document.

20.9 Source policy

Campaigns can either use existing leads or trigger new source runs.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignSourcePolicy = {
  mode:
    | "use_existing_leads"
    | "create_new_source_runs"
    | "hybrid";

  allowedSources: (
    | "apify"
    | "outscraper"
    | "manual_csv"
    | "instagram_inbound"
    | "messenger_inbound"
    | "meta_lead_ads"
    | "menulist_signal"
    | "referral"
  )[];

  sourceRunConfig?: {
    provider: "apify" | "outscraper" | "manual_csv";
    city?: string;
    areas?: string[];
    categories?: string[];
    queries?: string[];
    maxRawLeads?: number;
    maxResultsPerQuery?: number;
  };

  enrichmentPolicy?: {
    allowEnrichment: boolean;
    enrichOnlyIfScoreAbove: number;
    allowedEnrichmentTypes: (
      | "website_contact_extraction"
      | "social_identity_lookup"
      | "secondary_provider_lookup"
      | "manual_review"
    )[];
    maxEnrichmentCostUsd?: number;
  };
};

Important:

Campaigns should not run source collection and messaging blindly in one step.

Recommended flow:

source run
→ score leads
→ audience preview
→ campaign approval
→ outreach
20.10 Channel policy

Defines allowed channels and execution modes.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignChannelPolicy = {
  allowedChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  defaultChannelStrategy:
    | "ai_router"
    | "email_first"
    | "whatsapp_first"
    | "same_channel_as_inbound"
    | "manual_only"
    | "experiment";

  channelModes: {
    email?: {
      enabled: boolean;
      allowAutoSend: boolean;
      maxDailySends?: number;
      senderAccountId?: string;
    };

    whatsapp?: {
      enabled: boolean;
      allowAssistedSend: boolean;
      allowApiTemplateSend: boolean;
      maxDailySends?: number;
      requiredTemplateIds?: string[];
      channelAccountId?: string;
    };

    instagram?: {
      enabled: boolean;
      replyOnly: boolean;
      allowWarmOutbound?: boolean;
      maxDailyReplies?: number;
      channelAccountId?: string;
    };

    messenger?: {
      enabled: boolean;
      replyOnly: boolean;
      allowWarmOutbound?: boolean;
      maxDailyReplies?: number;
      channelAccountId?: string;
    };

    call?: {
      enabled: boolean;
      manualOnly: boolean;
      maxDailyCalls?: number;
    };
  };

  fallbackOrder: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  requireEligibilityCheck: true;
};

Default recommendation:

Email can auto-send if eligible.
WhatsApp is assisted/template-based.
Instagram/Messenger are reply-only or warm by default.
20.11 Offer policy

Defines which acquisition angles the campaign can use.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignOfferPolicy = {
  allowedOfferAngles: OfferAngle[];

  defaultOfferAngle?: OfferAngle;

  forcedOfferAngle?: OfferAngle;

  allowAiOfferSelection: boolean;

  conditionalClaims: {
    allowCustomerRequestClaim: boolean;
    allowLocalCampaignClaim: boolean;
    allowEarlyAccessClaim: boolean;
    allowFreeSetupClaim: boolean;
  };

  evidenceRequirements: {
    customerRequestClaimRequiresEvent: boolean;
    localCampaignClaimRequiresAreaMatch: boolean;
    freeSetupClaimRequiresPricingPolicy: boolean;
  };
};

Important:

AI cannot use an angle or claim not allowed by campaign policy.
20.12 Onboarding policy

Defines where the campaign can send leads.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignOnboardingPolicy = {
  allowedFlowIds: string[];

  defaultFlowId?: string;

  forcedFlowId?: string;

  allowAiFlowSelection: boolean;

  allowResumeFlow: boolean;

  allowManualAssistedFlow: boolean;

  trackingRequired: true;

  routeExpirationDays?: number;
};

Hard rule:

Every campaign link to MenuList onboarding must use a tracked growth route.

No raw onboarding URLs in campaigns.

20.13 Message policy

Defines allowed templates and message behavior.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignMessagePolicy = {
  allowedTemplateFamilies: string[];

  allowedTemplateIds?: string[];

  defaultTemplateFamily?: string;

  aiPersonalizationAllowed: boolean;

  maxAiPersonalizationLevel: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;

  requireMessageSafetyCheck: true;

  requireHumanApprovalFor: {
    coldWhatsApp: boolean;
    pricingResponses: boolean;
    experimentalTemplates: boolean;
    lowConfidenceAi: boolean;
    highRiskLeads: boolean;
  };

  followUpPolicyId?: string;
};

Default:

AI personalization allowed, but under guardrails.
Safety check always required.
20.14 AI policy

Defines how autonomous the campaign can be.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignAiPolicy = {
  enabled: boolean;

  autonomyLevel:
    | "suggest_only"
    | "draft_only"
    | "queue_for_approval"
    | "auto_execute_low_risk"
    | "auto_execute";

  allowedAiWorkers: (
    | "lead_scorer"
    | "channel_router"
    | "offer_selector"
    | "flow_router"
    | "message_generator"
    | "reply_classifier"
    | "objection_handler"
    | "next_best_action"
    | "campaign_optimizer"
  )[];

  confidenceThresholds: {
    autoActionMin: number;
    humanReviewBelow: number;
    blockBelow?: number;
  };

  humanApprovalRequiredFor: {
    whatsappCold: boolean;
    instagramOutbound: boolean;
    messengerOutbound: boolean;
    pricing: boolean;
    dncAmbiguity: boolean;
    highRiskLead: boolean;
  };
};

Recommended long-term default:

AI routes and drafts.
Email can auto-send if low-risk.
WhatsApp remains assisted unless template/policy path is clear.
Instagram/Messenger replies can auto-send only for simple low-risk replies inside active windows.
20.15 Campaign limits

Limits protect cost, channel health, and brand.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignLimits = {
  maxAudienceSize?: number;

  maxContactsTotal?: number;

  maxContactsPerDay?: number;

  maxByChannelPerDay?: {
    email?: number;
    whatsapp?: number;
    instagram?: number;
    messenger?: number;
    call?: number;
  };

  maxAiSpendUsd?: number;
  maxSourceSpendUsd?: number;
  maxTotalSpendUsd?: number;

  maxFollowUpsPerLead?: number;

  maxMessagesPerLead?: number;

  maxHumanReviewQueueSize?: number;

  maxNegativeRate?: number;
  maxDncRate?: number;
  maxBounceRate?: number;
  maxComplaintRate?: number;
};

Every campaign must have caps.

No uncapped campaigns.

20.16 Campaign schedule
TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignSchedule = {
  timezone: string;

  startAt?: Date;
  endAt?: Date;

  sendWindows?: {
    daysOfWeek: ("mon" | "tue" | "wed" | "thu" | "fri" | "sat" | "sun")[];
    startHourLocal: number;
    endHourLocal: number;
  }[];

  pacing:
    | "manual"
    | "evenly_distributed"
    | "as_fast_as_caps_allow"
    | "ai_optimized";

  blackoutDates?: Date[];
};

For India/local restaurant outreach, avoid sending at obviously bad hours.

The system should support local-time send windows.

20.17 Stop rules

Stop rules are non-negotiable.

TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignStopRules = {
  pauseIf: {
    negativeRateAbove?: number;
    dncRateAbove?: number;
    complaintRateAbove?: number;
    bounceRateAbove?: number;
    deliveryFailureRateAbove?: number;
    costPerCompletionAbove?: number;
    onboardingCompletionRateBelow?: number;
    humanReviewQueueAbove?: number;
    channelAccountHealthBelow?: "healthy" | "warning" | "restricted";
  };

  stopIf: {
    globalSuppressionIncident?: boolean;
    channelAccountRestricted?: boolean;
    templateRejected?: boolean;
    manualAdminStop?: boolean;
  };

  checkFrequencyMinutes: number;

  autoPauseEnabled: boolean;
};

If triggered:

pause campaign
cancel pending sends
notify admin
record reason
recommend fix
20.18 Experiment config

Campaigns can run experiments across:

source
channel
offer angle
template
onboarding flow
send time
follow-up timing
TypeScript
type GrowthCampaignExperimentConfig = {
  enabled: boolean;

  experimentId?: string;

  dimension:
    | "channel"
    | "offer_angle"
    | "template"
    | "onboarding_flow"
    | "send_time"
    | "follow_up"
    | "source";

  variants: {
    id: string;

    allocationPercent: number;

    channel?: "email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger";

    offerAngle?: OfferAngle;

    templateId?: string;

    onboardingFlowId?: string;

    sendTimeWindow?: {
      startHourLocal: number;
      endHourLocal: number;
    };

    followUpPolicyId?: string;
  }[];

  successMetric:
    | "onboarding_start_rate"
    | "onboarding_completion_rate"
    | "cost_per_completed_onboarding"
    | "negative_response_rate";

  guardrails: {
    maxNegativeRate?: number;
    maxDncRate?: number;
    minSampleSize?: number;
  };
};

Hard rule:

Eligibility and safety override experiment assignment.

If a variant requires WhatsApp but WhatsApp is blocked for a lead, do not send WhatsApp.

20.19 Campaign lifecycle

Use this lifecycle:

draft
→ review
→ approved
→ scheduled
→ running
→ paused
→ completed / stopped
→ archived
draft

Campaign can be edited.

No sends.

review

Audience preview, policy validation, templates, caps, and flows are checked.

approved

Ready to schedule/run.

scheduled

Waiting for start time.

running

Campaign can create/send actions.

paused

No new sends. Existing inbound can still be handled.

completed

Campaign ended normally.

stopped

Campaign stopped due to risk/manual stop.

archived

Read-only history.

20.20 Pre-launch validation

Before approval, run validation.

TypeScript
type CampaignValidationResult = {
  valid: boolean;

  blockers: {
    type:
      | "missing_audience"
      | "empty_audience"
      | "no_eligible_channel"
      | "missing_template"
      | "template_not_approved"
      | "missing_onboarding_flow"
      | "inactive_onboarding_flow"
      | "missing_caps"
      | "missing_suppression"
      | "unsafe_offer_claim"
      | "channel_account_unhealthy"
      | "budget_missing";

    severity: "low" | "medium" | "high" | "critical";
    message: string;
  }[];

  warnings: {
    type: string;
    message: string;
  }[];

  estimatedAudience: number;
  estimatedReachable: number;
  estimatedCost?: number;
};

Critical blockers prevent launch.

Examples:

no caps
no suppression
no approved template
no active onboarding flow
WhatsApp API campaign with unapproved template
email campaign without unsubscribe handling
20.21 Campaign execution flow

When campaign runs:

1. Load audience snapshot.
2. For each lead, run/update Lead Intelligence if stale.
3. Evaluate channel identities and eligibility.
4. Run AI Channel Router.
5. Run Offer Angle Selector.
6. Run Onboarding Flow Router.
7. Select/render guarded message.
8. Create action/send job.
9. Execute according to send mode.
10. Track events and outcomes.
11. Update campaign stats.
12. Apply stop rules continuously.

Important:

Campaign does not bypass any underlying system.

It orchestrates them.

20.22 Promotion campaign builder UI

Route:

/admin/growth/campaigns/new

Recommended wizard sections:

1. Campaign goal
2. Audience
3. Sources
4. Channels
5. Offer angles
6. Onboarding flows
7. Templates
8. AI autonomy
9. Caps and schedule
10. Experiments
11. Review and launch

This keeps campaigns deliberate.

20.23 Section 1 — Campaign goal

Fields:

campaign name
campaign type
primary objective
primary metric
target city/area/category
description

Example:

Name: Bangalore Cafe Menu Link Campaign
Type: cold_acquisition
Goal: completed_onboardings
Primary metric: onboarding_completion_rate
20.24 Section 2 — Audience

Filters:

lead segment
lead score
category
city
area
available channel
source
intent stage
retargeting bucket
last contacted
not recently contacted
exclude suppressed
exclude converted

Show live preview.

Actions:

preview audience
lock audience snapshot
export sample
view random sample

Random sample review is useful to catch bad filters before launching.

20.25 Section 3 — Sources

Choose:

use existing leads
create new source run
hybrid

If new source run:

provider
city
areas
categories
queries
max raw leads
source budget

If existing leads:

source filters
source quality thresholds

If hybrid:

source first, then score, then outreach after approval

Recommended:

Do not auto-message directly after a new source run without scoring and audience preview.
20.26 Section 4 — Channels

Select:

email
WhatsApp
Instagram
Messenger
call/manual

For each channel:

enabled?
send mode?
daily cap?
account?
fallback?

Examples:

Email: enabled, auto-send, max 200/day
WhatsApp: enabled, assisted-send, max 50/day
Instagram: inbound/reply only
Messenger: inbound/reply only

Show channel health before approval.

20.27 Section 5 — Offer angles

Choose allowed angles:

menu_link_qr
whatsapp_menu_link
instagram_bio_menu
simple_setup
local_restaurant_setup
customer_request
help_complete_onboarding
reactivation

Fields:

default angle
allow AI selection?
conditional claims?

Warnings:

customer_request selected but no demand signal filter exists
local_restaurant_setup selected but audience is not area-specific
free setup claim selected but pricing policy not configured
20.28 Section 6 — Onboarding flows

Choose allowed existing MenuList flows.

Fields:

allowedFlowIds
defaultFlowId
allow AI flow selection
allow resume flow
allow manual-assisted flow
tracking route expiration

Validation:

all selected flows active
campaign audience matches intended flow metadata
flow supports tracking route
20.29 Section 7 — Templates

Select:

template families
channel-specific templates
follow-up templates
DNC template
objection responses

Validation:

email templates have unsubscribe
WhatsApp API templates approved if API send enabled
templates match selected offer angles
templates match selected channels
message guardrails pass sample render

Show sample rendered messages for random leads.

20.30 Section 8 — AI autonomy

Choose campaign autonomy.

suggest_only
draft_only
queue_for_approval
auto_execute_low_risk
auto_execute

Recommended default:

auto_execute_low_risk for email
queue_for_approval for WhatsApp
reply-only with guardrails for Instagram/Messenger

Set thresholds:

auto action min confidence
human review below confidence
block below confidence
20.31 Section 9 — Caps and schedule

Fields:

max total contacts
max daily contacts
max by channel per day
max AI spend
max source spend
max total spend
max follow-ups
send windows
start/end dates
blackout dates

Must have:

daily caps
stop rules
schedule or manual launch

No uncapped campaigns.

20.32 Section 10 — Experiments

Optional.

Configure:

experiment dimension
variants
allocation
success metric
guardrails
minimum sample size

Example:

Test channel for A-score cafes:
Variant A: WhatsApp assisted
Variant B: Email
Metric: onboarding completion rate
Guardrail: negative response rate < 3%
20.33 Section 11 — Review and launch

Show final checklist:

audience size
sample leads
channel mix
eligible reachable count
templates
onboarding flows
caps
stop rules
AI autonomy
estimated cost
risks/warnings

Admin actions:

approve
schedule
run now
save draft

  requiredApprovals: string[];
};

The AI assistant should be a strategist, not an executor.

20.40 AI campaign recommendations

Examples:

Use WhatsApp assisted only for A-score leads with phone.
Use email for B-score leads.
Keep Instagram/Messenger as inbound-only.
Use menu_link_qr as default angle.
Route cafes to restaurant_quick_start.
Pause if DNC rate exceeds 2%.

Recommendations should be explainable.

Example 1 — Bangalore cafe cold acquisition

20.42 Campaign stop examples

Pause if:

DNC rate > 2%
negative rate > 5%
email bounce rate > 5%
WhatsApp assisted queue backlog > 100
onboarding completion rate < target after minimum sample
source duplicate rate > 35%

Stop if:

complaint spike
channel account restricted
template rejected
admin manual stop
severe safety violation

The system should prioritize long-term channel health over short-term volume.

20.43 Campaign learning loop

After campaign runs, the system should learn:

which source worked
which audience segment worked
which channel worked
which offer angle worked
which template worked
which onboarding flow worked
which follow-up worked
where negative/DNC risk appeared

The campaign result feeds:

Source Planner
Lead Scorer
Channel Router
Offer Angle Selector
Template Selector
Onboarding Flow Router
Next-Best-Action Engine
Campaign Optimizer

The campaign should make the whole Growth Engine smarter.

20.44 AI campaign review

After campaign ends or pauses, AI generates review.

Output:

summary
what worked
what failed
best segment
worst segment
channel performance
message performance
flow performance
cost per completion
negative/DNC analysis
recommended next campaign
recommended changes

Example:

A-score cafes in Koramangala via WhatsApp-assisted produced the best completion rate.
B-score restaurants via email had low starts.
Template v2 produced fewer replies but higher onboarding completion.
Recommend scaling WhatsApp-assisted A-score cafes by 30% and pausing HSR cloud kitchen segment.

This prevents you from manually analyzing campaign data.

20.45 Campaign failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Campaign becomes a broadcast blast

Fix:

audience filters, caps, eligibility, suppression, stop rules
Failure mode 2 — Campaign sends to bad leads

Fix:

Lead Intelligence threshold and random sample review
Failure mode 3 — Wrong channel mix

Fix:

AI Channel Router + channel performance feedback
Failure mode 4 — Too many experiments

Fix:

one experiment dimension per campaign
minimum sample size
clear success metric
Failure mode 5 — Campaign optimizes for replies

Fix:

primary metric = onboarding completion or cost per completion
Failure mode 6 — Campaign damages channel reputation

Fix:

stop rules, health dashboard, negative/DNC thresholds
Failure mode 7 — Attribution is missing

Fix:

tracked routes required, message IDs required, campaign versioning
20.46 Final campaign contract

Every launched campaign must have this final contract:

TypeScript
type FinalGrowthCampaignContract = {
  campaignId: string;

  name: string;
  type: GrowthCampaignType;

  objective: {
    primaryMetric:
      | "onboarding_start_rate"
      | "onboarding_completion_rate"
      | "cost_per_completed_onboarding"
      | "qualified_leads_contacted"
      | "interested_replies"
      | "flow_link_clicks";

    optimizationTarget:
      | "completed_onboardings"
      | "onboarding_starts"
      | "qualified_interest"
      | "learning"
      | "reactivation";
  };

  audienceSnapshotId: string;

  allowedChannels: ("email" | "whatsapp" | "instagram" | "messenger" | "call")[];

  allowedOfferAngles: OfferAngle[];

  allowedOnboardingFlowIds: string[];

  allowedTemplateFamilies: string[];

  aiAutonomyLevel:
    | "suggest_only"
    | "draft_only"
    | "queue_for_approval"
    | "auto_execute_low_risk"
    | "auto_execute";

  limits: {
    maxContactsTotal?: number;
    maxContactsPerDay?: number;
    maxByChannelPerDay?: Record<string, number>;
    maxAiSpendUsd?: number;
    maxTotalSpendUsd?: number;
    maxFollowUpsPerLead?: number;
  };

  stopRules: GrowthCampaignStopRules;

  trackingRequired: true;

  status: "approved" | "scheduled" | "running" | "paused" | "completed" | "stopped";

  approvedBy: string;

};

No campaign should run without this.

20.47 Final principle

The Promotion Campaign Builder is how MenuList turns the Growth Engine from a set of tools into a repeatable acquisition machine.

It should not ask:

Who can we message?

It should ask:

Which audience, through which channel, with which offer angle, into which existing onboarding flow, under what caps and stop rules, will produce the most completed MenuList onboardings with the least channel risk?

That is the right campaign question.

Next spec item: Experiment engine.

Spec 21 — Experiment Engine
21.1 Purpose

The Experiment Engine lets the Growth Engine test and learn systematically across:

lead sources
lead segments
channels
offer angles
message templates
send timing
follow-up logic
existing onboarding flow routing
AI routing decisions

Its purpose is not to run “random tests.”

Its purpose is to answer:

What actually produces completed MenuList onboardings at acceptable cost and risk?

The Experiment Engine prevents the system from relying on opinions like:

WhatsApp should work better.
This template feels better.
Cafes are probably better.
Instagram leads may convert.

Instead, it creates measured learning loops.

21.2 Core principle

The system should optimize for:

completed onboarding

not:

reply rate
open rate
click rate
message volume

Experiment success should usually be judged by:

onboarding_completion_rate
cost_per_completed_onboarding
negative_response_rate

Replies and clicks are diagnostic. They are not the main outcome.

21.3 What the Experiment Engine owns

It owns:

experiment creation
hypothesis definition
variant allocation
audience assignment
holdout/control logic
randomization
experiment guardrails
result tracking
winner selection
statistical confidence flags
experiment stop rules
experiment event logging
experiment result summaries
AI recommendations from experiments

It does not own:

lead sourcing itself
message generation itself
channel execution itself
onboarding flow UX
pricing
product onboarding
business activation

It coordinates other systems and measures outcomes.

21.4 Experiment object

Collection:

growthExperiments

Schema:

TypeScript
type GrowthExperiment = {
  id: string;

  name: string;

  status:
    | "draft"
    | "review"
    | "running"
    | "paused"
    | "completed"
    | "stopped"
    | "archived";

  hypothesis: string;

  type:
    | "source"
    | "channel"
    | "offer_angle"
    | "template"
    | "onboarding_flow"
    | "send_time"
    | "follow_up"
    | "ai_router"
    | "multi_factor";

  campaignId?: string;

  audience: {
    sourceAudienceSnapshotId?: string;

    filters?: GrowthCampaignAudience;

    minSampleSizePerVariant: number;
    maxSampleSizePerVariant?: number;
  };

  assignment: {
    method:
      | "random"
      | "weighted_random"
      | "deterministic_hash"
      | "manual"
      | "ai_bandit_later";

    unit:
      | "lead"
      | "conversation"
      | "message"
      | "campaign"
      | "source_run";

    holdoutPercent?: number;
  };

  variants: GrowthExperimentVariant[];

  metrics: {
    primary:
      | "onboarding_completion_rate"
      | "onboarding_start_rate"
      | "cost_per_completed_onboarding"
      | "negative_response_rate";

    secondary: (
      | "reply_rate"
      | "click_rate"
      | "interested_rate"
      | "route_rate"
      | "bounce_rate"
      | "dnc_rate"

    };
  };

    startAt?: Date;

type GrowthExperimentVariant = {
  id: string;

  name: string;

  allocationPercent: number;

  config: {
    sourceProvider?: "apify" | "outscraper" | "manual_csv" | "instagram_inbound" | "messenger_inbound" | "meta_lead_ads";

    };

      | "rule_based"

  };

  };

    | "active"
    | "paused"
    | "stopped";
