banned claims
channel policy
suppression rules
human approval
AI evals
audit logs
cost caps

AI does not directly “do whatever it wants.”

It operates inside the acquisition system.

Firestore should be used for:

hot operational state
work queues
lead summaries
inbox items
campaign configs
current channel health
approvals
suppression state

Not for heavy analytics.

Heavy analytics should go to:

BigQuery

Raw payloads should go to:

Cloud Storage

growthLeadSummaries

growthTemplateStats

Not raw events.

Hard cost rules:

no broad listeners

no dashboard from raw events

no raw provider payloads in Firestore

Yes. The lead-gen engine is strong, but if the goal is fast MenuList growth, there is one remaining layer I would add:

Distribution Flywheel Layer

The system we designed finds and converts businesses. The missing layer makes every customer-facing MenuList surface, every onboarding event, every QR/menu share, every inbound search, and every satisfied business create more leads.

In other words:

Lead gen = outbound acquisition.
Distribution flywheel = compounding acquisition.

You need both.

My conclusion

The current system is enough to replace a basic lead-gen/marketing team.

But to grow MenuList faster, add these long-term distribution features:

1. Demand Signal Capture Engine
2. Public Surface Acquisition Hooks
3. QR / Menu Link Viral Loop
4. Google Business Profile Menu-Link Campaign Engine
5. Meta Click-to-Message / Lead Ads Engine
6. Local Cluster Expansion Engine
7. Referral and Branch Expansion Engine
8. Partner / Agency Channel Engine
9. Retargeting Audience Builder
10. Market Coverage Map
11. Competitive Gap Monitor
12. Distribution Attribution Layer

These are not random features. They create owned distribution loops around MenuList.

1. Demand Signal Capture Engine

This is the biggest missing growth feature.

The idea:

When customers look for a business/menu and MenuList does not yet have that business onboarded, that demand becomes a high-intent business lead.

Examples of demand signals:

customer searches for “ABC Cafe menu”
customer lands on an unclaimed MenuList business/menu page
customer clicks “request menu”
customer scans a QR but business is not fully onboarded
customer tries to share a missing menu
customer asks for a restaurant menu through MenuList

This becomes a lead signal:

JSON
{
  "businessName": "ABC Cafe",
  "city": "Bangalore",
  "area": "Koramangala",
  "signalType": "customer_menu_request",
  "demandCount": 7,
  "leadPriority": "high",
  "recommendedAngle": "customer_request"
}

Why this matters:

“Customers requested your menu on MenuList” is much stronger than “we help restaurants create menu links.”

But only use this claim when the demand is real.

This creates an owned acquisition loop:

customer demand
→ business lead
→ owner contacted
→ business onboarded
→ better customer experience
→ more customer demand

This is much more defensible than scraping.

Build this.

2. Public Surface Acquisition Hooks

If MenuList already has or will have customer-facing pages, each page should quietly support acquisition.

Not aggressive. Not spammy.

Examples:

“Own this business?”
“Set up your MenuList menu link”
“Create your restaurant menu link + QR”
“Is this your restaurant?”
“Claim / update this menu”

This converts customer-facing traffic into owner acquisition.

Important boundary:

This should not turn into Google Business Profile management.
This should not become a full business dashboard feature.
This is only an acquisition hook into existing onboarding.

Every hook should create a tracked Growth Engine lead:

surface_view
owner_claim_click
setup_started
setup_completed

This gives you a non-paid acquisition loop from public demand.

3. QR / Menu Link Viral Loop

MenuList’s natural distribution object is:

menu link + QR

Every published menu link and QR can carry subtle distribution.

Examples:

small footer: “Menu by MenuList”
“Create your menu link”
“Get this for your restaurant”

The goal is not to advertise loudly. The goal is default presence.

This creates:

customer opens MenuList menu
→ sees MenuList as menu infrastructure
→ another business owner/customer discovers MenuList
→ new business starts onboarding

Track:

footer CTA impressions
footer CTA clicks
business owner claim clicks
QR scans
share events
referral source page

Add attribution:

lead.source = menu_surface_referral
lead.referredByBusinessId = existingBusinessId
lead.referredByMenuPage = pageId

This is important because it turns every onboarded business into a distribution node.

4. Google Business Profile Menu-Link Campaign Engine

This is a high-leverage positioning campaign, not a Google management product.

Google Business Profile allows restaurants/businesses to add a menu link in their profile; Google’s help page says businesses can edit profile information and enter the URL where their menu can be found. 
Google Help

That gives MenuList a strong owner-facing pitch:

Use your MenuList link as the menu link you can share on Google, WhatsApp, Instagram, and QR.

Do not say:

We manage your Google profile.
We found you on Google Maps.
Your Google listing is bad.

Say:

MenuList gives you one clean menu link you can use wherever customers look for your menu.

Feature to build:

GBP menu-link readiness detector

It checks whether a lead likely has:

no website
no clear menu link
PDF/image menu
Instagram-only presence
weak customer-facing link

Then the campaign angle becomes:

one clean menu link for public profiles + WhatsApp + Instagram + QR

This is a distribution angle, not a product expansion.

5. Meta Click-to-Message / Lead Ads Engine

You should not rely only on cold outbound.

Build paid/warm acquisition into the same Growth Engine.

Meta supports Lead Ads with webhook/CRM-style integrations so submitted leads can be received in real time, and Meta also supports ads that click to WhatsApp. 
Facebook Developers
+1

Features to add:

Click-to-WhatsApp campaign tracking
Click-to-Instagram campaign tracking
Click-to-Messenger campaign tracking
ad campaign attribution
paid lead scoring
fast follow-up queue
cost per onboarding completion by ad/campaign

Why this matters:

cold outbound creates supply
paid click-to-message creates intent
inbound social creates warmer conversations

The Growth Engine should handle all three.

Flow:

Meta ad / lead form / click-to-message
→ Growth Lead created
→ AI scores
→ channel router chooses follow-up
→ onboarding flow link sent
→ completion attributed back to ad/campaign

This lets you test paid acquisition without creating a separate marketing stack.

Spec 32 — MenuList Distribution Flywheel Engine
32.1 Purpose

The Distribution Flywheel Engine is the missing layer that turns MenuList from an outbound lead-generation system into a compounding distribution system.

The Growth Engine we designed does this:

find leads
→ qualify leads
→ message leads
→ route interested leads into onboarding
→ learn what converts

The Distribution Flywheel Engine does this:

capture demand from MenuList surfaces
→ convert customer/business interactions into owner leads
→ turn each onboarded business into a distribution node
→ identify market gaps and clusters
→ feed high-intent leads back into the Growth Engine

This is the difference between:

outbound acquisition

and:

owned distribution infrastructure
32.2 Core charter
The Distribution Flywheel Engine captures, scores, attributes, and routes growth signals created by MenuList’s own surfaces, customer behavior, QR/menu link usage, referrals, partners, paid intent channels, and local market coverage gaps into the Growth Engine as high-intent acquisition opportunities.

Simpler:

Every customer interaction, menu view, QR scan, owner claim, referral, partner lead, and local coverage gap should become structured growth intelligence.
32.3 Boundary

This is still marketing and distribution infrastructure.

It does not own:

MenuList onboarding UX
menu creation
menu editing
business verification
customer-facing menu page logic
QR generation logic
business dashboard
pricing/payment
business truth management

It owns:

demand signal capture
surface-to-lead conversion
distribution attribution
referral attribution
partner attribution
cluster opportunity scoring
market coverage intelligence
growth CTA experiments
saved growth audiences
distribution loop analytics

The clean boundary:

MenuList Product creates customer/business surfaces.
Distribution Flywheel observes and instruments those surfaces.
Growth Engine acts on the resulting acquisition signals.
Existing onboarding converts interested businesses.
32.4 Relationship with the Growth Engine

The Distribution Flywheel Engine does not replace the Growth Engine.

It feeds it.

Distribution Flywheel Engine
→ creates demand signals / warm leads / growth audiences
→ Growth Engine qualifies, routes, messages, and follows up
→ MenuList onboarding converts
→ feedback returns to both systems

The flow:

MenuList surface event
→ distribution signal
→ lead match/create
→ AI priority scoring
→ saved audience or direct Growth Lead
→ Growth Engine campaign / inbox / next-best-action
→ onboarding completion
→ distribution attribution updated
32.5 System modules

The Distribution Flywheel Engine has 12 modules:

1. Demand Signal Capture Engine
2. Public Surface Acquisition Hooks
3. QR / Menu Link Viral Loop
4. Google Menu-Link Opportunity Engine
5. Meta Paid Intent Engine
6. Local Cluster Expansion Engine
7. Referral and Branch Expansion Engine
8. Partner / Agency Channel Engine
9. Retargeting Audience Builder
10. Market Coverage Map
11. Menu Link Gap Monitor
12. Distribution Attribution Layer

These modules create growth loops around MenuList instead of depending only on scraped outbound leads.

32.6 Core principle

The system should not ask only:

Which businesses can we scrape and message?

It should ask:

Where is demand already appearing?
Which businesses are customers already looking for?
Which onboarded businesses can create more leads?
Which clusters are becoming dense?
Which surfaces can convert owners?
Which channel loops compound?

Outbound creates the first push.

Distribution creates compounding pull.

32.8 North-star metric

The Distribution Flywheel Engine should optimize:

distribution-sourced completed onboardings

More exact:

Number of completed MenuList onboardings that originated from owned surfaces, customer demand, QR/menu link loops, referrals, partners, paid intent, or market coverage signals.

Secondary metrics:

demand signals captured
owner claim clicks
public surface setup starts
QR/menu footer referral leads
partner-sourced leads
referral-sourced leads
cluster coverage growth
distribution cost per completed onboarding

Do not optimize only for:

surface impressions
QR scans
menu views
CTA clicks
referral clicks

Those are diagnostics.

The real output is:

completed onboarding
32.9 Signal hierarchy

Not every signal has equal value.

Use this priority model:

Tier 1 — Highest intent
owner clicks “Claim / Set up this business”
owner submits business contact
business starts onboarding from public surface
customer request count crosses threshold
partner submits direct owner lead
existing owner adds another branch

Action:

immediate Growth Lead creation / update
high-priority routing
Tier 2 — Strong signal
customer requests menu
repeated unclaimed business views
multiple searches for same business/menu
QR/menu page referral from another business
business owner clicks from MenuList footer
business replies to demand-based outreach

Action:

create or upgrade lead
use customer_request or public_surface angle if evidence exists
Tier 3 — Medium signal
menu page footer click
QR attribution click
public surface setup CTA impression + click
market gap detected
local cluster coverage opportunity

Action:

add signal to lead intelligence
include in saved audience
possibly campaign later
Tier 4 — Weak signal
single anonymous view
single menu page impression
low-confidence business match
generic area/category demand

Action:

aggregate into market coverage
do not contact directly from weak signal alone
Module 1 — Demand Signal Capture Engine
32.10 Purpose

The Demand Signal Capture Engine turns customer/business demand into owner acquisition leads.

It captures events like:

customer searches for a business menu
customer requests a missing menu
customer views an unclaimed business/menu page
customer clicks “request this menu”
customer shares a missing menu page
customer lands on a placeholder/unclaimed surface

This is high-leverage because the outreach can be based on real demand:

Customers have requested your menu on MenuList.

Use that claim only when real evidence exists.

32.14 Demand scoring
Demand Score =
  menu request weight
+ repeated searches
+ unique users
+ setup/claim clicks
+ recency
+ business fit
- low-confidence match penalty

Suggested weights:

request_menu_click: +40
owner_claim_click: +80
setup_cta_click: +90
repeat searches by unique users: +20–50
unclaimed page views: +5–20
matched food business: +20
low match confidence: -30

Thresholds:

80–100: immediate high-intent lead
60–79: create/upgrade lead, campaign eligible
40–59: aggregate and monitor
<40: no direct outreach
32.15 Demand-to-lead workflow
1. Demand event captured.
2. Match to existing product business or Growth Lead.
3. Update businessDemandSummary.
4. If threshold crossed, create or upgrade Growth Lead.
5. Set source = customer_demand_signal.
6. Set offer angle eligibility = customer_request.
7. Send to Growth Engine for scoring/routing.

Do not contact from a single weak event.

Use thresholds.

Module 3 — QR / Menu Link Viral Loop
32.22 Purpose

Every MenuList menu link and QR should be a distribution node.

When customers open a MenuList menu, other restaurant owners or customers may discover MenuList.

The loop:

business publishes MenuList link/QR
→ customers scan/open/share
→ more people see MenuList
→ some click “get this for your restaurant”
→ new business lead/onboarding

This creates compounding distribution.

32.23 Viral loop surfaces

Subtle hooks:

Menu by MenuList
Get this for your restaurant
Create your menu link + QR
Powered by MenuList

Placement:

footer
share screen
QR landing page
post-menu interaction
print/QR download page
business success screen

Important:

Do not make the menu page feel polluted.
Do not reduce customer experience.
Do not over-brand.

Module 4 — Google Menu-Link Opportunity Engine
32.27 Purpose

Restaurants can add or edit a menu URL in Google Business Profile through the menu link field; Google’s Business Profile help page describes entering the URL where the menu can be found under “Menu link.” 
Google Help

This creates a strong distribution angle:

MenuList gives you one clean menu link you can use across public profiles, WhatsApp, Instagram, and QR.

Important boundary:

MenuList does not manage Google Business Profile.
MenuList provides the menu link the owner can use where appropriate.

Do not build GBP management.

Build:

Google menu-link opportunity detection
32.28 Opportunity signals

Signals:

business has no website
business has weak/no clear menu link
business appears Instagram-only
business uses PDF/image menu
business has customer demand signal
business has no clean shareable link
business is food category and customer-facing

Do not store or reuse Google review/photo/menu content as product data.

Use this only as acquisition intelligence.

32.29 Menu-link opportunity schema

Collection:

googleMenuLinkOpportunities
TypeScript
type GoogleMenuLinkOpportunity = {
  id: string;

  leadId: string;

  business: {
    name: string;
    city?: string;
    area?: string;
    category?: string;
  };

  signals: {
    noWebsite?: boolean;
    noClearMenuLink?: boolean;
    pdfOrImageMenu?: boolean;
    instagramOnly?: boolean;
    customerDemand?: boolean;
    publicProfileOpportunity?: boolean;
  };

  opportunityScore: number; // 0-100

  recommendedAngle:
    | "menu_link_qr"
    | "google_profile_menu_link"
    | "simple_setup";

  outreachAllowed: boolean;

  messagingGuardrails: {
    cannotMentionGoogleScrape: true;
    cannotClaimWeManageGoogle: true;
    cannotSayListingBad: true;
  };

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};
32.30 Messaging rule

Allowed:

MenuList helps restaurants create a clean menu link they can share across customer-facing places like WhatsApp, Instagram, QR, and public profiles.

Banned:

We found you on Google Maps.
Your Google listing is missing a menu.
We manage your Google profile.
Your Google menu is bad.
Module 5 — Meta Paid Intent Engine
32.31 Purpose

The Distribution Flywheel should ingest paid/warm demand from Meta.

Meta’s Lead Ads documentation supports using webhooks to receive submitted leads in real time for CRM-style integrations. 
Facebook Developers
 Meta also has official developer documentation for Ads that Click to WhatsApp, which outlines creating an ad campaign and messaging ad creative for click-to-WhatsApp flows. 
Facebook Developers
 Instagram messaging webhooks can provide real-time HTTP notifications for Instagram messaging events. 
Facebook Developers

This lets MenuList route paid or social-intent leads into the same Growth Engine.

boosted social CTA campaigns
retargeting audiences

2. Verify webhook.
3. Normalize lead data.
4. Match/create Growth Lead.
5. Source = paid_intent.

7. Channel Router chooses fast follow-up path.
8. Existing onboarding route sent.
9. Completion attributed to Meta campaign/ad.

Paid intent leads should have higher priority than cold scraped leads.

Mumbai / Bandra / dessert shops

Clusters matter because they create:

32.39 Cluster workflows
1. Source runs update known businesses.
2. Growth outcomes update conversion metrics.
3. Distribution events update demand signals.
4. Cluster score recalculates.
5. AI suggests next cluster campaign.
6. Campaign Builder creates draft.

Example recommendation:

Expand Koramangala cafes.
Reason: high A-lead density, low DNC rate, strong WhatsApp completion, growing customer demand.

32.64 Guardrails
Public surface guardrails

Do not:

make menu pages feel spammy
mislead customers
imply unverified ownership
interrupt menu viewing
show aggressive owner CTAs

Do:

subtle owner CTA
clear setup route
track attribution
respect user experience
Customer demand guardrails

Do not claim:

many customers requested your menu

unless true.

Use:

Customers have requested your menu on MenuList

only if a real demand signal exists.

If count is small, avoid numbers.

If count is high and verified, optionally use numbers later.

Gap signal guardrails

Do not say:

your website is bad
your menu is missing
your Google listing is incomplete

Use gaps internally.

Outbound should stay simple:

MenuList helps restaurants create a clean menu link + QR for customers.
Referral guardrails

Do not spam contacts referred by someone else.

Referred leads still pass:

dedupe
suppression
lead scoring
eligibility
campaign policy
Partner guardrails

Partners should not get unrestricted send capability.

They can:

submit leads
share referral links
view limited performance

They should not:

message through MenuList
access lead database
see other partners’ data
override suppression

32.74 Final system contract

The Distribution Flywheel Engine should satisfy this contract:

1. Every meaningful customer/business surface event can become a structured signal.
2. Every signal is matched, scored, and attributed.
3. Strong signals create or upgrade Growth Leads.
4. Growth Engine handles outreach and onboarding routing.
5. Public hooks are subtle and product-safe.
6. Demand-based claims require real evidence.
7. QR/menu links create attributable referral loops.
8. Partner/referral leads pass the same suppression and qualification checks.
9. Market coverage guides cluster expansion.
10. Distribution analytics measure completed onboardings, not clicks.
11. Firestore stores summaries; BigQuery handles heavy analytics.
12. No distribution feature expands MenuList into CRM/POS/support/product bloat.
32.75 Final principle

The Growth Engine gets MenuList its first distribution motion.

The Distribution Flywheel Engine makes that motion compound.

The long-term goal is:

outbound creates initial coverage
coverage creates customer demand
customer demand creates owner leads
owner leads create more onboarded businesses
onboarded businesses create more QR/menu-link distribution
distribution creates more demand

That is the loop that can make MenuList grow faster without permanently depending on paid scraping or a lead-gen team.

Spec 33 — Demand Signal Capture Engine
33.1 Purpose

The Demand Signal Capture Engine converts customer and owner intent on MenuList surfaces into structured acquisition signals.

It answers:

Which businesses are customers looking for?
Which businesses are being requested?
Which unclaimed business/menu pages are getting demand?
Which owner-like users are trying to claim or set up a page?
Which demand signals are strong enough to become Growth Leads?
Which signals justify a customer_request outreach angle?

This is one of the highest-leverage additions because it creates leads from real demand, not only scraped supply.

The Growth Engine finds businesses externally.

The Demand Signal Capture Engine finds businesses because users/customers are already asking for them inside MenuList.

33.2 Core principle

The system should distinguish between:

weak anonymous interest

and:

actionable business demand

A single anonymous page view should not trigger outreach.

But repeated searches, request-menu clicks, owner-claim attempts, or setup-start events should create strong acquisition signals.

The rule:

Do not contact businesses because one random user viewed a page.
Do contact or prioritize businesses when real customer/owner demand accumulates.
33.3 Strategic value

This engine creates a stronger acquisition wedge than cold outbound.

Cold outbound says:

MenuList helps restaurants create a clean menu link + QR.

Demand-led outreach can say, if true:

Customers have requested your menu on MenuList.

That is a higher-intent reason to care.

But the claim must be evidence-backed.

No fake demand.

No inflated demand.

No “many customers” unless the count supports it.

33.4 Boundary

This engine owns:

demand event capture
business demand aggregation
signal-to-lead matching
demand scoring
claim eligibility
demand-driven audience creation
demand attribution
demand dashboards

It does not own:

customer-facing menu page UX
MenuList onboarding UX
business verification
menu creation
public business truth
customer account logic
outbound messaging
pricing

It only observes MenuList surfaces and feeds actionable signals into the Growth Engine.

33.5 Demand signal sources

Capture signals from these surfaces:

Menu search
Business/menu page
Unclaimed business page
Missing menu page
QR landing page
Public claim CTA
Request menu CTA
Share flow
Post-menu interaction
404 / missing business/menu route
Owner setup CTA

Possible examples:

customer searches “ABC Cafe menu”
customer clicks “request menu”
customer opens unclaimed ABC Cafe page
customer shares missing menu page
owner clicks “Own this business?”
owner starts setup from public page
owner submits contact
customer suggests a missing business
33.6 Signal types

Use a fixed taxonomy.

TypeScript
type DemandSignalType =
  | "business_search"
  | "menu_search"
  | "unclaimed_business_page_view"
  | "unclaimed_menu_page_view"
  | "missing_menu_page_view"
  | "request_menu_click"
  | "customer_suggested_business"
  | "missing_menu_share"
  | "owner_claim_click"
  | "owner_setup_click"
  | "owner_contact_submitted"
  | "setup_started_from_surface"
  | "repeat_demand_threshold_crossed";

Meaning:

business_search:
A user searched for a business.

menu_search:
A user searched for a business menu.

unclaimed_business_page_view:
A user viewed a known but unclaimed business page.

unclaimed_menu_page_view:
A user viewed a known but unclaimed menu page.

missing_menu_page_view:
A user landed on a missing/placeholder menu surface.

request_menu_click:
A user explicitly requested the menu.

customer_suggested_business:
A user submitted a missing business.

missing_menu_share:
A user shared a missing/unclaimed menu page.

owner_claim_click:
Someone clicked “Own this business?” or similar.

owner_setup_click:
Someone clicked “Set up menu link / QR.”

owner_contact_submitted:
Owner-like user submitted contact.

setup_started_from_surface:
User entered existing MenuList onboarding from a public surface.

repeat_demand_threshold_crossed:
Aggregate demand crossed a configured threshold.
33.7 Signal strength hierarchy

Not all signals are equal.

Very strong
owner_contact_submitted
setup_started_from_surface
owner_setup_click
owner_claim_click

These indicate likely owner/business intent.

Default action:

create or upgrade Growth Lead immediately
Strong
request_menu_click
customer_suggested_business
repeat_demand_threshold_crossed
multiple unique users searching/requesting same business

Default action:

create/upgrade Growth Lead when threshold is met
Medium
missing_menu_share
unclaimed_menu_page_view from repeated users
menu_search repeated for same business

Default action:

aggregate and monitor; create lead if score crosses threshold
Weak
single anonymous view
single search
single unclaimed page view

Default action:

aggregate only
33.8 Core data model

Use four main collections:

customerDemandSignals
businessDemandSummaries
demandSignalMatches
demandClaimEligibility

Plus summary/analytics collections:

demandDailyStats
demandSavedAudiences
demandSignalIncidents

Cost principle:

Raw demand signals can be high-volume.
Dashboards must read summaries, not raw signals.
33.9 customerDemandSignals schema

This is the raw event-like object.

TypeScript
type CustomerDemandSignal = {
  id: string;

  signalType:
    | "business_search"
    | "menu_search"
    | "unclaimed_business_page_view"
    | "unclaimed_menu_page_view"
    | "missing_menu_page_view"
    | "request_menu_click"
    | "customer_suggested_business"
    | "missing_menu_share"
    | "owner_claim_click"
    | "owner_setup_click"
    | "owner_contact_submitted"
    | "setup_started_from_surface"
    | "repeat_demand_threshold_crossed";

  business: {
    rawName?: string;
    normalizedName?: string;

    category?: string;

    country?: string;
    city?: string;
    normalizedCity?: string;
    area?: string;
    normalizedArea?: string;

    productBusinessId?: string;
    growthLeadId?: string;

    matchConfidence?: number;
  };

  surface: {
    surfaceType:
      | "search"
      | "business_page"
      | "menu_page"
      | "placeholder_page"
      | "qr_landing"
      | "public_claim_surface"
      | "share_surface"
      | "unknown";

    surfaceId?: string;
    path?: string;
    referrerPath?: string;
  };

  actor: {
    anonymousIdHash?: string;
    userId?: string;
    sessionIdHash?: string;
    ipHash?: string;
    userAgentHash?: string;

    actorType?:
      | "customer"
      | "owner_like"
      | "unknown";
  };

  attribution: {
    source:
      | "organic"
      | "search"
      | "menu_page"
      | "qr"
      | "share"
      | "public_claim"
      | "partner"
      | "ad"
      | "unknown";

    campaignId?: string;
    experimentId?: string;
    variantId?: string;

    referringBusinessId?: string;
    referringMenuPageId?: string;
    partnerId?: string;
  };

  signal: {
    strengthScore: number; // 0-100
    reason: string[];
  };

  processing: {
    status:
      | "new"
      | "matched"
      | "aggregated"
      | "lead_created"
      | "ignored"
      | "failed";

    processedAt?: Date;
    error?: string;
  };

  idempotencyKey: string;

  createdAt: Date;

  expireAt?: Date;
};
33.10 Cost policy for raw demand signals

customerDemandSignals can grow quickly.

Do not keep all raw events forever in Firestore.

Recommended:

High-value signals:
retain longer

Low-value view/search signals:
TTL after 7–30 days after rollup

All signals:
export to BigQuery or daily aggregate if needed

Retention suggestion:

owner_contact_submitted: long-term or until lead created + audit retained
owner_claim_click: 90–180 days
request_menu_click: 90–180 days
single page view/search: 7–30 days
aggregated weak signals: summary retained, raw TTL

Firestore dashboards should read:

businessDemandSummaries
demandDailyStats
demandSavedAudiences

not customerDemandSignals.

33.11 Idempotency

Demand events need dedupe.

Use idempotency key:

signalType + normalizedBusinessKey + anonymousId/session + surface + day/hour bucket

Examples:

request_menu_click:abc-cafe:koramangala:bangalore:anon123:2026-06-20
owner_claim_click:businessId:pageId:sessionHash
business_search:queryHash:sessionHash:timestampBucket

Do not let page refreshes inflate demand.

33.12 businessDemandSummaries schema

This is the main operational object.

TypeScript
type BusinessDemandSummary = {
  id: string; // businessKey or productBusinessId

  businessKey: string;

  business: {
    name: string;
    normalizedName: string;

    category?: string;

    country?: string;

  };

  counts: {

    unclaimedBusinessViews: number;

    ownerClaimClicks: number;

  };

  recent: {

  claimEligibility: {

    evidenceCount?: number;
    evidenceWindowDays?: number;
    lastEvaluatedAt?: Date;
  };

  recommendedAction:
    | "create_growth_lead"
    | "upgrade_existing_lead"
    | "add_to_customer_request_campaign"
    | "add_to_saved_audience"
    | "hold"
    | "ignore"
    | "human_review";

  routingHints?: {
    recommendedOfferAngle?:
      | "customer_request"
      | "menu_link_qr"
      | "simple_setup"
      | "instagram_bio_menu"
      | "whatsapp_menu_link";

    recommendedPriority?: "low" | "normal" | "high" | "urgent";
  };

  status:
    | "monitoring"
    | "lead_created"
    | "lead_linked"
    | "campaign_eligible"
    | "ignored"
    | "converted";

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};
33.13 Business key generation

Use stable matching keys.

productBusinessId if known
else normalizedName + normalizedArea + normalizedCity
else normalizedName + normalizedCity
else search/query hash if insufficient

Function:

TypeScript
function buildBusinessDemandKey(input: {
  productBusinessId?: string;
  normalizedName?: string;
  normalizedArea?: string;
  normalizedCity?: string;
}) {
  if (input.productBusinessId) return `product:${input.productBusinessId}`;

  if (input.normalizedName && input.normalizedArea && input.normalizedCity) {
    return `name_area_city:${input.normalizedName}:${input.normalizedArea}:${input.normalizedCity}`;
  }

  if (input.normalizedName && input.normalizedCity) {
    return `name_city:${input.normalizedName}:${input.normalizedCity}`;
  }

  return null;
}

If no reliable key:

store signal
do not create lead
aggregate only if later matched
33.14 Demand scoring formula

Use an interpretable formula first.

Demand Score =
  0.35 × Customer Demand Score
+ 0.35 × Owner Intent Score
+ 0.15 × Recency Score
+ 0.10 × Business Fit Score
+ 0.05 × Source Confidence
Customer Demand Score
request_menu_clicks
repeat menu searches
unique customer actors
missing menu shares
unclaimed menu views

Example scoring:

request_menu_click = +35
unique request user = +10
repeat menu search = +5 each, capped
missing menu share = +15
unclaimed page view = +2 each, capped
Owner Intent Score
owner_claim_click = +70
owner_setup_click = +80
owner_contact_submitted = +95
setup_started_from_surface = +100
Recency Score
last 24h = high
last 7d = medium/high
last 30d = medium
older = low
Business Fit Score

Use Growth Lead Intelligence if lead exists.

Otherwise:

food category match
city/category target
known business type
33.15 Demand score thresholds

Recommended:

90–100:
urgent lead, immediate Growth Engine routing

75–89:
create/upgrade lead, customer_request or setup intent campaign eligible

60–74:
create/upgrade lead if business match is strong; otherwise human review

40–59:
saved audience / monitor

<40:
aggregate only

Owner intent overrides:

owner_contact_submitted → immediate lead
setup_started_from_surface → immediate lead/onboarding feedback
owner_setup_click → high priority
owner_claim_click → high priority

The most sensitive feature is whether the system can say:

Create a separate claim eligibility object.

Collection:

demandClaimEligibility

33.17 Claim rules
Customer request claim allowed

Allowed when:

request_menu_click >= configured threshold
or customer_suggested_business exists
or repeated unique menu searches cross threshold

Recommended threshold:

at least 1 explicit request_menu_click
or 3+ unique demand signals within 30 days

Safer initial threshold:

explicit request_menu_click required
Count mention allowed

Only if:

count is accurate
window is clear
admin approves count usage

Default:

do not mention exact count

Use:

Customers have requested your menu on MenuList.

not:

Many customers have requested your menu.

unless justified.

Owner intent claim

If owner clicked setup/claim, outreach should not say “customers requested.”

Use:

You started MenuList setup here:
{{flow_url}}

or:

Sharing the MenuList setup link again in case useful.
33.18 Demand-to-Growth Lead matching

When a summary crosses threshold:

1. Try match productBusinessId.
2. Try match existing growth lead by dedupe keys.
3. Try match by normalizedName + area + city.
4. If match confidence high, update lead.
5. If medium, human review.
6. If no match, create Growth Lead.

Match confidence:

exact productBusinessId = 1.0
exact leadId from route/surface = 1.0
same normalized name + area + city = 0.80–0.90
same name + city only = 0.60–0.75
fuzzy name only = human review

33.22 Demand campaign workflow
1. Demand summary crosses threshold.
2. Lead created/upgraded.
3. Lead enters saved audience: Customer Requested Menus.
4. Campaign Builder creates demand campaign.
5. Audience preview excludes suppressed/recently contacted leads.
6. Offer angle = customer_request only where claim allowed.
7. Channel Router chooses email/WhatsApp/etc.
8. Message sent with tracked onboarding route.
9. Onboarding outcome attributed to demand signal.

Example message, if claim allowed:

Hi {{business_name}} team,

Customers have requested your menu on MenuList.

You can set up your MenuList menu link here:
{{flow_url}}

No fake urgency.

No inflated numbers.

33.23 Owner intent workflow

When someone clicks “Own this business” or “Set up MenuList link”:

1. Capture owner_claim_click or owner_setup_click.
2. If user enters onboarding, create route/feedback.
3. If user abandons before setup, create high-intent Growth Lead if contact exists.
4. If no contact, save anonymous demand signal.
5. If contact submitted, create/upgrade lead and prioritize immediate follow-up.

Owner intent should usually route to:

existing onboarding flow

not a separate sales conversation.

33.24 Missing business suggestion workflow

If customer suggests a business:

1. Customer submits business name/location.
2. Signal captured as customer_suggested_business.
3. AI normalizes business.
4. Try match existing lead/product business.
5. If not found, create demand summary.
6. If enough info, create Growth Lead.
7. If weak info, hold for aggregation/manual review.

Do not create outreach from vague suggestions like:

“that dosa place near me”

unless match becomes reliable.

Demand surfaces can be abused.

Add controls:

33.50 Final principle

The Demand Signal Capture Engine is the first true distribution flywheel layer.

Outbound asks:

Can we convince this business to care?

Demand-led acquisition says:

Customers are already looking for this business/menu. Let’s help the owner respond.

That is a stronger wedge.

The rule:

Use demand signals to prioritize and personalize acquisition.
Never invent demand.
Never over-contact from weak signals.
Never let raw event volume become Firebase cost.

Spec 34 — Public Surface Acquisition Hooks
34.1 Purpose

The Public Surface Acquisition Hooks module turns MenuList’s customer-facing surfaces into owner-acquisition entry points.

It answers:

Where should MenuList show owner-facing CTAs?
What should those CTAs say?
When should they appear?
Which existing onboarding flow should they route to?
How should the click be tracked?
When should a click create or upgrade a Growth Lead?
How do we avoid damaging the customer-facing experience?

This module is not about cold outreach.

It is about capturing intent already happening on MenuList-owned surfaces.

The core idea:

Every public MenuList surface can quietly ask:
“Is this your business? Set up your MenuList menu link + QR.”

But it must do this without turning customer pages into marketing pages.

34.2 Strategic role

The Growth Engine acquires businesses externally.

Public Surface Acquisition Hooks acquire businesses from MenuList’s own traffic.

This creates an owned loop:

customer visits MenuList surface
→ owner/business sees or clicks setup hook
→ Growth Lead or onboarding route created
→ business completes onboarding
→ business publishes MenuList menu link/QR
→ more customer traffic
→ more owner/business acquisition

This is the beginning of MenuList distribution compounding from its own surfaces.

34.3 Boundary

This module owns:

owner-facing CTA placement
CTA copy
hook eligibility
hook tracking
hook experiments
surface-to-lead creation
surface-to-onboarding routing
surface attribution
hook performance summaries

It does not own:

business verification
claim approval workflow
menu editing
business dashboard
customer-facing page UX itself
QR generation
pricing
MenuList onboarding flow internals
public business truth management

Important:

“Own this business?” is an acquisition hook, not a full claim-management system.

If the owner clicks, they should go into an existing MenuList onboarding/setup flow.

34.4 Core principle

Hooks should be:

subtle
contextual
truthful
owner-oriented
trackable
low-friction

Hooks should not be:

aggressive
spammy
misleading
visually dominant
claiming verified ownership
interrupting customers

The public page’s primary user is still the customer looking for menu/business information.

Owner acquisition is secondary.

34.5 Hook types

Use a fixed taxonomy.

TypeScript
type PublicSurfaceHookType =
  | "own_this_business"
  | "claim_this_business"
  | "setup_menu_link"
  | "create_menu_link_qr"
  | "update_this_menu"
  | "request_menu"
  | "get_this_for_your_restaurant"
  | "add_another_branch"
  | "complete_your_setup"
  | "business_owner_cta";

Meanings:

own_this_business:
Soft CTA for owner identification.

claim_this_business:
Stronger CTA, use carefully only when claim/onboarding path exists.

setup_menu_link:
Direct acquisition CTA.

create_menu_link_qr:
Best generic owner CTA.

update_this_menu:
Use only where update flow exists or routes to onboarding.

request_menu:
Customer-facing demand signal, handled by Demand Signal Capture.

get_this_for_your_restaurant:
Viral acquisition CTA from a menu/customer-facing surface.

add_another_branch:
Post-onboarding or owner-facing branch expansion CTA.

complete_your_setup:
For owners who started but did not complete.

business_owner_cta:
Generic fallback.
34.6 Surface types

Hooks can appear on these surfaces:

TypeScript
type PublicSurfaceType =
  | "unclaimed_business_page"
  | "unclaimed_menu_page"
  | "claimed_menu_page"
  | "business_page"
  | "search_results_page"
  | "no_results_page"
  | "missing_menu_page"
  | "qr_landing_page"
  | "share_page"
  | "request_menu_confirmation"
  | "post_onboarding_success_page"
  | "public_footer";

Each surface needs different hook behavior.

34.7 Surface-by-surface hook strategy
1. Unclaimed business page

Purpose:

convert business owners who find their own page

Recommended hooks:

“Own this business?”
“Set up your MenuList menu link + QR”
“Create a clean menu link for customers”

Placement:

small banner near business header
secondary CTA below main customer content
footer CTA

Do not overdo it.

Primary customer experience should remain intact.

2. Unclaimed menu page

Purpose:

turn missing/weak menu demand into owner onboarding

Recommended hooks:

“Is this your restaurant?”
“Set up the MenuList menu link”
“Create menu link + QR for customers”

Also include customer-side:

“Request this menu”

Customer request goes to Demand Signal Capture.

Owner setup goes to Growth/onboarding route.

3. Claimed menu page

Purpose:

viral distribution, not claim acquisition

Recommended hook:

“Menu by MenuList”
“Get this for your restaurant”

This overlaps with the QR/Menu Link Viral Loop module, but the tracking should still use Public Surface Hooks.

Placement:

small footer
share screen
optional post-view CTA

Do not show “Own this business?” on already claimed pages unless the viewer is the owner and session context supports it.

4. Business page

Purpose:

convert business owners and capture customer demand

Hooks:

owner hook:
“Own this business? Set up your MenuList link.”

customer hook:
“Request menu”

Separate the two paths clearly.

5. Search results page

Purpose:

capture customer demand and owner intent

Hooks:

For search result:

“Is this your business?”

For no result:

“Suggest a business”
“Add your restaurant to MenuList”

Customer suggestion goes to Demand Signal Capture.

Owner add/setup goes to onboarding/Growth.

6. No-results page

Purpose:

convert missing demand into either customer request or owner setup

Two CTAs:

Customer:
“Request a menu”

Owner:
“Add your restaurant”

Keep them separate.

7. Missing menu page

Purpose:

capture explicit demand and route owner setup

Hooks:

Customer:
“Request this menu”

Owner:
“Own this restaurant? Set up the menu link”
8. QR landing page

Purpose:

support customer menu access while preserving viral attribution

Hook:

small footer:
“Create your own MenuList menu link + QR”

Avoid intrusive CTAs.

A QR scan is usually customer intent, not owner intent.

9. Share page

Purpose:

when someone shares a MenuList menu/page, carry acquisition attribution

Hook:

“Get this for your restaurant”

Track referring menu/business.

10. Request-menu confirmation page

Purpose:

after a customer requests a menu, optionally create more demand or owner path

Hooks:

“Know the owner? Share this request.”
“Own this business? Set up the menu link.”

Be careful. Do not turn customer request flow into spam.

11. Post-onboarding success page

Purpose:

branch/referral expansion

Hooks:

“Add another branch”
“Know another restaurant that needs a menu link?”
“Share MenuList with another business”

This feeds Referral and Branch Expansion.

12. Public footer

Purpose:

low-key global acquisition presence

Hook:

“Create a menu link + QR with MenuList”

Keep it small.

34.8 Hook placement principles

For customer-facing menu pages:

hook should never compete with menu content
hook should never block menu access
hook should never feel like an ad overlay
hook should usually be footer or secondary placement

For unclaimed/missing pages:

owner CTA can be stronger
customer request CTA can be prominent

For post-onboarding/admin-adjacent pages:

referral/branch CTA can be more visible

34.14 Cost policy for hook events

Hook events can become high-volume.

Rules:

hook_click:
write to Firestore

owner_contact_submitted:
write to Firestore

setup_started:
write to Firestore

request_menu_clicked:
write to Firestore and Demand Signal Capture

hook_impression:
do not always write raw Firestore doc at high traffic
batch, sample, or send to analytics pipeline
roll up to summaries

Default Firestore raw retention:

hook_click: 90 days or until attributed
owner_contact_submitted: long-term enough for audit
hook_impression: sampled or TTL 7–30 days

Dashboards must read:

distributionHookSummaries
distributionDailyStats
businessDistributionSummaries

not raw events.

Keep it short.

34.18 Owner contact workflow
1. User clicks owner hook.
2. If direct onboarding is available, create tracked route.
3. If contact needed, open short owner contact form.
4. On submission, normalize contact.
5. Dedupe against Growth Leads and suppressions.
6. Create/upgrade Growth Lead.
7. Source = public_surface_owner_intent.
8. Priority = high/urgent.
9. Existing onboarding route created or NBA decides follow-up.

This is a high-intent lead.

It should not sit in cold campaign backlog.

34.19 Direct onboarding route workflow

For strong hooks like:

Create menu link + QR

Flow:

1. Hook clicked.
2. Growth route created.
3. Route attribution stores hookId, surface, business/page.
4. User redirected to existing onboarding flow.
5. onboarding_started/completed feedback returns.
6. Distribution attribution updated.

Route attribution should include:

TypeScript
distribution: {
  source: "public_claim_cta" | "menu_page_footer" | "qr_surface";
  hookId: string;
  surfaceType: PublicSurfaceType;
  surfaceId?: string;
  referringBusinessId?: string;
}
34.20 Hook-to-lead workflow

If a hook click does not start onboarding but gives enough signal:

1. Hook click recorded.
2. Demand/intent summary updated.
3. If owner-like or repeated, create/upgrade Growth Lead.
4. Lead enters Growth Engine with source = public_surface_intent.
5. NBA decides:
   - immediate follow-up
   - send onboarding link
   - human review
   - hold

Weak hook clicks without contact may be aggregated only.

34.21 Owner-like detection

Viewer is owner-like if:

clicked owner hook
opened owner contact form
submitted owner contact
came from business/admin-like path
clicked “update menu”
clicked “claim”
searched exact business repeatedly from same session

Do not over-infer.

Owner-like detection increases priority but does not prove ownership.

34.22 Hook targeting rules

Basic rules:

Do not show claim hook on verified/claimed business to random users.
Do not show update hook unless update/setup path exists.
Do not show customer_request claim unless demand evidence exists.
Do not show aggressive owner CTA on menu content area.
Do not show branch/referral CTA except post-onboarding or owner context.

For unclaimed pages:

show owner setup hook
show request menu hook

For claimed pages:

show subtle “Get this for your restaurant” only

For QR landing pages:

show footer-level viral hook only
34.23 Hook visibility engine

Create a deterministic resolver before any AI optimization.

TypeScript
function shouldShowHook(input: ResolveDistributionHooksInput, hook: DistributionHook) {
  if (hook.status !== "active" && hook.status !== "experiment") return false;

  if (hook.targeting.onlyUnclaimed && input.business?.claimed) return false;

  if (hook.targeting.onlyClaimed && !input.business?.claimed) return false;

  if (hook.targeting.onlyFoodBusiness && !isFoodCategory(input.business?.category)) return false;

  if (hook.targeting.hideForConvertedBusiness && input.business?.onboardingCompleted) return false;

  if (hook.targeting.minDemandScore && (input.demand?.demandScore ?? 0) < hook.targeting.minDemandScore) return false;

  return true;
}

AI can optimize among eligible hooks, not bypass eligibility.

34.24 Hook ranking

If multiple hooks are eligible, rank them.

Hook Rank Score =
  surface fit
+ owner intent fit
+ demand score fit
+ historical completion rate
+ experiment allocation
- UX risk
- dismissal rate

Do not show too many hooks.

Recommended max:

1 primary owner hook
1 secondary customer demand hook
1 subtle footer hook

On menu pages:

usually only footer hook

On unclaimed/missing pages:

primary owner hook + customer request hook
34.25 UX risk score

Each hook has a UX risk score.

TypeScript
type HookUxRisk = {
  hookId: string;

  riskScore: number; // 0-100

  riskFactors: (
    | "too_prominent"
    | "interrupts_menu_view"
    | "modal"
    | "repeated_display"
    | "high_dismissal_rate"
    | "low_completion_rate"
    | "customer_confusion"
  )[];

  recommendedAction:
    | "allow"
    | "reduce_prominence"
    | "move_to_footer"
    | "pause"
    | "experiment_only";
};

This prevents the public surface from becoming acquisition-heavy.

Do not pick winner by click-through alone.

Public Surface Hooks should call Demand Signal Capture for relevant events.

34.37 Safety and trust rules

Do not show misleading hooks.

Examples:

Bad:

Claim your official MenuList profile

unless claim/verification exists.

Better:

Set up your MenuList menu link

Bad:

Customers are waiting for your menu

unless evidence supports it.

Better:

Create a clean menu link for customers

Bad:

Your menu is missing

Better:

Set up a MenuList menu link + QR
34.38 Customer experience guardrails

Track:

hook dismissal rate
customer confusion reports
bounce/exit after hook shown
menu task completion
negative feedback

If hook harms customer experience:

move to footer
reduce frequency
pause
change copy
show only on unclaimed/missing pages

Do not sacrifice menu usability for owner acquisition.

34.39 Frequency rules

Avoid repeated hook harassment.

For anonymous/session users:

do not show same modal repeatedly
do not show owner CTA after dismissal for cooldown period
footer hooks are okay
inline hooks can be limited

type HookFrequencyPolicy = {
  hookId: string;

  maxImpressionsPerSession?: number;

34.40 Owner contact spam handling

Some submissions may be spam.

Signals:

invalid phone/email
non-business text
bot-like repeated submissions
mismatched business
abusive content

Workflow:

owner contact submitted
→ validate
→ if strong, create/update Growth Lead
→ if weak, human review
→ if spam, reject and optionally suppress actor/session
34.41 Firebase cost strategy

High-volume surfaces must be careful.

Raw event strategy
write clicks and submissions
sample impressions
aggregate impressions server-side/client-side if high volume
export raw impressions to analytics/BigQuery if needed
Summary docs

Read:

distributionHookSummaries
distributionDailyStats
businessDistributionSummaries
TTL

TTL low-value raw events.

hook_impression raw: 7–30 days
hook_click raw: 90 days
owner_contact_submitted: longer
setup_started: tied to route/feedback
Avoid
real-time listener on hook events

per-impression Firestore writes on high-traffic pages
34.42 Recommended first implementation slice

Build these first:

1. distributionHooks collection
2. hook resolver API
3. hook_click event tracking
4. owner_setup_click tracking
5. owner_contact_submitted form
6. route creation from setup hook
7. hook-to-Growth Lead creation
8. hook summaries
9. public hooks dashboard
10. customer_request integration for request_menu hook

Surfaces to start with:

unclaimed business/menu page
missing menu page
claimed menu page footer
post-onboarding success page

Do not start with every page and every impression.

34.43 Acceptance criteria

This module is ready when:

1. Product surfaces can request eligible hooks from a resolver.
2. Hooks can render with approved copy and placement.
3. Hook clicks are tracked.
4. Owner setup clicks create tracked onboarding routes.
5. Owner contact submissions create or update Growth Leads.
6. Request menu hooks create Demand Signals.
7. Hook-created leads have distribution attribution.
8. Hook-created routes feed onboarding feedback.
9. Hook dashboard shows click → start → completion funnel.
10. Unsupported claims are blocked.
11. Raw impression events do not create Firestore cost risk.
12. Hooks can be paused instantly.
34.44 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Hooks hurt customer UX

Fix:

subtle placement
dismissal tracking
footer-first hooks
pause high-risk hooks
UX guardrail metrics
Failure mode 2 — Hooks imply verified claim

Fix:

use “Set up MenuList link” instead of heavy “claim” wording unless verification exists
Failure mode 3 — Hook clicks do not attribute

Fix:

all hook actions create distributionAttribution and tracked route
Failure mode 4 — Firestore cost spike

Fix:

do not write every impression
summary docs
BigQuery/export
TTL
Failure mode 5 — Owner contact spam

Fix:

validation
rate limits
human review
spam flags
Failure mode 6 — Customer_request claim used incorrectly

Fix:

claim eligibility required
message guardrail check
claim usage audit
34.45 Final contract

The Public Surface Acquisition Hooks module must guarantee:

1. Every hook is approved and trackable.
2. Hooks appear only where eligible.
3. Hooks do not damage the customer menu experience.
4. Owner actions route to existing onboarding or Growth Engine.
5. Customer request actions route to Demand Signal Capture.
6. Hook-created leads are deduped and suppression-checked.
7. Hook-created routes are tracked.
8. Hook performance is judged by onboarding completion.
9. Unsupported demand/ownership claims are blocked.
10. Firestore does not store high-volume raw impressions by default.
34.46 Final principle

Public Surface Acquisition Hooks turn MenuList’s own surfaces into acquisition infrastructure.

The right behavior is:

A customer uses MenuList normally.
An owner can easily find a setup path.
Every owner action is tracked.
Every completed onboarding is attributed.
The public surface stays clean.

This creates owned distribution without turning MenuList into an ad-heavy or claim-management product.

Next spec item: QR / Menu Link Viral Loop.

Spec 35 — QR / Menu Link Viral Loop
35.1 Purpose

The QR / Menu Link Viral Loop turns every MenuList menu link and QR code into a distribution surface.

The goal is simple:

Every business that uses MenuList should quietly help MenuList acquire more businesses.

The loop:

business creates MenuList menu link + QR
→ customers scan/open/share the menu
→ MenuList brand/link is seen in a useful context
→ another business owner clicks “Get this for your restaurant”
→ Growth Lead or onboarding route is created
→ new business completes onboarding
→ new business creates more MenuList links/QRs

This is not paid marketing.

This is distribution embedded into the product’s natural usage surface.

35.2 Strategic value

The strongest MenuList distribution object is:

a customer-facing menu link + QR

Every onboarded restaurant/cafe becomes a node in the network:

in-store QR
WhatsApp menu link
Instagram bio menu link
shared menu link
public menu page
footer attribution

If designed correctly, MenuList growth becomes less dependent on:

scraping
cold outbound
paid ads
manual lead-gen

and more driven by:

usage
visibility
shares
QR scans
owner curiosity
customer demand
referrals

This is the compounding layer.

35.3 Boundary

This module owns:

QR/menu-link distribution attribution
viral CTA tracking
referring business attribution
menu footer acquisition hooks
QR scan attribution
share attribution
get-this-for-your-restaurant flows
distribution lead creation
distribution summaries
viral loop experiments

It does not own:

menu page UX itself
menu data
QR code design/product generation logic
restaurant onboarding UX
business dashboard
business verification
menu editing
pricing
customer-facing product features

Product owns:

menu page
QR generation/download
business menu link
customer-facing menu experience

Distribution Flywheel owns:

tracking, attribution, acquisition hooks, and growth routing around those surfaces
35.4 Core principle

The viral loop must be:

subtle
useful
attributed
low-friction
non-invasive
brand-safe

It must not make MenuList menus feel like ad pages.

The customer came to see the menu.

The business owner or adjacent operator may discover MenuList secondarily.

So the public experience priority is:

1. customer menu access
2. business utility
3. subtle MenuList distribution

Never reverse that order.

35.5 Main loops

There are five viral loops.

1. QR scan loop
2. Menu link share loop
3. Menu footer CTA loop
4. Business owner copy loop
5. Post-onboarding branch/referral loop
Loop 1 — QR scan loop
customer scans MenuList QR
→ opens MenuList menu
→ sees subtle MenuList attribution
→ another business owner/customer clicks “Get this for your restaurant”
→ onboarding route created

This is strongest in-store.

Loop 2 — Menu link share loop
business shares MenuList menu on WhatsApp/Instagram
→ recipient opens menu
→ MenuList distribution hook visible
→ new business lead created if owner intent appears

This is strongest for WhatsApp/social distribution.

Loop 3 — Menu footer CTA loop
visitor reaches bottom/footer of menu
→ sees “Create your menu link + QR”
→ clicks
→ routed to existing onboarding flow

This is the simplest owned distribution hook.

Loop 4 — Business owner copy loop
restaurant owner sees another restaurant’s MenuList page
→ wants similar menu link/QR
→ clicks “Get this for your restaurant”
→ starts onboarding

This is likely to happen through competitors, friends, agencies, customers, or local discovery.

Loop 5 — Post-onboarding branch/referral loop
business completes onboarding
→ sees “Add another branch” or “Share with another restaurant”
→ new branch/referral lead created

This connects to the Referral and Branch Expansion Engine.

35.6 Core objects

New collections:

qrDistributionAssets
menuLinkDistributionEvents
menuLinkDistributionSummaries
businessDistributionSummaries
menuLinkReferralTokens
distributionAttributions
distributionDailyStats

Existing collections reused:

growthLeads
growthLeadRoutes
growthFeedbackEvents
distributionHooks
distributionSurfaceEvents
businessReferralSignals
partnerReferralEvents
35.7 QR distribution asset

Each QR should have a durable tracking identity.

Collection:

qrDistributionAssets
TypeScript
type QrDistributionAsset = {
  id: string;

  productBusinessId: string;
  menuPageId?: string;

  qrType:
    | "in_store_table"
    | "counter"
    | "print_menu"
    | "poster"
    | "packaging"
    | "social"
    | "downloaded"
    | "unknown";

  status:
    | "active"
    | "paused"
    | "revoked"
    | "deprecated";

  destination: {
    menuUrl: string;
    menuPageId?: string;
  };

  tracking: {
    qrTokenHash: string;
    shortPath: string; // /q/{token}
    campaignId?: string;
    createdFrom?: "onboarding" | "business_dashboard" | "operator" | "system";
  };

  attribution: {
    source: "qr_surface";
    productBusinessId: string;
    referringBusinessId?: string;
  };

  stats: {
    scans: number;
    uniqueScanActors?: number;
    menuOpens: number;
    footerCtaClicks: number;
    referredLeads: number;
    referredOnboardingStarts: number;
    referredOnboardingCompletions: number;
  };

  createdAt: Date;
  updatedAt: Date;
};
35.8 QR URL strategy

For printed or downloaded QR codes, use a durable short route:

menulist.com/q/{qrToken}

Flow:

/q/{qrToken}
→ validate token
→ record qr_scan event
→ resolve current menu destination
→ redirect to menu page

Why use a redirect route:

destination can change later
QR remains durable
scan is attributable
referring business is known
campaign/source is known

Do not put sensitive data in the QR URL.

Bad:

menulist.com/menu?businessId=abc&ownerPhone=...

Good:

menulist.com/q/x7Kp92Lm

35.12 Cost policy for menu link events

Some events can be high-volume.

High-volume:

qr_scan
menu_link_open
footer_cta_impression

Higher-value:

footer_cta_click
get_this_for_restaurant_click
create_menu_link_click
owner_setup_started
referred_lead_created
referred_onboarding_completed

Firestore policy:

Do not write every menu_link_open to Firestore if traffic becomes high.
Do not write every footer_cta_impression to Firestore at high volume.
Do write clicks, setup starts, lead creations, and completions.
Use summaries and BigQuery/analytics for high-volume raw events.

Dashboard reads:

menuLinkDistributionSummaries
businessDistributionSummaries
distributionDailyStats

not raw events.

35.15 Distribution score formula
Business Distribution Score =
  QR scan volume
+ menu link open volume
+ share volume
+ footer CTA clicks
+ referred leads
+ referred onboarding completions
+ recency

Suggested weighting:

QR scans: low/medium value
menu opens: low value
shares: medium value
footer CTA clicks: high value
referred leads: high value
referred onboarding completions: very high value

Example:

1000 QR scans but no referred leads = visible but not distribution-converting
20 referred leads and 5 completions = strong distribution node
35.16 Menu footer CTA

The simplest viral loop is a footer CTA.

Approved examples:

Menu by MenuList
Create your menu link + QR
Get this for your restaurant

Recommended footer pattern:

Small attribution:
Menu by MenuList

Secondary CTA:
Create your menu link + QR

Keep it subtle.

Do not add:

large banners
popups
modal interruptions
repeated prompts

on customer menu pages.

35.17 CTA click workflow

When user clicks:

Create your menu link + QR

Flow:

1. Record footer_cta_click or get_this_for_restaurant_click.
2. Create distribution attribution with referring business/menu.
3. Create growth route to existing onboarding flow.
4. If user enters onboarding, feedback links back to referring business.
5. If user abandons and contact exists later, create Growth Lead.

If no business/contact info is known:

route directly to onboarding
attribute by route
no Growth Lead until onboarding starts or contact is captured

35.23 Owner-like signal from QR/menu surface

A QR/menu visitor becomes owner-like if they:

click “Create your menu link + QR”
click “Get this for your restaurant”
open owner contact/setup form
start onboarding
submit business contact
click from business dashboard/referral context

A normal QR scan is not owner intent.

Do not create Growth Lead from customer menu scan alone.

35.24 Viral lead creation

When someone starts onboarding from a viral CTA:

1. Create growth route.
2. Existing onboarding collects business info.
3. Feedback event creates or links Growth Lead.
4. Source = qr_surface / menu_page_footer / menu_link_share.
5. Referring business attribution stored.

If contact form exists before onboarding:

create Growth Lead immediately

Lead source example:

TypeScript
lead.source = {
  primaryProvider: "menulist_distribution",
  primarySourceType: "menu_link_viral_loop",
  importedAt: now
};

Add:

TypeScript
lead.distribution = {
  source: "menu_page_footer",
  referringProductBusinessId,
  referringMenuPageId,
  qrAssetId,
  referralTokenId
};

or distributionAttribution if anonymous route

businessReferralSignal created/linked
35.37 Integration with Market Coverage Map

Koramangala cafes are generating QR/menu referrals.
Increase cluster campaign there.
35.38 Integration with Growth Engine

When viral lead/contact exists:

source = menulist_distribution
sourceType = qr_menu_viral_loop

Recommended lead intelligence boost:

owner_setup_started → high intent
get_this_for_restaurant_click + contact → high intent
footer CTA click only → medium intent
QR scan only → no lead

NBA should route:

owner_setup_started → send/resume onboarding
contact submitted → immediate follow-up
footer CTA click with no contact → wait/aggregate
35.39 Integration with onboarding feedback

Route attribution must connect to feedback.

Flow:

1. Viral CTA creates growthLeadRoute.
2. User starts onboarding.
3. recordGrowthFeedback receives routeId.
4. route.status = started/completed.
5. distributionAttribution outcome updated.
6. referring business summary updated.
7. campaign/source/channel stats updated if applicable.

This is how viral loop performance becomes measurable.

35.40 Firebase cost strategy

High-volume risk:

menu_link_open
qr_scan
footer_impression

Cost-safe design:

1. Use redirect route logging for QR scans only where necessary.
2. Batch/aggregate high-volume opens.
3. Store raw clicks/setup starts in Firestore.
4. Store high-volume raw events in analytics/BigQuery or sample.
5. Keep Firestore summaries for dashboards.
6. Use TTL for raw events.

Suggested Firestore writes:

qr_scan:
write summary increment; raw event sampled or stored with TTL depending volume

footer_cta_click:
write raw event + summary

get_this_for_restaurant_click:
write raw event + summary + route

owner_setup_started:
write raw event + route/lead attribution

referred_onboarding_completed:
write durable attribution event
35.41 Summary update pattern

For a footer CTA click:

1. menuLinkDistributionEvents write
2. menuLinkDistributionSummary update
3. businessDistributionSummary update
4. distributionDailyStats update

Do not update many unrelated summaries synchronously.

For onboarding completion:

1. growthFeedbackEvent
2. distributionAttribution outcome update
3. businessDistributionSummary update
4. campaign/source summary if campaign exists
35.42 Indexes

Recommended indexes:

qrDistributionAssets:
- productBusinessId ASC, status ASC
- tracking.qrTokenHash ASC

menuLinkDistributionEvents:
- source.productBusinessId ASC, createdAt DESC
- source.qrAssetId ASC, createdAt DESC
- eventType ASC, createdAt DESC
- result.growthLeadId ASC, createdAt DESC

menuLinkDistributionSummaries:
- productBusinessId ASC
- period.window ASC, counts.referredOnboardingCompletions DESC

businessDistributionSummaries:
- distribution.score DESC
- business.city ASC, business.area ASC, distribution.score DESC

Avoid indexing:

path
userAgentHash
reason arrays
raw actor metadata
35.43 Operating workflow

Daily:

review new viral leads
review owner-intent CTA clicks
review referred onboarding starts
check top referring businesses
check any UX/dismissal warnings

Weekly:

review viral loop completion rate
review footer CTA variants
review QR scan to owner conversion
identify high-distribution businesses
identify clusters with organic spread

Monthly:

distribution share of total onboardings
best referring businesses
cluster-level viral growth
decision: increase footer/QR hook experiments or keep stable

Secondary:

get-this click rate

35.45 What not to build

Do not build yet:

complex referral rewards

Those can create complexity or harm UX before attribution proves the loop.

Build:

tracking
subtle CTAs
route attribution

experiments

first.

35.46 First implementation slice

Build first:

1. qrDistributionAssets
2. /q/{qrToken} redirect route
3. footer CTA: “Create your menu link + QR”
4. footer CTA click tracking
5. growth route creation from footer CTA
6. distributionAttribution for route
7. onboarding feedback attribution
8. businessDistributionSummary
9. viral loop dashboard

Start with only:

claimed menu page footer
QR redirect tracking
post-onboarding share/copy action tracking

Do not instrument every page view on day one.

35.47 Acceptance criteria

This module is ready when:

1. QR codes can resolve through tracked durable routes.
2. QR scans can be attributed to a business/QR asset.
3. Menu footer CTA can create a tracked onboarding route.
4. Onboarding completions from footer/QR routes are attributed.
5. Existing businesses receive internal distribution scores.
6. Dashboard shows QR/menu loop funnel.
7. Raw high-volume events do not create Firestore cost risk.
8. Hooks can be paused/experimented.
9. Customer menu experience remains clean.
10. No unsupported claims are shown.
35.48 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Menu pages become ad-heavy

Fix:

footer-first design
no popups
UX guardrail metrics
pause high-risk hooks
Failure mode 2 — QR URL cannot change later

Fix:

use /q/{qrToken} redirect route
Failure mode 3 — No attribution from viral leads

Fix:

all footer/QR onboarding routes carry distribution attribution
Failure mode 4 — Firestore cost spikes from scans/views

Fix:

summary-first tracking
sample raw events
BigQuery for high-volume analytics
TTL raw events
Failure mode 5 — CTA clicks do not become leads

Fix:

direct route to onboarding
optional owner contact capture
NBA follow-up for started-not-completed
Failure mode 6 — Referring business attribution is lost

Fix:

route attribution must include referringProductBusinessId/menuPageId/qrAssetId
35.49 Final contract

The QR / Menu Link Viral Loop must guarantee:

1. Every QR asset has a durable attribution identity.
2. Every viral CTA click is tracked.
3. Every setup route from a menu/QR surface is attributed.
4. Referring businesses can be credited internally.
5. Distribution performance is measured by completed onboardings.
6. Customer menu experience remains primary.
7. High-volume events do not overload Firestore.
8. The loop feeds the Growth Engine, not a separate product flow.
35.50 Final principle

The QR/menu link loop is MenuList’s natural distribution advantage.

A restaurant does not just become a customer.

It becomes a surface.

Its menu link, QR code, footer, shares, and customer usage can all create more MenuList demand.

The correct loop is:

business uses MenuList
→ customers open MenuList
→ other owners discover MenuList
→ new businesses onboard
→ more MenuList surfaces exist

That is how MenuList starts compounding from usage instead of only from outreach.

Spec 36 — Google Menu-Link Opportunity Engine
36.1 Purpose

The Google Menu-Link Opportunity Engine identifies restaurants, cafes, bakeries, dessert shops, and food businesses where MenuList has a strong acquisition wedge around a simple idea:

One clean MenuList menu link can be used wherever customers look for the business:
Google profile, WhatsApp, Instagram, QR, website, and in-store.

This module does not manage Google Business Profiles.

It does not edit Google listings.

It does not promise Google ranking, SEO improvement, more orders, or GBP optimization.

Its job is narrower:

detect businesses that likely need a clean customer-facing menu link
→ score the opportunity
→ choose safe acquisition angle
→ feed those leads into the Growth Engine
→ route interested owners into existing MenuList onboarding

Google’s official Business Profile help says restaurants can manage menu content and add a “Menu link” by entering the URL where their menu can be found, which makes a clean MenuList URL a useful owner-facing asset. Google also says restaurant profiles can manage menu content, menu URLs, and menu photos/PDFs.
Google Help
+1

36.2 Core positioning

The correct external positioning is:

MenuList gives restaurants one clean menu link + QR that they can share across customer-facing places.

Optional channel-specific wording:

You can use the same MenuList link on WhatsApp, Instagram, QR, website, and public profiles where customers look for your menu.

Avoid saying:

We manage your Google profile.
We found you on Google Maps.
Your Google menu is missing.
Your Google listing is incomplete.
Your profile is bad.
We will improve your Google ranking.

This module should use Google/menu-profile signals internally, but the outreach should stay clean and non-creepy.

36.3 Strategic value

This is a strong acquisition wedge because most food businesses understand the problem:

customers ask for the menu
customers check Google/WhatsApp/Instagram
menus are often scattered across PDFs, photos, old links, Instagram posts, or no link at all
QR menus need a simple destination

MenuList’s wedge:

one clean menu link + QR

The internal strategic meaning:

MenuList becomes the canonical customer-facing menu link that can travel across public discovery surfaces.

But do not say that to SMB owners.

Say:

clean menu link + QR for customers
36.4 Boundary

This module owns:

Google/profile/menu-link opportunity detection
menu-link gap scoring
safe acquisition angle recommendation
lead scoring boost
campaign audience creation
message guardrails
opportunity dashboard
Google-menu-link campaign analytics

It does not own:

Google Business Profile editing
GBP API writes
business verification
Google ranking/SEO promises
menu transcription
Google Posts
review management
order/reservation management
product onboarding
MenuList customer-facing menu page logic

If later MenuList supports owner-authorized GBP updates, that should be a separate explicitly scoped product/integration. This spec does not assume or require that.

36.5 Core idea

The engine should answer:

Does this business have a strong reason to want a clean MenuList menu link?

Not:

Can we update their Google listing?

The useful signal is not only “Google menu missing.” The useful signal is broader:

this business likely lacks a clean, durable, customer-facing menu URL.

That is the MenuList opportunity.

36.6 Opportunity types

Use a fixed taxonomy.

TypeScript
type GoogleMenuLinkOpportunityType =
  | "no_website"
  | "no_clear_menu_link"
  | "menu_link_missing_or_unclear"
  | "pdf_menu"
  | "image_menu"
  | "instagram_only_menu"
  | "old_or_broken_menu_link"
  | "multiple_confusing_menu_sources"
  | "public_profile_menu_link_opportunity"
  | "customer_demand_for_menu"
  | "qr_destination_needed"
  | "unknown";

Meaning:

no_website:
Business appears to have no owned website.

no_clear_menu_link:
Business may have some online presence, but no clean customer-facing menu link is obvious.

menu_link_missing_or_unclear:
Public profile/menu link signal is weak, missing, or unclear.

pdf_menu:
Menu appears to exist as a PDF, not a clean mobile menu link.

image_menu:
Menu appears to exist as images/photos.

instagram_only_menu:
Business relies mainly on Instagram posts/highlights/bio for menu.

old_or_broken_menu_link:
Menu URL is broken, outdated, redirected badly, or inaccessible.

multiple_confusing_menu_sources:
Customers may see multiple menu sources, creating inconsistency.

public_profile_menu_link_opportunity:
Business could benefit from one clean link to use on customer-facing public profiles.

customer_demand_for_menu:
MenuList has actual demand/request signals for this business.

qr_destination_needed:
Business is a good candidate for QR menu usage.
36.7 Opportunity signal sources

Possible signal inputs:

Apify / Google Maps source data
business website crawl
website menu-link extraction
social profile extraction
MenuList demand signals
MenuList public surface interactions
operator review
manual upload/import
lead reply / owner message
existing MenuList onboarding feedback

Important:

Do not depend on one source.
Do not trust one scraped field blindly.
Do not contact from weak/uncertain signal alone.

36.9 Opportunity scoring

Use an interpretable score.

Opportunity Score =
  menu need
+ business fit
+ customer demand
+ channel/contactability
+ QR/share utility
- risk

Suggested weights:

Menu need:              35
Business fit:           20
Customer demand:        20
Contactability:         10
QR/share utility:       10
Freshness/confidence:    5
Risk penalty:          -30 max

Examples:

No website + food business + phone/email + no clear menu link:
high opportunity

Instagram-only cafe + active Instagram:
high opportunity for instagram_bio_menu

Customer requested menu:
urgent/high opportunity if claim eligibility exists

Business already has clean modern menu link:
low opportunity or different angle

Large chain with central site:
human review or lower priority
36.10 Score thresholds
85–100:
high-priority campaign/contact candidate

70–84:
campaign eligible

55–69:
enrich or hold, depending contactability

40–54:
low priority / monitor

<40:
ignore or reject for this angle

Customer demand override:

customer_request claim allowed → priority boost

Owner intent override:

owner/setup signal → urgent/high, regardless of Google-menu-link score

Messaging should not use direct negative claims even with evidence unless explicitly approved.

Use evidence to prioritize, not to shame the business.

36.19 Google menu-link campaign workflow

do not store full website crawl text in Firestore
store crawl summary only
store raw crawl in Cloud Storage if needed
dashboard reads stats/summaries
opportunity list uses bounded query
BigQuery for opportunity analytics
36.37 Indexes

Recommended:

googleMenuLinkOpportunities:
- status ASC, score.opportunityScore DESC
- recommendation.recommendedAction ASC, score.opportunityScore DESC
- business.normalizedCity ASC, business.normalizedArea ASC, score.opportunityScore DESC
- opportunityType ASC, score.opportunityScore DESC
- leadId ASC

googleMenuLinkOpportunityStats:
- scope.campaignId ASC
- scope.opportunityType ASC

Avoid indexing:

evidence.summary
large evidence arrays
raw crawl fields
36.38 First implementation slice

Build:

1. opportunity schema
2. rule-based detector using existing lead/source fields
3. simple AI detector for high-value leads
4. opportunity score
5. saved audience: High Menu-Link Opportunity
6. safe template: menu_link_qr / public profile menu link
7. campaign dry-run guardrails
8. dashboard list
9. attribution to onboarding completions

Do not start with complex GBP/API integration.

Do not start with automated website crawling at large scale.

Start with:

source data + no website + demand signals + category + contactability

Then add enrichment.

36.39 Acceptance criteria

This module is ready when:

1. Leads can receive a menu-link opportunity score.
2. Opportunity type is stored and visible.
3. Saved audience can target high-score opportunities.
4. Campaign can use safe menu-link/public-profile angle.
5. Messages cannot mention Google scraping or GBP management.
6. Customer_request angle is allowed only with demand evidence.
7. Onboarding completions are attributed to opportunity type.
8. Dashboard shows opportunity → contacted → started → completed.
9. Weak/uncertain opportunities go to enrichment or review.
10. Firebase dashboards read summaries, not raw evidence.
36.40 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Drifts into GBP management

Fix:

strict messaging guardrails
no GBP write APIs
no “manage Google profile” copy
Failure mode 2 — Creepy outreach

Fix:

do not mention scraping/source
use generic customer-facing menu link value
Failure mode 3 — False menu-missing claims

Fix:

do not use negative claims
use safe positive promise
Failure mode 4 — Customer_request overuse

Fix:

demandClaimEligibility required
claim usage audit
Failure mode 5 — Low-quality source creates bad opportunities

Fix:

source quality scoring
human review for low confidence
enrichment threshold
Failure mode 6 — Crawling cost explodes

Fix:

crawl only A/B leads or campaign candidates
store summaries
use cost caps
36.41 Final contract

The Google Menu-Link Opportunity Engine must guarantee:

1. It detects menu-link opportunity, not Google-management opportunity.
2. It recommends safe MenuList offer angles.
3. It never requires or implies GBP control.
4. It never uses unsupported negative claims.
5. It uses customer_request wording only with evidence.
6. It feeds existing Growth Engine campaigns.
7. It routes interested leads into existing MenuList onboarding flows.
8. It measures success by completed onboardings.
9. It is cost-controlled through summaries and selective enrichment.
36.42 Final principle

This module should make MenuList’s acquisition message sharper:

One clean menu link + QR for every place customers ask for your menu.

Google/public-profile context is useful because restaurant owners understand customer discovery there.

But MenuList should not position itself as a Google-management tool.

The correct long-term wedge is:

MenuList becomes the clean customer-facing menu link that owners can use across discovery, messaging, and in-store surfaces.
