Spec 37 — Meta Paid Intent Engine
37.1 Purpose

The Meta Paid Intent Engine brings paid and semi-warm demand from Meta into the MenuList Growth Engine.

It handles:

Meta Lead Ads
Click-to-WhatsApp ads
Click-to-Instagram Direct ads
Click-to-Messenger ads
retargeting campaigns
paid social lead follow-up
downstream conversion feedback back to Meta

This is not a separate marketing stack.

It is a paid-intent intake layer that turns Meta-generated intent into structured MenuList acquisition state:

Meta lead / message / click
→ Growth Lead
→ AI scoring
→ channel routing
→ existing MenuList onboarding route
→ feedback + attribution
→ campaign optimization

Meta supports Lead Ads webhooks for real-time lead notifications, official click-to-WhatsApp ad integrations, ads that click to Instagram Direct, and Conversions API / CRM integrations for sending downstream funnel data back to Meta.
Facebook Developers
+3
Facebook Developers
+3
Facebook Developers
+3

37.2 Strategic role

The rest of the Growth Engine handles:

cold lead supply
owned distribution
inbound organic signals
public hooks
QR/menu link loops
referrals

The Meta Paid Intent Engine adds:

paid warm intent

This matters because cold outbound has friction.

Paid intent can produce leads who have already done one of these:

submitted a form
clicked WhatsApp
opened Instagram DM
opened Messenger
engaged with a MenuList ad
clicked a retargeting ad

That lead should not be treated the same as a cold Apify lead.

It should enter a faster path:

paid intent lead
→ immediate scoring
→ immediate response
→ onboarding link / assisted follow-up
→ attribution back to ad/campaign
37.3 Boundary

This module owns:

Meta lead intake
Meta click-to-message attribution
paid lead normalization
paid lead scoring boost
paid campaign attribution
paid follow-up workflow
paid-intent inbox routing
Meta campaign performance summaries
conversion feedback back to Meta, if configured
paid audience retargeting inputs

It does not own:

Meta creative design
Meta media buying strategy
MenuList product onboarding
pricing
business verification
menu creation
restaurant CRM
customer support

It integrates paid Meta demand into the Growth Engine.

It does not become an ads manager clone.

37.4 Core principle

Paid intent should be routed faster than cold outbound but still pass through the same safety layers.

Paid intent lead flow:

Meta lead received
→ normalize
→ dedupe
→ suppression check
→ Growth Lead create/update
→ AI Lead Intelligence
→ Channel Identity Registry
→ Channel Eligibility
→ AI Channel Router
→ Existing Onboarding Flow Router
→ Message Template + Guardrails
→ Channel Execution / Inbox
→ Feedback Attribution

Paid intent does not bypass:

suppression
DNC
message safety
channel policy
eligibility
onboarding route tracking

Paid intent changes priority, not safety rules.

37.5 Supported Meta acquisition paths

The module should support four paths.

1. Meta Lead Ads / Instant Forms
2. Click-to-WhatsApp ads
3. Click-to-Instagram Direct ads
4. Click-to-Messenger ads

Later:

retargeting audiences
lookalike/source audience exports
Conversions API / CRM funnel feedback
37.6 Path 1 — Meta Lead Ads / Instant Forms
Purpose

Capture business-owner leads through forms.

Example lead form questions:

Business name
City / area
Business category
Phone
Email
Do you want a menu link + QR?
Preferred contact method

Meta’s Lead Ads webhook integration can send lead notifications in real time, which is the right pattern for fast Growth Engine ingestion.
Facebook Developers
+1

Best use

Use Lead Ads for:

owner/contact capture
city/category campaigns
retargeting owner-like audiences
testing business-owner demand
lower-friction setup interest
Not ideal for
complex onboarding
long education
highly qualified sales conversations

Forms can generate low-quality leads if the question design is too loose.

37.7 Path 2 — Click-to-WhatsApp ads
Purpose

Drive business owners directly into a WhatsApp conversation.

Meta has official documentation for ads that click to WhatsApp.
Facebook Developers

Best use

Use Click-to-WhatsApp for:

restaurant/cafe owners who prefer direct chat
high-intent “send menu link setup” campaigns
A/B tests where WhatsApp response is likely stronger
local cluster campaigns
Growth Engine behavior

When user messages through WhatsApp:

webhook creates/updates Growth Lead
WhatsApp identity created
conversation created
reply classifier detects intent
NBA sends onboarding route or asks minimal qualification

This is inbound/warm WhatsApp, not cold outbound.

37.8 Path 3 — Click-to-Instagram Direct ads
Purpose

Drive owners into Instagram DMs.

Meta business help describes ads that click to Instagram Direct as ads shown in Instagram Feed or Stories that allow people to start a message with the business by clicking the ad.
Facebook

Best use

Use Click-to-Instagram for:

Instagram-heavy cafes
dessert shops
bakeries
visual food brands
owners already active on Instagram
Growth Engine behavior

When inbound DM arrives:

Instagram identity created
conversation created
AI reply classifier runs
send setup link if intent clear
route to Instagram-friendly onboarding flow

This should remain inbound/reply-window based.

Do not convert it into cold Instagram DM blasting.

37.9 Path 4 — Click-to-Messenger ads
Purpose

Drive owners into a Messenger conversation from Facebook/Meta ads.

Meta Business documentation describes lead-generation flows using Instagram Direct, Messenger, or WhatsApp as message destinations.
Facebook

Best use

Use Messenger for:

Facebook-heavy local businesses
older SMB operators
businesses responding from Facebook Page context
click-to-message lead generation experiments
Growth Engine behavior

Same as Instagram:

inbound message
→ conversation
→ classifier
→ onboarding route
→ attribution

37.17 Paid lead normalization workflow
1. Lead Ads webhook received.
2. Verify webhook.
3. Store compact metaPaidEvent.
4. Retrieve lead details if required.
5. Apply form field mapping.
6. Normalize business name, email, phone, city, area, category.
7. Generate dedupe keys.
8. Check suppression.
9. Match existing Growth Lead.
10. Create/update Growth Lead.
11. Run AI Lead Intelligence.
12. Create paid intent attribution.
13. Trigger Next-Best-Action.

No manual spreadsheet handoff.

37.18 Paid lead scoring

Paid leads should get an intent boost, but not automatic qualification.

Paid intent score:

lead form submitted = strong intent
click-to-message inbound = strong intent
replied to ad conversation = strong intent
business info complete = stronger
valid phone/email = stronger
category/city fit = stronger

But reject or review if:

wrong category
consumer not business
missing business name
invalid contact
duplicate suppressed lead
spam response
outside target geography

Add to Lead Intelligence:

TypeScript
paidIntent?: {
  sourceType:
    | "lead_ad"
    | "click_to_whatsapp"
    | "click_to_instagram"
    | "click_to_messenger";

  intentScore: number;
  formCompletenessScore?: number;
  adCampaignId?: string;
  adId?: string;
};
37.19 Paid lead priority

Recommended NBA priority:

owner/contact submitted via Lead Ad:
high

click-to-WhatsApp inbound:
urgent/high if asks setup/details

click-to-Instagram inbound:
high if active window and intent clear

click-to-Messenger inbound:
high if active window and intent clear

retargeting ad click from existing warm lead:
high if prior clicked/started

Paid intent decays quickly.

Response should be fast.

37.20 Meta Lead Ads workflow
1. Business owner submits instant form.
2. Meta webhook notifies MenuList.
3. MenuList retrieves/normalizes lead.
4. Dedupe + suppression check.
5. Growth Lead created/updated.
6. AI Lead Intelligence scores.
7. Channel Router selects best follow-up:
   - WhatsApp if phone and allowed
   - email if email
   - call/manual if high value
8. Flow Router creates existing onboarding route.
9. Message sent/prepared.
10. Onboarding feedback updates Meta attribution.

Default follow-up:

fast, short, direct

Example:

Hi {{business_name}}, thanks for your interest in MenuList.

You can set up your menu link + QR here:
{{flow_url}}
37.21 Click-to-WhatsApp workflow
1. User clicks ad to WhatsApp.
2. User sends message.
3. WhatsApp webhook receives inbound.
4. Match to Meta ad/campaign if metadata available.
5. Create Growth Lead / conversation.
6. Reply Classifier detects intent.
7. If clear interest, send onboarding route.
8. If unclear, ask one qualifying question.
9. Feedback attributes completion to ad/campaign.

This is the ideal WhatsApp path because the user initiated.

But still respect WhatsApp policy windows and DNC.

37.22 Click-to-Instagram workflow
1. User clicks Instagram Direct ad.
2. User sends DM.
3. Instagram webhook receives message.
4. Create/match Growth Lead.
5. Conversation enters Unified Inbox.
6. Classifier detects intent.
7. Reply with setup link if appropriate.
8. Route to Instagram-friendly onboarding flow.
9. Attribute completion to ad/campaign.

Do not use this to justify cold DMs.

Only reply to initiated conversations.

37.23 Click-to-Messenger workflow
1. User clicks Messenger ad.
2. User starts conversation.
3. Messenger webhook receives message.
4. Create/match Growth Lead.
5. Classifier + NBA choose response.
6. Send onboarding route if intent clear.
7. Attribute completion.

Messenger works best if the audience is Facebook-active.

37.24 Paid intent conversation policy

Paid message conversations should be treated as inbound/warm.

Rules:

reply on same channel first
respect active response window
route to onboarding quickly if intent clear
ask at most one clarifying question if needed
switch channel only if user provides contact or original window expires

Do not over-qualify.

The ad already did some filtering.

37.25 Qualification questions

Keep Meta lead forms short.

Recommended fields:

Business name
Phone or WhatsApp number
City/area
Business type
Do you want a menu link + QR?

Optional:

Instagram handle
Email
Number of outlets
Preferred contact method

Avoid long forms.

Long forms reduce volume.

Too-short forms reduce quality.

The Growth Engine can score after submission.

37.26 Paid lead message templates
Lead Ad follow-up — WhatsApp/email
Hi {{business_name}}, thanks for your interest in MenuList.

You can set up a clean menu link + QR for your customers here:
{{flow_url}}
Click-to-WhatsApp inbound reply
Thanks for messaging MenuList.

You can set up your menu link + QR here:
{{flow_url}}
Instagram DM reply
Thanks for reaching out. MenuList helps restaurants create a clean menu link for Instagram bio, WhatsApp, and QR.

Start here:
{{flow_url}}
Messenger reply
Thanks for your interest in MenuList.

You can set up your menu link + QR here:
{{flow_url}}

Keep paid-intent replies short.

They already clicked an ad.

37.27 Paid intent offer angles

Allowed offer angles:

menu_link_qr
whatsapp_menu_link
instagram_bio_menu
simple_setup
local_restaurant_setup
customer_request, only if demand evidence exists

Recommended mapping:

Lead Ads:
menu_link_qr / simple_setup

Click-to-WhatsApp:
whatsapp_menu_link / simple_setup

Click-to-Instagram:
instagram_bio_menu

Click-to-Messenger:
menu_link_qr / simple_setup

Retargeting:
help_complete_onboarding / reactivation
37.28 Meta conversion feedback

Meta Conversions API is designed to connect advertiser marketing data, including website/app/business messaging events, to Meta; Meta also has a Conversions API for CRM integration guide for sending down-funnel CRM event data back to Meta.
Facebook Developers
+1

For MenuList, the useful feedback events are:

lead_received
qualified_lead

onboarding_completed

This can help measurement and optimization if configured correctly.

37.30 Conversion feedback workflow

5. Conversion feedback event created.
6. If enabled and allowed, server sends event to Meta.
7. Status logged.
8. Failures go to retry/dead-letter.

Do not block MenuList onboarding or internal attribution on Meta feedback success.

Meta feedback is secondary.

response time

scale campaign because cost per lead is low

Good recommendation:

pause campaign because cost per lead is low but only 1% qualified and no completions

37.58 First implementation slice

Build first:

1. Meta Lead Ads webhook ingestion
2. Meta lead form field mapping
3. metaPaidLeads collection
4. paid lead normalization
5. dedupe + suppression check
6. Growth Lead creation/update
7. fast email/WhatsApp follow-up through existing Growth Engine
8. tracked onboarding route
9. paid intent summary
10. dashboard: cost per completed onboarding, qualified rate, completion rate

Second:

Click-to-WhatsApp ingestion + inbound conversation attribution

Third:

Click-to-Instagram/Messenger attribution

Fourth:

Conversion API / CRM feedback to Meta

Do not start with all integrations at once.

37.59 Acceptance criteria

This module is ready when:

1. Meta Lead Ads webhook creates paid lead records.
2. Paid lead fields map correctly to Growth Lead fields.
3. Dedupe and suppression are enforced.
4. Paid leads enter Growth Engine with correct attribution.
5. Paid leads can receive tracked onboarding route.
6. Onboarding completion attributes back to Meta campaign/ad/form.
7. Dashboard shows cost per completed onboarding.
8. Bad paid leads are labeled/rejected.
9. Click-to-message inbound conversations can be attributed to Meta source.
10. Conversion feedback events can be queued, sent, and audited if enabled.
11. Firebase dashboards use summaries, not raw events.
37.60 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Optimizing for cost per lead

Fix:

primary metric = cost per completed onboarding
Failure mode 2 — Paid leads are low quality

Fix:

form quality analysis
required fields
AI quality classifier
reject reasons
campaign pause recommendations
Failure mode 3 — Slow follow-up

Fix:

paid intent priority boost
inbox SLA
auto-send low-risk follow-up
Failure mode 4 — Click-to-message windows expire

Fix:

active window priority
urgent inbox queue
NBA same-channel reply
Failure mode 5 — Attribution lost

Fix:

store campaign/ad/form IDs
route ID required
feedback updates paid attribution
Failure mode 6 — Conversion feedback sends wrong data

Fix:

conversion feedback validator
idempotency
privacy/consent policy
dead-letter queue
admin toggle
Failure mode 7 — Firebase cost spikes

Fix:

compact events
summary docs
TTL raw events
BigQuery analytics
no excessive polling
37.61 Final contract

The Meta Paid Intent Engine must guarantee:

1. Meta leads and click-to-message conversations become structured Growth Leads.
2. Paid leads are deduped, suppressed, and scored before outreach.
3. Paid intent receives faster priority but not safety bypass.
4. Every paid lead is attributed to Meta campaign/ad/form/destination where possible.
5. Every onboarding route is tracked.
6. Success is measured by completed onboarding and cost per completion.
7. Conversion feedback to Meta is optional, controlled, and audited.
8. Bad forms/campaigns can be identified and paused.
9. Click-to-message leads stay inside the Unified Inbox and channel policy model.
10. Firestore stores hot state and summaries; heavy analytics go to BigQuery.
37.62 Final principle

Meta Paid Intent should not be a separate marketing island.

It should become another lead and intent source inside the MenuList Growth Engine.

The correct loop is:

Meta creates paid intent
→ Growth Engine qualifies and routes
→ Existing MenuList onboarding converts
→ Attribution measures cost per completed onboarding
→ Optimizer scales only what produces real completions

The rule:

Paid acquisition is useful only when it produces completed MenuList onboarding at acceptable cost and risk.

Spec 38 — Local Cluster Expansion Engine
38.1 Purpose

The Local Cluster Expansion Engine helps MenuList grow by concentrated local market density instead of scattered individual outreach.

It answers:

Which city / area / category should MenuList attack next?
Where do we already have momentum?
Where is customer demand rising?
Where are leads converting?
Where are channels healthy?
Where is source quality strong?
Where should we stop wasting effort?
Which local cluster should become the next acquisition campaign?

A cluster is:

city + area + category

Examples:

Bangalore / Koramangala / cafes
Bangalore / Indiranagar / bakeries
Bangalore / HSR / cloud kitchens
Mumbai / Bandra / dessert shops
Delhi / Hauz Khas / restaurants

The engine turns growth from:

random lead collection

into:

territory-by-territory distribution expansion
38.2 Strategic reason

MenuList should not grow as a random database of disconnected SMBs.

It should grow by coverage density.

Density matters because it creates:

more visible MenuList surfaces in a local area
more QR/menu-link exposure
more customer demand signals
more owner recognition
more local referrals
better campaign learning
better channel targeting
lower source waste
stronger inevitability

The long-term strategic pattern:

pick a local cluster
→ source businesses
→ onboard enough of them
→ MenuList becomes familiar locally
→ customers and owners see MenuList repeatedly
→ distribution loops strengthen
→ move to adjacent cluster

This is how MenuList becomes default infrastructure, not just another SaaS doing scattered outreach.

38.3 Boundary

This module owns:

cluster definition
market coverage tracking
cluster opportunity scoring
cluster campaign suggestions
source-run planning by cluster
distribution signal aggregation by cluster
channel performance by cluster
coverage dashboard
cluster expansion recommendations
cluster-level experiments

It does not own:

lead sourcing implementation
message sending
MenuList onboarding
business verification
menu creation
pricing
customer-facing surface UX
field sales operations
generic market research product

It informs the Growth Engine where to focus.

The Growth Engine still executes acquisition.

38.4 Core principle

The system should not ask:

Where can we find more leads?

It should ask:

Where can MenuList build local density fastest with acceptable cost and risk?

That means each cluster is judged by:

lead supply
lead quality
customer demand
contactability
channel performance
source cost
onboarding completion
negative/DNC risk
existing MenuList coverage
distribution loop potential
38.5 Cluster definition

A cluster is a market cell.

TypeScript
type ClusterKey = {
  country: string;
  city: string;
  area?: string;
  category: string;
};

Canonical cluster ID:

country_city_area_category

Example:

india_bangalore_koramangala_cafe
india_bangalore_indiranagar_bakery
india_mumbai_bandra_restaurant

Use normalized fields:

normalizedCountry
normalizedCity
normalizedArea
normalizedCategory

Do not let spelling variants create different clusters.

38.6 Cluster category taxonomy

Use controlled categories, not raw source categories.

Recommended initial categories:

restaurant
cafe
bakery
dessert_shop
juice_shop
tea_shop
cloud_kitchen
bar_pub
fast_food
food_truck
sweet_shop
ice_cream_shop
other_food
unknown_food

The Growth Engine can map raw categories to these.

Example:

“Coffee shop” → cafe
“Cake shop” → bakery or dessert_shop
“South Indian Restaurant” → restaurant
“Biryani outlet” → restaurant / cloud_kitchen depending source

Cluster strategy depends on category quality, so normalize early.

Collection:

type MarketCoverageCell = {
  id: string; // normalizedCountry_normalizedCity_normalizedArea_normalizedCategory

  };

      | "unknown"
      | "empty"
      | "mapped"
      | "sourced"
      | "contacting"
      | "early_coverage"
      | "growing_density"
      | "strong_density"
      | "saturated"
      | "paused";
  };

  };

    bestSourceProvider?: string;

    bestOfferAngle?: OfferAngle;

  };

    stageRecommendation:
      | "discover"

      | "run_campaign"
      | "retarget"
      | "increase_density"
      | "partner_push"
      | "hold"
      | "pause"
      | "avoid";

    reason: string[];

  };

  timestamps: {

    lastCampaignAt?: Date;
    lastCompletionAt?: Date;
    updatedAt: Date;
    createdAt: Date;
  };
};
38.9 Coverage density stages

Use explicit cluster stage labels.

unknown:
No reliable data yet.

empty:
No known businesses or no useful lead source.

mapped:
Known business count exists, but no meaningful sourcing/contacting.

sourced:
Leads sourced and deduped.

contacting:
Campaigns/outreach running.

early_coverage:
Some completed onboardings exist.

growing_density:
Repeated completions + local distribution signals.

strong_density:
MenuList has visible local presence and owned distribution loops.

saturated:
Enough coverage or low remaining opportunity.

paused:
Risk, poor quality, or cost makes the cluster unattractive for now.

The goal is to move clusters:

unknown → mapped → sourced → contacting → early_coverage → growing_density → strong_density

Not all clusters should be pursued.

Some should become:

pause / avoid
38.10 Cluster opportunity scoring

The score should answer:

Should MenuList invest acquisition effort in this cluster now?

Formula:

Cluster Opportunity Score =
  Lead Supply Score
+ Lead Quality Score
+ Contactability Score
+ Demand Signal Score
+ Conversion Performance Score
+ Distribution Momentum Score
+ Strategic Density Score
- Cost Penalty
- Risk Penalty

Suggested weights:

Lead supply:                 15
Lead quality:                15
Contactability:              10
Demand signals:              15
Conversion performance:      20
Distribution momentum:       10
Strategic density:           10
Cost penalty:               -15 max
Risk penalty:               -30 max
38.11 Score components
Lead Supply Score

Signals:

known business count
growth leads count
source availability
source freshness
duplicate rate

High if:

many businesses found
low duplicate rate
sources can reliably produce leads

Low if:

few businesses
high duplicates
bad categories
stale/uncertain data
Lead Quality Score

Signals:

A/B lead ratio
fit score distribution
business category match
scale match
non-food contamination

High if:

many A/B single-location food SMBs

Low if:

many chains, wrong verticals, low-fit businesses
Contactability Score

Signals:

phone availability
email availability
WhatsApp likelihood
Instagram presence
valid identity rate
bounce/wrong-number rate

High if:

many contact-ready leads

Low if:

few contacts or high wrong-contact rate
Demand Signal Score

Signals:

customer menu requests
business searches
public hook clicks
unclaimed page demand
customer-request eligible businesses

High if:

customers already look for these businesses/menus
Conversion Performance Score

Signals:

contacted → onboarding started
routed → onboarding completed
cost per completion
completion by channel
completion by source

High if:

cluster already converts
Distribution Momentum Score

Signals:

QR/menu referral leads
menu footer leads
public hook leads
business referrals
partner referrals
repeat demand

High if:

MenuList is starting to spread from usage
Strategic Density Score

Signals:

adjacent to strong cluster
brand visibility potential
category consistency
local cluster usefulness
owner network overlap
partner availability

High if:

winning this cluster helps adjacent clusters
Cost Penalty

Signals:

source cost
AI/enrichment cost
operator cost
paid cost
low conversion cost inefficiency

Penalty if:

cost per completed onboarding is high
Risk Penalty

Signals:

DNC rate
negative rate
wrong-contact rate
bounce rate
complaint rate
channel health issues
low source confidence

Penalty if:

cluster creates channel/brand risk
38.12 Opportunity score interpretation
85–100:
Attack now. Strong cluster.

70–84:
Good candidate. Build or scale campaign.

55–69:
Selective. Source/enrich/test first.

40–54:
Monitor or run small experiment.

<40:
Hold, pause, or avoid.

Risk override:

If DNC/complaint/wrong-contact risk is high, do not scale even if opportunity score is high.
38.13 Cluster recommendations

The engine should output one of these:

TypeScript
type ClusterStageRecommendation =
  | "discover"
  | "source_more"
  | "run_campaign"
  | "retarget"
  | "increase_density"
  | "partner_push"
  | "hold"
  | "pause"
  | "avoid";

Meaning:

discover:
Not enough data. Run lightweight source/demand discovery.

source_more:
Sources look promising; collect more leads.

run_campaign:
Enough lead supply and quality; launch acquisition campaign.

retarget:
There are warm/clicked/started-not-completed leads to recover.

increase_density:
Cluster is working; scale within safety caps.

partner_push:
Use referrals/partners because direct outbound is less efficient.

hold:
Not enough opportunity now.

pause:
Risk or cost is high.

avoid:
Poor fit or bad source quality.

38.18 Local cluster campaign angle

Cluster campaigns can use local language, but only if true.

Banned:

Everyone in your area is joining.

We are the official local partner.

38.27 AI planner guardrails

AI must not recommend scaling if:

DNC rate high
complaint rate high
wrong-contact rate high
channel health warning/restricted
sample size too small
source quality bad
campaign is immature

AI must not recommend:

fake local social proof
cold Instagram/Messenger blasts
uncapped source runs
uncapped campaigns
WhatsApp scale without health/cap review

If uncertain:

recommend experiment or small source run

not full scale.

38.30 Retargeting by cluster

Clusters should surface retargeting pockets:

clicked_not_started in Koramangala cafes
started_not_completed in Indiranagar bakeries
not_now cooldown expired in HSR restaurants
customer_requested but not contacted
public hook clicked but no onboarding

Cluster retargeting is often higher leverage than sourcing more cold leads.

Recommendation example:

Before sourcing more Koramangala cafes, retarget 43 clicked-not-started leads from last campaign.
38.31 Partner/referral by cluster

Some clusters may be better served by partners/referrals.

Signals:

low cold response
high partner/referral presence
local agencies/vendors active
strong existing MenuList business distribution
same-owner multi-branch patterns

Recommendation:

partner_push

Action:

identify existing high-distribution businesses
ask for branches/referrals
create partner outreach list
use referral engine
38.32 Cluster-level distribution flywheel

As cluster density grows:

more MenuList QR/menu surfaces
→ more customer demand signals
→ more owner clicks
→ more referrals
→ more local recognition
→ lower acquisition friction

Cluster engine should track:

outbound-sourced completions
distribution-sourced completions
referral-sourced completions
customer-demand-sourced completions
paid-intent completions

Long-term goal:

distribution-sourced share increases over time

If a cluster always requires cold outbound, it may not be compounding.

38.39 Cluster risk management

Pause or avoid cluster if:

DNC rate high
wrong-contact rate high
bounce rate high
complaint rate high
very low qualified rate
source duplicate rate high
operator backlog too high
channel health weak
completion rate near zero after sufficient sample

Cluster can be paused without pausing entire city/category.

Example:

Pause HSR cloud kitchens
Continue Koramangala cafes

This prevents one bad segment from polluting broader strategy.

channel experiment within cluster

Examples:

Koramangala cafes:
WhatsApp assisted vs email

Indiranagar dessert shops:
instagram_bio_menu vs menu_link_qr

Bangalore bakeries:
Apify vs partner referral source

38.42 Cluster maturity score

Separate from opportunity score.

Opportunity score = should we invest now?
Maturity score = how developed is this cluster?

Maturity score components:

onboarded coverage

distribution-sourced leads
customer demand
referrals
local channel performance stability

Maturity levels:

0: unknown
1: discovered
2: sourced
3: early traction
4: repeatable acquisition
5: compounding distribution

This helps strategic review.

38.49 Acceptance criteria

This module is ready when:

1. Every Growth Lead can map to a cluster.
2. Every onboarding completion can map to a cluster.
3. marketCoverageCells track known/qualified/contacted/completed counts.
4. Cluster opportunity score is calculated.
5. Dashboard ranks clusters by opportunity.
6. AI can recommend source/campaign/retarget/pause actions.
7. Campaign Builder can create a campaign from a cluster.
8. Distribution signals update cluster opportunity.
9. Cluster performance is measured by completed onboarding and risk.
10. Dashboard uses summary docs, not raw lead/message scans.
38.50 First implementation slice

Build first:

1. cluster key generator
2. marketCoverageCells
3. cluster assignment on lead creation/update
4. cluster assignment on onboarding feedback
5. basic cluster daily stats
6. opportunity score v1
7. cluster dashboard table
8. “Create campaign from cluster” action
9. source plan suggestion using Apify
10. cluster safety/risk summary

Do not start with map visualization.

Start with:

ranked table + campaign action

That is enough for decisions.

38.51 Failure modes
Failure mode 1 — Random cluster expansion

Fix:

opportunity score + evidence + cost/risk thresholds
Failure mode 2 — Chasing big markets too early

Fix:

cluster density over broad city coverage
Failure mode 3 — Scaling high-risk clusters

Fix:

risk penalty + safety override + pause recommendation
Failure mode 4 — Coverage estimates are fake precision

Fix:

store confidence and treat estimates directionally
Failure mode 5 — Dashboard scans raw leads

Fix:

marketCoverageCells + clusterDailyStats + BigQuery
Failure mode 6 — Cluster campaign uses fake local proof

Fix:

local copy guardrails
Failure mode 7 — Too many categories fragment learning

Fix:

controlled normalized category taxonomy
38.52 Final contract

The Local Cluster Expansion Engine must guarantee:

1. Every lead and onboarding outcome can be mapped to a local cluster.
2. Every cluster has coverage, performance, risk, and opportunity state.
3. Cluster recommendations are based on completion, cost, risk, and distribution signals.
4. Cluster campaigns can be generated but not launched without dry-run and approval.
5. High-risk clusters are paused or held, not scaled.
6. Local messaging uses true locality only, never fake social proof.
7. Dashboards read summaries, not raw operational collections.
8. The system helps MenuList build density, not random scattered coverage.
38.53 Final principle

MenuList should not expand as a flat list of businesses.

It should expand like infrastructure:

cluster by cluster
category by category
surface by surface
distribution loop by distribution loop

The Local Cluster Expansion Engine makes growth deliberate.

The rule:

Win dense local clusters.
Let density create recognition.
Let recognition create demand.
Let demand create more businesses.
Then expand to adjacent clusters.
